Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.title: DiffGIPC: Differentiable Mixed-Coordinate Contact Dynamics on GPU
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.authors_text: Kemeng Huang, Bowen Ren, Xinyu Lu, Minchen Li, Taku komura
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.summary: DiffGIPC is a GPU-accelerated framework that efficiently optimizes contact-rich dynamics in deformable and rigid bodies, achieving significant speedups in gradient evaluations while ensuring non-penetration.
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.debug_abstract: Contact-rich inverse problems require efficient gradients and reliable enforcement of non-penetration. Existing differentiable methods provide fast simulation and rigid-deformable coupling, but contact treatments based on penalties or velocity-level constraints can permit penetration or positional drift. Incremental Potential Contact (IPC) maintains non-penetration through geometric barriers and {continuous collision detection (CCD)}. However, repeated forward and backward evaluations remain costly in full-space finite-element (FEM) implementations, particularly when nearly rigid components retain many vertex {degrees of freedom (DoFs)}. We present DiffGIPC, a GPU-accelerated differentiable IPC framework for optimizing interacting deformable and nearly rigid bodies. Our affine-body derivatives enable {rest-shape} design, initial-state optimization, and articulated control while retaining only twelve motion DoFs per affine body. These gradients account for how changes in geometry, placement, and actuation affect other objects through collision and friction. We preserve these interactions in one coupled FEM-affine adjoint system per frame, reducing the backward-system size without discarding the dependencies that drive the inverse problem. GPU-optimized backward computation further reduces the cost of repeated gradient evaluations. A reusable PyTorch interface connects supported physical parameters to user-defined parameter maps and losses across design, identification, motion, placement, and articulated control. Experiments demonstrate peak speedups over DiffIPC of approximately 150.0x with full-space FEM and 4133.3x with affine bodies for combined forward simulation and backward differentiation.

Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.title: REVEAL: Reverse Engineering Agentic Latents from Frontier-Model Traces
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.authors_text: Yuetian Du, Meng Wang, Yucheng Wang, Zhangzhe Chen, Wei Wang
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.summary: The REVEAL framework enables the extraction of reusable local controls from frontier-model trajectories, enhancing smaller agents' performance without requiring model retraining.
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.debug_abstract: Frontier LLM agents perform complex interactive tasks, but their inference costs motivate transferring their experience to smaller open-source agents. Distillation and latent communication typically require target-model training or access to source-model internals. We study how textual frontier-model trajectories can provide reusable local controls for a frozen agent. Inspired by protocol reverse engineering, we introduce $\textit{Agentic Latents}$, comprising anchored states and dynamic profiles of feedback--response cycles elicited by replay in the target model. Our training-free framework, $\textbf{REVEAL}$ ($\textbf{REV}$erse $\textbf{E}$ngineering $\textbf{A}$gentic $\textbf{L}$atents), uses these profiles and trajectory outcomes to match and select local events from successful and failed rollouts of the same task and source model. Their response-transition contrasts yield a target-specific steering direction, applied before each response. Within-benchmark evaluations on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and Humanity's Last Exam with tools report higher accuracy than unmodified agents across three targets. Representation analyses and behavioral case studies support reusing frontier-model experience as local activation control.

Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.title: PingpongDuo: Agile Humanoid Table Tennis Doubles with Safe Team Coordination
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.authors_text: Haoran Jiang, Yichao Zhong, Kai Zhang, Cheng Liu, Yixuan Pan
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.summary: PingpongDuo is a hierarchical framework enabling agile humanoid table tennis doubles with safe coordination, improving ball-return success by 13.2% and achieving rapid, precise movements.
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.debug_abstract: Unlike singles, humanoid table tennis doubles requires teammates to strike in strict alternation while sharing a confined workspace. Rapid repositioning can compromise striking accuracy, while uncoordinated teammate movements introduce collision risks. We present PingpongDuo, a hierarchical framework for agile humanoid doubles with safe team coordination. At the team level, a planner jointly selects positioning targets and uses learned risk estimates to filter risky proposals, preferentially preserving the current striker's target. At the individual level, separate footwork and striking skills combine agile movement with precise racket control. The skills are guided by human motion references, including footwork collected from human doubles play, and trained from states produced by one another to support rapid transitions. A racket-arm residual further refines strikes after movement using return feedback from a simulator calibrated with real ball-flight and contact measurements. In simulation, PingpongDuo improves the ball-return success rate by 13.2% over the state-of-the-art baseline, while achieving approximately 2 cm positioning error during clearance. In real-world experiments, a robot completes a 2.15 m clearance-and-recovery cycle in 2.4 s with a peak speed of 2.23 m/s, while two robots sustain more than 10 consecutive strikes in strict alternation.

Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.title: Reflect After Failure: Brain-Inspired Self-Evolving Agents for Embodied Spatial Intelligence
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.authors_text: Xin Li, Xiaohuan Gu, Yifan Wang, Shaobin Ling, Tianli Shi
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.summary: HiMeco, a brain-inspired self-evolving agent, enhances embodied spatial intelligence by diagnosing failures and refining strategies through metacognitive reflection and memory consolidation.
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.debug_abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have made substantial progress in spatial reasoning, and self-evolving agents further extend these capabilities to embodied environments by learning from interactions. However, current self-evolution remains particularly challenging in embodied spatial tasks, complex and multi-step decisions from partial visual evidence making it difficult to determine why an execution fails. The failure may stem from misperception, insufficient exploration, or incorrect planning, yet execution feedback alone rarely reveals which component is responsible. As a result, simply accumulating interaction experience can reinforce ineffective strategies. To address this, we propose HiMeco, a brain-inspired self-evolving agent for embodied spatial intelligence, inspired by metacognitive monitoring and hippocampal memory consolidation. Through Hippocampal-Metacognitive Reflection, HiMeco diagnoses failures in perception-exploration-planning (PEP), then compares execution attempts to derive reusable strategies and guidance for avoiding recurring errors. It also abstracts interaction programs into parameterized skills, using evidence contracts and execution-based validation to determine their retention and reuse. These strategies and skills guide subsequent interactions, with memory updated only between rounds and model parameters kept frozen. HiMeco achieves state-of-the-art performance on ESI-Bench, and it also improves accuracy on EmbSpatial-Bench by 3.94 percentage points without evolution.

Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.title: Atomic-WAM: Execution-Grounded Atomic-Motion Reasoning for World Action Models
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.authors_text: Shijun Shi, Zhe Liu, Zhi Hou, Yinan Chen, Tao Zhang
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.summary: Atomic-WAM integrates task reasoning and action generation through atomic-motion descriptions, enhancing robotic control with execution-grounded learning for improved task success rates.
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.debug_abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) typically adapt video foundation models to robotic control through joint video and action prediction. However, task-level instructions may leave the next physical interaction underspecified, requiring semantic grounding and state-dependent motion selection. To this end, we introduce Atomic-WAM, an understand-then-execute framework that connects task reasoning to action generation through atomic-motion descriptions. Specifically, a vision-language reasoner describes the next local motion from the task instruction and visual context, guiding a WAM to predict future video and an action chunk. Furthermore, an automatic annotation pipeline curates temporally aligned, contact-enriched supervision from multi-view DROID demonstrations. To make atomic-motion predictions executable by the WAM, we post-train the reasoner with Execution-Grounded GRPO (EG-GRPO). With the WAM fixed, EG-GRPO adapts the reasoner through rewards for motion appropriateness and execution success. Finally, Atomic-WAM achieves 39.6% task success under default instructions and 31.6% under vague instructions in a real-to-sim evaluation on RoboLab. Project page: https://ssj9596.github.io/Atomic-WAM-project

Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.title: LAGO: Language Agents with Reusable Growing Options
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.authors_text: Yuran Wu, Mengkang Hu, Qionglin Qiu, Fanqing Meng, Qiguang Chen
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.summary: LAGO introduces reusable language agents as temporally extended options to enhance task decomposition and execution, achieving improved performance on long-horizon tasks without model weight updates.
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.debug_abstract: Long-horizon tasks expose a weakness of monolithic tool-use loops: one agent must decompose, execute, and verify a task within a single trajectory. We introduce LAGO, which treats specialized language agents as reusable temporally extended options. A meta-agent retrieves options from a persistent library or spawns new ones, dispatches sub-tasks, verifies results, and admits successful novel options. The library grows across tasks without updating model weights. On 500 SWE-bench Verified tasks, frozen Qwen3.5-35B-A3B in both roles resolves 58.6% under single-attempt evaluation with the official Docker evaluator. On a fixed 150-task subset, we re-run mini-SWE-agent, Terminus 2, and LAGO with the same policy, temperature, task IDs, and evaluator; their resolve rates are 49.3%, 57.3%, and 60.3%, respectively. Cross-model experiments provide evidence consistent with a role for decomposition quality. A 50-task component ablation finds four fewer resolved tasks without decomposition, two fewer with shuffled reused content, and six fewer without the library. These results support reusable agent-options as a practical abstraction for task streams, while leaving component-level causality task- and model-dependent.

Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.title: Coordi-pi: Coordination-Aware Dual-Hand Action Representation for Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.authors_text: Yiming Meng, Yanming Shao, Weijie Shen, Kunyang Lin, Jiayu Sun
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.summary: Coordi-$\pi$ introduces a structured action representation for bimanual manipulation, enhancing performance significantly by explicitly encoding hand identity and temporal synchronization.
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.debug_abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have shown strong potential for general-purpose robotic manipulation, but extending them to bimanual dexterous manipulation introduces a high-dimensional and structured action space. Existing bimanual VLA policies commonly concatenate right- and left-side arm--hand actions at each control timestep, leaving cross-hand interactions implicit within a single action vector. We introduce Coordi-$π$, a structured action representation for bimanual dexterous manipulation. Coordi-$π$ represents the right- and left-side arm--hand actions as individual action tokens and organizes them into an interleaved sequence, explicitly exposing the two sides within the action sequence. To explicitly encode hand identity and temporal synchronization in this interleaved representation, a learnable hand-identity embedding distinguishes the two sides, while sequence--control-timestep factorized rotary positional encoding (RoPE) separates sequence position from control timestep, allowing actions at the same control timestep to share a temporal coordinate while retaining distinct sequence positions. Across all five bimanual dexterous manipulation tasks in DexJoCo, Coordi-$π$ achieves state-of-the-art performance under both \textit{rand-obj} and \textit{rand-full}, improving the average success rate over $π_{0.5}$ from 31.9\% to 51.3\% and from 18.3\% to 32.3\%, respectively. Coordi-$π$ also consistently outperforms $π_{0.5}$ across four real-world bimanual dexterous manipulation tasks.

Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.title: OmniHOI: Dexterous Hand-Object Interaction from Monocular Human Video
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.authors_text: Ting Mao, Yanming Shao, Ziheng Wang, Haoyu Liu, Yiqun Wang
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.summary: OmniHOI is a novel pipeline that converts monocular videos of hand-object interactions into accurate trajectories for dexterous robots, achieving significantly improved success rates over prior methods.
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.debug_abstract: Monocular videos of human manipulation provide abundant dexterous demonstrations, yet reconstructing hand-object interaction from a single view and transferring it to robot hands remain difficult, limiting their direct use for robot execution. Prior methods either require task-specific RL training, limiting scalability, or assume clean motion-capture trajectories and thus cannot operate directly on video. We present OmniHOI, a pipeline that turns an RGB video of hand-object interaction into an interaction-faithful trajectory on dexterous hands. The key idea is to enforce physical consistency using the evidence available at each stage: image evidence during reconstruction, contact geometry during retargeting, and dynamics during physics-in-the-loop refinement. Each stage optimizes the corresponding representation directly, correcting errors before they propagate downstream or must be absorbed by a learned policy. Across 150 motion-capture trajectories transferred to each of five dexterous hands with 6 to 22 DoF, we achieve 39-89% success, compared with at most 31% for prior transfer methods. On 60 monocular video clips, we achieve 53% success, compared with 28% for the best prior video-to-robot pipeline. Its trajectories also execute on a real bimanual robot across diverse tasks.

Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.title: VGGT-Diff: Visual Geometry Meets Diffusion for Sparse-View Novel View Synthesis
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.authors_text: Kangjie Chen, Xiangyu Li, Dongbin Zhang, Chaoda Zheng, Shijia Chen
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.summary: VGGT-Diff integrates geometry-based routing with a diffusion model for enhanced novel view synthesis from sparse views, achieving state-of-the-art performance through robust conditioning and consistency techniques.
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.debug_abstract: We present VGGT-Diff, a geometry-routed multi-view diffusion model for sparse-view novel view synthesis. Existing novel view synthesis (NVS) methods face a fundamental trade-off: reconstruction-based approaches preserve observed geometry but struggle to synthesize unseen regions, while diffusion-based methods provide strong generative priors yet rely on implicit source-to-query correspondence. VGGT-Diff bridges these regimes by routing visual geometry latents from VGGT-Ω into a pretrained video diffusion model. Each visual token is associated with a 3D point and confidence, then transformed into query-aligned latent conditions through a confidence-aware Visual Geometry Router (VGR) that preserves front and back surface evidence. These conditions guide joint target-view denoising, while Point-Track Residual Consistency (PTRC) regularizes predicted-clean residuals along reliable 3D tracks, improving multi-view stability. We further introduce robust geometry conditioning, combining training-time regularization with inference-time guidance for improved robustness. Experiments show competitive or state-of-the-art performance across interpolation and extrapolation under different viewpoint difficulties. Our code is available at https://github.com/chenkangjie1123/VGGT-Diff.

Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.title: GAE: Learning a Geometry-Native Latent Space for 3D-Consistent World Generation
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.authors_text: Jiahao Lu, Minghao Yin, Wenbo Hu, Hengyu Liu, Wang Zhao
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.summary: The GAE introduces a geometry-native latent space enhancing 3D-consistent world generation, improving visual quality and coherence by reparameterizing features for diverse tasks.
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.debug_abstract: We present a compact geometry-native latent space as a shared foundation for perception and generation. Visual generators can produce photorealistic frames without preserving a consistent 3D scene. We argue that this is not only a modeling problem but also a representation problem: generators typically evolve appearance-centric latents, while perception models recover geometry in a semantically rich space that encodes cross-view structure. Rather than adding geometry as another output, we reparameterize a geometry foundation model's features into a compact latent space for generation. We realize this shift with the geometry-native autoencoder (GAE), whose latent is jointly decodable to appearance, depth, cameras, and point maps. With this state, a standard conditional flow supports diverse generation tasks. In controlled comparisons that hold the generator and training protocol fixed, replacing the latent with GAE improves both visual quality and independently measured 3D coherence: FVD falls by $12.7\%$ and $23.1\%$ on RealEstate10K and DL3DV, and camera-trajectory error is halved on RealEstate10K. Together, these results show that the latent space is central to geometry-consistent generation and can serve as a shared interface between perception and generation.

Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.title: Dual-Evolving Reinforcement Learning for Automated Reward Design
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.authors_text: Sitao Cheng, Tianle Li, Xuhan Huang, Xunjian Yin, Difan Zou
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.summary: Dual-Evolving Reinforcement Learning (DERL) enhances automated reward design by using a dual-training framework that adapts reward structures based on inner policy performance feedback.
Language and Vision (LaVi) Lab.debug_abstract: Crafting effective reward signals remains a central challenge in reinforcement learning (RL) for complex reasoning. Existing methods for automated reward optimization search with a fixed proposer which never learns from its costly trials. We present Dual-Evolving Reinforcement Learning (DERL), a dual-training framework for autonomous discovery of reward structures. An outer-loop proposer composes a reward from task primitives, and an inner policy trains with this reward. The proposer itself learns by policy gradient from the validation performance of the inner policy. Thus, DERL utilizes past-trial feedback to shape its reward-proposal distribution, an empirical meta-gradient of task success. We validate DERL on embodied (ALFWorld), scientific (ScienceWorld), and mathematical (GSM8K, MATH) reasoning. On multi-turn agent benchmarks, DERL outperforms strong baselines, significantly on out-of-distribution tasks. In mathematics, DERL improves on the outcome reward where directly added primitives hurt. Further analyses under matched compute show that our proposer effectively captures the meta-gradient to discover useful reward signals.

机器人与自动化研究中心.title: Towards Agentic Robots: Model, Data, Environment, and Harness
机器人与自动化研究中心.authors_text: Chonghan Qin, Dongming Wu, Kaituo Feng, Jiaxu Wang, Xinlei Yu
机器人与自动化研究中心.summary: This paper outlines the evolving concept of agentic robots, categorizing research into four domains while addressing challenges and future directions for enhancing robotic intelligence and adaptability.
机器人与自动化研究中心.debug_abstract: Foundation models are driving a paradigm shift in robotic intelligence, moving beyond low-level action prediction to goal-directed orchestration of data collection, model training, task planning, and real-world execution. We characterize this emerging paradigm as an agentic robots, in which agents reason over human instructions, interact with robotic environments, rectify execution errors autonomously, and dynamically adjust operational strategies. Although this field develops fast, current studies are not well connected. Researchers have no consistent view of how to combine different agentic functions into a complete robot system. This paper provides a unified overview of existing research on agentic robots. We first trace the development from robot policies to agentic systems, covering vision-language-action models, world models, and world-action models. We then clarify the definition and scope of agentic robots and organize existing research into seventeen categories across four functional domains: Model, Data, Environment, and Harness. Across these domains, we examine how agents shape model learning and robot decisions, collect and curate robot data, construct worlds, tasks, and tests for learning and evaluation, and organize capabilities for robot use. Finally, we discuss open challenges and outline directions for future research. Looking forward, we hope this work contributes to a clearer understanding of agentic robots and supports new approaches to making them more capable, reliable, and adaptive.

机器人与自动化研究中心.title: Designing Textual Interfaces To Enhance Llm Reasoning On Audio-Visual Question Answering
机器人与自动化研究中心.authors_text: Yi Wang, Tianzi Wang, Tong Lei, Dahan Wang, Peter Bell
机器人与自动化研究中心.summary: This paper explores how different textual interface designs impact prompt optimization for audio-visual question answering in multimodal reasoning systems, revealing trade-offs in interpretability and optimization difficulty.
机器人与自动化研究中心.debug_abstract: Automatic prompt optimization (APO) has shown strong effectiveness for text-based LLMs and LLM systems, but its application to audio-visual understanding systems requires suitable textual interfaces through which multimodal reasoning can be exposed to text-based optimizers. We investigate how the design of textual interfaces affects prompt optimization for multimodal reasoning, on the audio-visual question answering task. We compare three interface designs, including a direct inference system consisting of a single omni-modal large language model (OmniLLM), a captioner-reasoner system, and an agentic architecture in which a primary agent orchestrates subagent OmniLLMs. Experiments with Qwen3-Omni and Gemini show that direct prompt optimization provides model-dependent gains; the captioner-reasoner system and the agentic system expose more interpretable optimization interfaces but are harder to optimize, where error analysis of cases affected by optimization is conducted. Our study highlights textual interface design as an important factor in making prompt optimization effective for omni-modal reasoning systems. Our implementation details are specified in GitHub repo.

机器人与自动化研究中心.title: EvoWeave: Composing Reusable Agent Experience through Operation Level Graphs
机器人与自动化研究中心.authors_text: Guanhua Zhu, Bo Shen, Lei Zhang, Fadi Deek, Zhi Wei
机器人与自动化研究中心.summary: EvoWeave is a framework that enhances interactive agents' task performance by efficiently composing reusable operations through a structured experience memory and dependency graph.
机器人与自动化研究中心.debug_abstract: Different tasks often require interactive agents to perform similar operations at intermediate steps. Retrieving an entire past workflow can introduce irrelevant steps, whereas retrieving isolated operations can discard the dependencies needed to reuse them. We introduce EvoWeave, a framework for experience memory that represents abstract states as nodes and reusable operations as directed edges with input and output contracts, provenance, and capability references. A planner decomposes the current task into a dependency graph; operation retrieval and bounded directed search then assemble relevant experience fragments. An execution agent can inspect these fragments and their referenced capabilities, while reflection separates concrete execution evidence from reusable abstractions. We study the framework across four benchmarks, five evaluation settings, and three language model backbones. Across backbones, AppWorld Normal and Challenge task goal completion average 51.91 and 27.99, respectively, exceeding the baseline without memory by 6.99 and 4.99 percentage points. An AppWorld ablation associates directed connections with an additional improvement of 2.08 points over independent operation cards. The results motivate composition of reusable operations while exposing tradeoffs in retrieval overhead and conditions for valid reuse.

机器人与自动化研究中心.title: REVEAL: Reverse Engineering Agentic Latents from Frontier-Model Traces
机器人与自动化研究中心.authors_text: Yuetian Du, Meng Wang, Yucheng Wang, Zhangzhe Chen, Wei Wang
机器人与自动化研究中心.summary: The REVEAL framework enables the extraction of reusable local controls from frontier-model trajectories, enhancing smaller agents' performance without requiring model retraining.
机器人与自动化研究中心.debug_abstract: Frontier LLM agents perform complex interactive tasks, but their inference costs motivate transferring their experience to smaller open-source agents. Distillation and latent communication typically require target-model training or access to source-model internals. We study how textual frontier-model trajectories can provide reusable local controls for a frozen agent. Inspired by protocol reverse engineering, we introduce $\textit{Agentic Latents}$, comprising anchored states and dynamic profiles of feedback--response cycles elicited by replay in the target model. Our training-free framework, $\textbf{REVEAL}$ ($\textbf{REV}$erse $\textbf{E}$ngineering $\textbf{A}$gentic $\textbf{L}$atents), uses these profiles and trajectory outcomes to match and select local events from successful and failed rollouts of the same task and source model. Their response-transition contrasts yield a target-specific steering direction, applied before each response. Within-benchmark evaluations on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and Humanity's Last Exam with tools report higher accuracy than unmodified agents across three targets. Representation analyses and behavioral case studies support reusing frontier-model experience as local activation control.

Multimedia Lab (MMLab).title: VGGT-Diff: Visual Geometry Meets Diffusion for Sparse-View Novel View Synthesis
Multimedia Lab (MMLab).authors_text: Kangjie Chen, Xiangyu Li, Dongbin Zhang, Chaoda Zheng, Shijia Chen
Multimedia Lab (MMLab).summary: VGGT-Diff integrates geometry-based routing with a diffusion model for enhanced novel view synthesis from sparse views, achieving state-of-the-art performance through robust conditioning and consistency techniques.
Multimedia Lab (MMLab).debug_abstract: We present VGGT-Diff, a geometry-routed multi-view diffusion model for sparse-view novel view synthesis. Existing novel view synthesis (NVS) methods face a fundamental trade-off: reconstruction-based approaches preserve observed geometry but struggle to synthesize unseen regions, while diffusion-based methods provide strong generative priors yet rely on implicit source-to-query correspondence. VGGT-Diff bridges these regimes by routing visual geometry latents from VGGT-Ω into a pretrained video diffusion model. Each visual token is associated with a 3D point and confidence, then transformed into query-aligned latent conditions through a confidence-aware Visual Geometry Router (VGR) that preserves front and back surface evidence. These conditions guide joint target-view denoising, while Point-Track Residual Consistency (PTRC) regularizes predicted-clean residuals along reliable 3D tracks, improving multi-view stability. We further introduce robust geometry conditioning, combining training-time regularization with inference-time guidance for improved robustness. Experiments show competitive or state-of-the-art performance across interpolation and extrapolation under different viewpoint difficulties. Our code is available at https://github.com/chenkangjie1123/VGGT-Diff.

Multimedia Lab (MMLab).title: Dual-Evolving Reinforcement Learning for Automated Reward Design
Multimedia Lab (MMLab).authors_text: Sitao Cheng, Tianle Li, Xuhan Huang, Xunjian Yin, Difan Zou
Multimedia Lab (MMLab).summary: Dual-Evolving Reinforcement Learning (DERL) enhances automated reward design by using a dual-training framework that adapts reward structures based on inner policy performance feedback.
Multimedia Lab (MMLab).debug_abstract: Crafting effective reward signals remains a central challenge in reinforcement learning (RL) for complex reasoning. Existing methods for automated reward optimization search with a fixed proposer which never learns from its costly trials. We present Dual-Evolving Reinforcement Learning (DERL), a dual-training framework for autonomous discovery of reward structures. An outer-loop proposer composes a reward from task primitives, and an inner policy trains with this reward. The proposer itself learns by policy gradient from the validation performance of the inner policy. Thus, DERL utilizes past-trial feedback to shape its reward-proposal distribution, an empirical meta-gradient of task success. We validate DERL on embodied (ALFWorld), scientific (ScienceWorld), and mathematical (GSM8K, MATH) reasoning. On multi-turn agent benchmarks, DERL outperforms strong baselines, significantly on out-of-distribution tasks. In mathematics, DERL improves on the outcome reward where directly added primitives hurt. Further analyses under matched compute show that our proposer effectively captures the meta-gradient to discover useful reward signals.

Berkeley Artificial Intelligence Researc.title: NePPO: Near-Potential Policy Optimization for General-Sum Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
Berkeley Artificial Intelligence Researc.authors_text: Addison Kalanther, Sanika Bharvirkar, Shankar Sastry, Chinmay Maheshwari
Berkeley Artificial Intelligence Researc.summary: NePPO introduces a novel MARL framework that optimizes a potential function to approximate Nash equilibria in general-sum games, outperforming existing algorithms like IPPO and MAPPO.
Berkeley Artificial Intelligence Researc.debug_abstract: Multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) is increasingly used to design learning-enabled agents that interact in shared environments. However, training MARL algorithms in general-sum games remains challenging: learning dynamics can become unstable, and convergence guarantees typically hold only in restricted settings such as two-player zero-sum or fully cooperative games. Moreover, when agents have heterogeneous and potentially conflicting preferences, it is unclear what system-level objective should guide learning. In this paper, we propose a new MARL pipeline called Near-Potential Policy Optimization (NePPO) for computing approximate Nash equilibria in mixed cooperative--competitive environments. The core idea is to learn a player-independent potential function such that the Nash equilibrium of a cooperative game with this potential as the common utility approximates a Nash equilibrium of the original game. To this end, we introduce a novel MARL objective such that minimizing this objective yields the best possible potential function candidate and consequently an approximate Nash equilibrium of the original game. We develop an algorithmic pipeline that minimizes this objective using zeroth-order gradient descent and returns an approximate Nash equilibrium policy. We empirically show the superior performance of this approach compared to popular baselines such as IPPO and MAPPO.

武汉大学.title: EvoSpatial: Experience-Driven Skill and Tool Evolution for Spatial Reasoning Agents
武汉大学.authors_text: Bin Yu, Shijie Lian, Zhaolong Shen, Xiaopeng Lin, Yao Zhang
武汉大学.summary: EvoSpatial is a framework that enhances spatial reasoning agents by evolving skills and tools through execution feedback, improving performance across multiple benchmarks without requiring ground-truth data.
武汉大学.debug_abstract: Spatial reasoning agents can inspect tool outputs and repair errors, but reusing these lessons requires preserving both the computation and the conditions that make it valid. We introduce EvoSpatial, a framework that learns from execution experience by updating a library of linked skills and tools. Skills describe procedures, geometric assumptions, and verification steps; tools implement the operations those procedures require. When solving a task, the agent retrieves relevant skills and synthesizes reusable computational functions if existing tools are insufficient. After each task, execution feedback and evidence checks guide skill revision and tool consolidation, without ground-truth answers or benchmark scores. Across 20 benchmarks, EvoSpatial averages 63.9, 4.0 percentage points above the average reported by SpatialClaw. The evolved library also improves held-out and cross-benchmark performance when updates are disabled, and trajectories generated with evolved skills improve supervised fine-tuning, even without external skills at evaluation. Keeping checked procedures on record, together with the tools that support them, lets an agent carry spatial reasoning experience from one task to the next.

武汉大学.title: Masked Diffusion Vision-Language Models for Temporal Action Localization
武汉大学.authors_text: Fengshun Wang, Zhengbo Zhang, Zhigang Tu
武汉大学.summary: This paper presents a masked diffusion vision-language model for temporal action localization, enhancing semantic reasoning and boundary accuracy through innovative training objectives and denoising techniques.
武汉大学.debug_abstract: Temporal action localization (TAL) requires recognizing the target event and localizing its start and end times precisely in untrimmed videos. Recent vision-language formulations improve semantic reasoning and support language-conditioned outputs, but their autoregressive decoders still generate tokens from left to right, preventing later semantic evidence from revising earlier timestamp predictions. We adapt masked diffusion vision-language models (MDVLMs) to TAL so that semantic tokens and boundary tokens remain editable throughout iterative denoising with bidirectional attention, allowing temporal boundaries and semantic content to be refined jointly. Direct adaptation, however, creates two TAL-specific mismatches: standard masked diffusion training corrupts all positions uniformly at random, but the time tokens are more reliable when enough semantic context is available; and token-level cross-entropy does not reflect temporal IoU. To address these mismatches, we introduce a Planned Training Objective that uses boundary-aware masking and step-weighted reconstruction to rehearse the late recovery of time tokens, together with a Step-Level IoU Reward that provides overlap-aware supervision during denoising. A standard sequence-level cross-entropy term provides the base reconstruction signal. Experiments on ActivityNet-RTL, ActivityNet-1.3, and THUMOS-14 show that MDVLM-TAL improves both temporal reasoning and boundary localization over autoregressive vision-language baselines, with especially strong gains under stricter temporal IoU criteria. The source code is available at https://github.com/ycwfs/MDVLM-TAL .

武汉大学.title: Global Cross-Modal Geo-Localization: A Million-Scale Dataset and a Physical Consistency Learning Framework
武汉大学.authors_text: Yutong Hu, Jinhui Chen, Chaoqiang Xu, Yuan Kou, Sili Zhou
武汉大学.summary: The paper presents CORE, a million-scale dataset for cross-modal geo-localization, and introduces PLANET, a novel framework that enhances accuracy by integrating physical consistency in geo-tagged imagery.
武汉大学.debug_abstract: Cross-modal Geo-localization (CMGL) matches ground-level text descriptions with geo-tagged aerial imagery, which is crucial for pedestrian navigation and emergency response. However, existing studies are constrained by narrow geographic coverage and simplistic scene diversity, failing to reflect the immense spatial heterogeneity of global architectural styles and topographic features. To bridge this gap and facilitate universal positioning, we introduce CORE, the first million-scale dataset dedicated to global CMGL. CORE comprises 1,034,786 cross-view images sampled from 225 distinct geographic regions across six continents, offering an unprecedented variety of perspectives in varying environmental conditions and urban layouts. We leverage the zero-shot reasoning of Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) to synthesize high-quality scene descriptions rich in discriminative cues. Furthermore, we propose a physical-law-aware network (PLANET) for cross-modal geo-localization. PLANET introduces a novel contrastive learning paradigm to guide textual representations in capturing the intrinsic physical signatures of satellite imagery. Extensive experiments across varied geographic regions demonstrate that PLANET significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods, establishing a new benchmark for robust, global-scale geo-localization. The dataset and source code will be released at https://github.com/YtH0823/CORE.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: Graph-Reweighted Behavior Cloning with Human Interventions for Precise Robotic Manipulation
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Xiaoman Li, Zhiqiang Yang, Jiayu Hu, Jipeng Kong, Yang Zhang
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: The paper introduces Graph-Reweighted Behavior Cloning (GR-BC), an offline framework that enhances robotic manipulation by optimizing action selection through a task-conditioned goal-reachability graph, improving success rates without requiring complex models.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: Long-horizon precise manipulation produces mixed-quality data for post-training vision-language-action (VLA) models: even successful demonstrations and intervention-assisted rollouts may contain detours, hesitations, failed attempts, and imperfect recoveries. The key challenge is to identify which action chunks actually advance the task, rather than uniformly cloning or discarding imperfect trajectories. We propose Graph-Reweighted Behavior Cloning (GR-BC), an offline iterative post-training framework that builds a task-conditioned goal-reachability graph over demonstrations and iteratively collected rollouts, including both successful and failed episodes with human interventions. Reverse graph search computes minimal remaining steps to task success within the dataset support, and each action chunk is weighted by how much its execution reduces this potential. This consequence-based weighting reuses recoverable segments from failed trajectories, leverages interventions as recovery paths, and down-weights locally regressive chunks even inside successful trajectories. New rollouts are incorporated by appending them to the graph and rerunning search, without training a reward model, action-conditioned critic, or progress predictor. Across four precise manipulation tasks and three VLA backbones, GR-BC improves single-round supervised fine-tuning and reaches 91% success after a few offline iterations, without trajectory comparisons or progress labels. More details and videos are available at: https://gr-bc.github.io

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: Towards Agentic Robots: Model, Data, Environment, and Harness
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Chonghan Qin, Dongming Wu, Kaituo Feng, Jiaxu Wang, Xinlei Yu
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: This paper outlines the evolving concept of agentic robots, categorizing research into four domains while addressing challenges and future directions for enhancing robotic intelligence and adaptability.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: Foundation models are driving a paradigm shift in robotic intelligence, moving beyond low-level action prediction to goal-directed orchestration of data collection, model training, task planning, and real-world execution. We characterize this emerging paradigm as an agentic robots, in which agents reason over human instructions, interact with robotic environments, rectify execution errors autonomously, and dynamically adjust operational strategies. Although this field develops fast, current studies are not well connected. Researchers have no consistent view of how to combine different agentic functions into a complete robot system. This paper provides a unified overview of existing research on agentic robots. We first trace the development from robot policies to agentic systems, covering vision-language-action models, world models, and world-action models. We then clarify the definition and scope of agentic robots and organize existing research into seventeen categories across four functional domains: Model, Data, Environment, and Harness. Across these domains, we examine how agents shape model learning and robot decisions, collect and curate robot data, construct worlds, tasks, and tests for learning and evaluation, and organize capabilities for robot use. Finally, we discuss open challenges and outline directions for future research. Looking forward, we hope this work contributes to a clearer understanding of agentic robots and supports new approaches to making them more capable, reliable, and adaptive.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: TacClaw-Infinity: A Large-Scale Vision-Tactile-Language-Action Dataset for Dexterous Manipulation
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Fucai Zhu, Xidong Zhang, Yichi Zhang, Yipan Wang, Fubo Wang
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: TacClaw-Infinity is a comprehensive VTLA dataset for dexterous manipulation, featuring over 10,000 hours of diverse, high-quality, structured tactile and visual data from various environments.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: Large-scale robot learning increasingly relies on diverse human demonstrations, yet tactile manipulation data remain difficult to scale, and existing multimodal datasets often lack consistent quality control and structured supervision. We present TacClaw-Infinity, a large-scale structured Vision-Tactile-Language-Action (VTLA) dataset for contact-rich manipulation, collected with TacClaw, a tactile-enabled UMI-style handheld interface that records synchronized visual observations, fingertip tactile signals, and end-effector trajectories without requiring a target robot during data collection. TacClaw-Infinity is built through a distributed worldwide collection across homes, laboratories, industrial workplaces, retail stores, and outdoor environments including tasks contributed by academic and industrial collaborators. Together, these efforts yield over 10,000 hours, 1 million episodes, and 1 billion frames spanning more than 1,000 task types. We develop a scalable pipeline for trajectory reconstruction, multimodal quality control, embodiment-aware filtering, and structured annotation, covering contact-centric segmentation, subtask description, and spatial grounding. We validate TacClaw-Infinity at both the data and model levels: At the data level, we assess the collection interface, the action-space compatibility of the curated demonstrations, and the structured annotations, while for the model level, we demonstrate cross-embodiment transfer across three heterogeneous robots without robot-specific demonstrations.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Model Decision-Making for Autonomous Driving Guided by Chinese Philosophical Wisdom
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Xiaojun Bi, Xiaoyuan Ma, Yiwen Sun, Tianren Huang, Chaoran Liu
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: The CPW-Drive framework integrates Chinese philosophical wisdom into autonomous driving decision-making, enhancing safety and efficiency through a retrieval-augmented generation approach, outperforming traditional methods.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: Autonomous driving decision systems must balance safety, efficiency, and social norms in complex traffic interactions. Philosophical and ethical considerations have received limited attention in existing autonomous driving decision-making approaches based on numerical optimization, sequence prediction, and large language models (LLMs). We propose Chinese Philosophical Wisdom-Guided Driving (CPW-Drive), a closed-loop retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) framework that incorporates value guidance derived from Chinese philosophy into autonomous driving decision-making. Using Chinese Confucian thought as its knowledge source, CPW-Drive consolidates LLM-extracted keywords from relevant classical texts into driving-relevant value principles through manual screening and validation. It then contextualizes these principles through scenario-specific cases to form retrievable and reusable value guidance. We further propose Physics-aware Spatial Similarity Retrieval (PSSR), which compares vehicle layouts and velocity-extrapolated states to retrieve physically relevant historical cases. On Highway-env's multilane highway-driving task, CPW-Drive achieves success rates of 93.0%, 86.0%, and 72.0% across three traffic configurations. These results outperform the strongest baseline by 8.0, 22.5, and 25.0 percentage points, respectively. Across all configurations, CPW-Drive achieves the highest collision-free step count and maintains a low lane-change frequency. The results suggest that structured value guidance can improve simulated closed-loop safety and stability while introducing efficiency and latency trade-offs.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: Why Do VLMs Fail at Remote Physiological Measurement? Rethinking with Physiological Grounding and Numerical Alignment
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Xiao Yang, Zekun Zhang, Yuxuan Fan, Duoxun Tang, Ziyang Liu
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: The paper introduces VITAL, a framework enhancing Vision-Language Models for remote physiological measurement by aligning visual and physiological data while improving numerical accuracy.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: Video-based remote physiological measurement (RPM) has broad applications, while Vision-Language Models (VLMs) provide a promising opportunity to enable end-to-end physiological monitoring for future human-aware intelligent systems. However, existing RPM methods rely on task-specific models and cannot be seamlessly integrated with the multimodal understanding and interaction capabilities of VLMs. We revisit RPM with VLMs and provide empirical evidence for two major bottlenecks: generic visual semantic representations fail to preserve fine-grained physiological cues; while discrete token prediction in autoregressive generation is inherently misaligned with continuous numerical measurement. To address these challenges, we propose VITAL (Visual-physiological Token Alignment for Language Models), a visual-physiological token alignment framework for RPM and preserving general vision tasks. VITAL retains the original visual pathway for semantic understanding and introduces an independent physiological pathway to jointly model semantic and physiological information. Moreover, we propose a structured numerical alignment approach to improve the reliability of generative heart rate estimation by enhancing numerical relationship modeling. Extensive experiments show that VITAL improves cross-domain estimation performance on multiple rPPG datasets while preserving the general visual understanding capability of VLMs, demonstrating its effectiveness as a unified visual-physiological model. Code will be released.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: SEDM: Selective Self-Evolving Distributed Memory for Agents
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Yichen Liu, Anna Min, Yinzhi Wang, Yuhang Yao, Yichen Han
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: SEDM introduces a selective memory framework for agents that optimizes memory sharing and usage, significantly enhancing task success while reducing processing costs.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: Agents in a society can reuse each other's experience, but indiscriminate memory use increases processing cost and can reduce task success. We present SEDM (Selective Self-Evolving Distributed Memory), a framework that selects both what agents share and when recipients use it. On the sender side, SEDM admits memories through paired execution tests, ranks them by relevance and measured utility, and abstracts them for cross-domain reuse. On the recipient side, Calibrated Memory Gating (CMG) predicts success with and without memory in a single forward pass, learning from paired outcomes including ties. It injects memory only when the calibrated success gain outweighs a context-cost penalty. SEDM exceeds the strongest evaluated baseline on LoCoMo open-domain questions by 15.1 F1 points and outperforms G-Memory on FEVER and HotpotQA with 16-32% fewer prompt tokens. In a controlled HotpotQA study, CMG achieves success comparable to always using memory with 18% fewer agent input tokens. Within the full SEDM pipeline on LoCoMo, CMG outperforms both always-use and no-memory policies for two SEDM memories while using 19-31% fewer input tokens than always-use. These results show that selective use can recover value from shared memories that hurt performance when injected indiscriminately.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: PhySGA: A Physics-Space Grounded Agentic Framework for Generalizable and Interactive 3D Composition
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Weichen Lyu, Chong Xia, Mingyu Dong, Long Xu, Shengjun Zhang
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: PhySGA introduces a novel framework for interactive 3D object composition, leveraging agent exploration and physical simulation to enhance precision and adaptability in complex tasks.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: 3D object composition is pivotal to digital content creation and robot simulation, while also serving as a critical testbed for physical intelligence in foundation models. Previous methods either leverage large language models to directly predict object coordinates, or utilize generative diffusion priors to synthesize composite images for visual alignment, both of which rely on static priors in digital spaces. However, these methods consistently struggle with complex compositions such as precise hanging, gravity-driven settling and hidden containment, as these tasks require interactive construction processes involving global planning, fine-grained alignment, and physical simulation. To address these challenges, we propose PhySGA, a Physics-Space Grounded Agentic Framework for 3D composition via agent exploration and physical simulation, enabling the universal interactive assembly of rigid, articulated, and deformable objects. Directly applying vanilla LLMs or VLMs to this task proves insufficient, as current models inherently lack grounded physical understanding and interactive construction experience. To overcome this limitation, we design a collaborative feedforward-feedback architecture: an Assembly Agent focuses on geometric and kinematic reasoning for global step planning and coarse adjustment, while a Critic Agent reasons over contact dynamics for simulator state diagnosis and fine-grained closed-loop correction. Furthermore, Action Routers map semantic planning and analysis onto executable physical primitives within the simulator, while a task-specific Self-Evolving Skill Library distills historical trial-and-error feedback into reusable experiences, boosting success rates and minimizing exploration attempts. Extensive experiments within Isaac Sim demonstrate that PhySGA significantly surpasses existing methods in relation fidelity, physical plausibility, and visual quality.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: Hindsight-Privileged RLVR: Single-Rollout Token Credit Without Group Sampling
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Wei Chen, Yubing Wu, Zhou Xu, Haoyue Zhang, Delu Zeng
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: Hindsight-Privileged RLVR (HP-RLVR) improves token credit assignment in RLVR by using single-rollout updates based on future outcomes, outperforming GRPO in efficiency and maintaining accuracy.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) trains language models from checked task outcomes, but assigning a terminal reward to individual reasoning tokens or actions remains difficult. Group-relative methods such as Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) sample several attempts per prompt, but lose their reward-based learning signal when all attempts receive the same outcome. We propose Hindsight-Privileged RLVR (HP-RLVR), a single-rollout method that turns a completed trajectory's own future into token-level update weights. The generating policy snapshot scores each eligible token under its causal history and under a hindsight context containing the realized future and verifier feedback. A normalized Jensen--Shannon divergence between the two views weights the reward relative to a historical baseline, yielding bounded token credit for both successful and failed attempts, with no reference solution or learned critic. In paired Qwen3-8B runs over a shared $100$-step schedule, HP-RLVR trains $1.21\times$, $1.46\times$, and $2.30\times$ faster than GRPO on mathematics, code generation, and ALFWorld, using one eighth the rollouts per prompt. Accuracy is comparable overall, with HP-RLVR ahead on mathematics at all three sizes and GRPO ahead on code and ALFWorld. In ALFWorld, $43.2\%$ (4B) and $49.0\%$ (8B) of GRPO's gradient-norm records are zero, versus none for HP-RLVR.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: DD-GBP: Anytime Multi-Arm Planning and Continuous Execution via Distributed Dynamic Gaussian Belief Propagation
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Zhao Jin, Fengyi Dai, Yuetong Yin, Yunan Wang, Wenjie Chen
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: The DD-GBP method enables efficient, safe, and scalable online multi-arm planning in dynamic environments, achieving high success rates and robust performance under communication challenges.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: Safely executing long-horizon multi-arm tasks online in complex dynamic environments remains challenging. We propose a new distributed dynamic Gaussian belief propagation (DD-GBP) method that directly plans joint-space trajectories through parallel local inference. A unified Gaussian-process (GP) parameterization connects adaptive planning horizons, interpolation-time factors, and continuous execution. Each robot maintains a local tree-structured factor graph and exchanges messages asynchronously over active inter-arm links. Dynamic subnet reconstruction and event-triggered updates reduce communication and inference costs while responding to moving obstacles. We also provide theoretical analyses of local inference accuracy, anytime early stopping, triggered-replanning consistency, and GP-consistent execution. In 50 long-horizon, multi-target four-arm scenes with moving obstacles, DD-GBP achieves $92.5\%$ collision-free all-target completion and the highest success rate among six representative baselines. Scenario ablations demonstrate long-horizon safety and robustness to communication impairment and extreme conditions; success remains $86.0\%$ under $90\%$ packet loss. Execution results further show substantially suppressed extreme velocity and acceleration peaks relative to Syn-GBP. On one workstation, obstacle-free tests with 30 coexisting arms retain $99.87\%$ success and a $15.80$ ms mean warm solve, exceeding 60 Hz and outperforming the compared methods in scalability. Dual-arm transport experiments under dynamic interference demonstrate online response and practical deployability. To the best of our knowledge, these results establish a new state of the art for online long-horizon multi-arm planning in dynamic scenes.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: EmbodiedEvo: Self-Evolving Coding Agent For Physical Intelligence
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Wenyi Li, Yizhe Chi, Youjie Zheng, Chunyu Liu, Xiaoqiu Wang
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: EmbodiedEvo is a self-evolving coding agent that distills physical feedback into reusable skills, enhancing performance in unseen tasks while reducing execution costs.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: Coding agents can construct executable programs and revise them through feedback, offering a foundation for embodied control without target-task fine-tuning. Through a programmatic robot interface, the agent observes the scene, executes control programs, and adapts them to the resulting physical state, serving as the closed-loop policy. However, this within-episode adaptation does not automatically preserve experience across scenes. Our trajectory analysis shows that agents spend interaction and inference budgets establishing effective operations and identifying their preconditions, while fresh agents cannot reuse these discoveries. This motivates EmbodiedEvo, a self-evolving coding agent that distills physical feedback into reusable code Skills and diagnostic Lessons. Experience is acquired on one Playground scene per task, then frozen for independent agents in unseen scenes, without updating model weights. On RoboDojo-Sim, EmbodiedEvo achieves an average score of 44.48 and a success rate of 37.82\%, surpassing all officially verified results. Paired tests show the largest gains on memory-dependent tasks and successful reuse of coordinated procedures, while fine contact control remains difficult. Experience from stronger models also improves weaker executors: Astra's experience raises Sol and Luna's success rates by 8.86 and 5.50 percentage points over no experience. Compared with raw interaction history, Skills and Lessons achieve comparable task performance at 53.0\% lower execution cost.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: OneLA: Learning Many Worlds from Latent Actions
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Ziyu Zhu, Zhaoxu Sun, Fan Jiang, Chiyu Wang, Junfeng Ni
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: OneLA introduces a framework for learning continuous latent actions from videos, enabling unified control across diverse domains and improving action transfer and generative performance.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: Learning world models across diverse domains calls for a unified control space, yet ac- tion interfaces vary across domains and action annotations are often scarce. Latent ac- tions learned directly from videos offer a promising way to establish such a space without explicit action supervision. However, learning shared latent actions across domains re- mains challenging, as variations in appearance, embodiment, and dynamics can entangle domain-specific visual cues with transferable transition structure. To this end, we intro- duce OneLA, a simple framework that learns continuous latent actions through a shared orthogonal dictionary and a common predictive objective, without task-specific designs or cross-domain alignment losses during latent action pretraining. These latent actions pro- vide a shared conditioning interface for world models, with lightweight adapters mapping native control commands into the same space. Conditioned on latent actions and the cur- rent visual state, the world model predicts context-dependent transitions for controllable rollout. OneLA improves action readout across domains and reduces action cycle-transfer rotation error by 24.8% over the strongest evaluated baseline. A joint-training comparison further shows a 20.5% improvement in Human Preference Score v3 (HPSv3) for real- scene generation. These results suggest a path toward general-purpose world models that learn from diverse videos and support flexible control through latent action space.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: FoveaVLA: Foveation Actions Replace the Wrist Camera in VLAs
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Bingao Chen, Lihan Zha, C. Karen Liu, Guy Tevet
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: FoveaVLA enhances Vision-Language-Action models by using learned foveation actions to replace wrist cameras, improving manipulation success rates in complex tasks.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: We present FoveaVLA, a Vision-Language-Action (VLA) model that replaces the wrist camera with learned foveation actions. Wrist cameras provide close-up detail but restrict the view to the end-effector's surroundings. External cameras see the whole scene, but the policy receives them at low resolution, so the fine detail needed for manipulation is lost. FoveaVLA recovers this detail by predicting, alongside each action chunk, the interaction region to observe at the next policy query. The policy then receives crops of these regions, taken from the original-resolution images, together with the full views. We build FoveaVLA on $π_{0.5}$ in two configurations, Single and Dual, using one or two external stereo cameras with full and foveal RGB and depth inputs, and post-train both on DROID with RoboInter interaction annotations. Across four real-world task suites, FoveaVLA-Single achieves 70.8% success with one external RGB-D view, and FoveaVLA-Dual achieves 77.1%, versus 52.1% for the wrist-equipped $π_{0.5}$. Both match the baseline on plain pick-and-place and improve success with distractors, cloth manipulation, and far-away objects.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: ActionOPD: Distilling Decisions, Not Tokens
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Huining Yuan, Xiangmin Yi, Zelai Xu, Zixu Wang, Xinlei Chen
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: ActionOPD introduces a novel action-level on-policy distillation method that aligns student agents with teacher decisions, improving performance without requiring token-level supervision or shared model architectures.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: Distilling capable language-model agents into smaller models requires aligning the student's behavior with the teacher's. This raises a fundamental question: at which states and at what granularity should this alignment be performed? Offline imitation provides dense but token-specific supervision and can suffer from state-distribution mismatch. Token-level on-policy distillation (OPD) addresses this mismatch but typically requires teacher token probabilities and compatible tokenization. We argue that semantic actions provide a natural unit of supervision for agent distillation. We introduce ActionOPD, an action-level on-policy distillation method motivated by maximizing expected teacher-action likelihood at student-encountered states. At each such state, ActionOPD samples actions from both the student and a black-box teacher, rewarding student actions according to their semantic agreement with the sampled teacher actions. Through policy optimization, ActionOPD aligns the student's action-level behavior with the teacher's decisions without requiring reproduction of teacher-written reasoning or access to teacher token probabilities. Training Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B with two teachers on diverse, curated tool-use tasks yields average gains of 3.3-6.9 percentage points across four out-of-distribution benchmarks. ActionOPD scales favorably with student size and teacher capability, without requiring the teacher and student to share a model family or tokenizer. On $τ^2$-bench, ActionOPD achieves competitive performance against offline distillation and token-level OPD. We further explore Self-ActionOPD with a same-model teacher and privileged context. These results establish ActionOPD as a promising approach to agent distillation.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: Interlock: From Local Correctness to Task Completion in Long-Horizon Agents
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Linji Hao, Yanji He, Zihan Wang, Hansi Yang, Jiayuan Zhang
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: The Interlock framework enhances long-horizon task completion in agents by using a typed completion graph to maintain relationships among tasks, improving performance metrics across various benchmarks.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: Large language model agents increasingly undertake long-horizon tasks in complex environments characterized by fragmented evidence, partially completed states, and dependencies across resources and artifacts. Existing agents may satisfy individual requirements while failing to maintain these relationships, producing locally correct but incomplete outcomes. These failures arise because task completion depends on relationships among environmental evidence, consequential decisions, and required effects. To address this completion gap, we propose Interlock, a framework for task synthesis that represents each task as a typed completion graph. Grounding edges connect public evidence to decisions, coupling hyperedges impose joint constraints across components, and realization edges connect decisions to all required downstream effects. Interlock compiles this graph into a resettable workspace, a public request, and an evaluation rubric. A source-coverage review checks whether the original requirements survive generation, while a public-input review checks whether the rubric is supported by the materials available to the solver. An agent-as-judge inspects execution artifacts and runs verification scripts, retaining trajectories judged to satisfy all mandatory requirements. To evaluate training utility, we fine-tune two Qwen3.6 backbones on their own accepted trajectories. Across the two backbones, training improves AutomationBench task pass rates by 4.00-4.50 percentage points, JobBench weighted scores by 3.20-6.64 points, and Harvey LAB criterion pass rates by 3.89-4.16 percentage points. These results demonstrate the training utility of the synthesized experience across external task environments.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: DEFlow: Deep Equilibrium Flow Maximum-Entropy Reinforcement Learning
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Ruslan Ageev, Huaze Tang, Runqing Miao, Jiarong Li, Wenbo Ding
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: DEFlow introduces a deep equilibrium flow policy that enhances sampling efficiency and off-policy training in reinforcement learning, achieving significant performance improvements across various tasks.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: Expressive flow policies can represent multiple high-value actions, but sampling them with few integration steps while retaining tractable action densities remains challenging. We introduce DEFlow, a deep equilibrium flow policy that replaces explicit Euler sampling with implicit Euler integration and solves all intermediate actions jointly as an equilibrium system. We combine implicit differentiation with a discrete change-of-variables formula for the final-action density, enabling off-policy training within soft actor-critic without backpropagating through solver iterations. DEFlow achieves an average relative improvement of approximately 10% in mean successful coverage over the strongest baseline across four Multi-Goal docking variants. It also achieves the highest mean time-averaged return on four of five manipulation tasks, while remaining broadly competitive across five MuJoCo tasks. These results support implicit flow policies for tasks requiring both diversity and precision, at the cost of additional nonlinear and linear solves. Primary

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: DexCast: Learning Real-World Dexterous Control from Human Videos
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Zihan Gao, Yuhong Zhang, Mengzhe Wang, Kaisheng Liu, Shengpeng Li
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: DEXCAST enables learning dexterous robotic hand control from monocular RGB-D videos using a novel perception module, eliminating the need for costly teleoperated demonstrations.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: Recent advances in 3D hand-object interaction (HOI) perception have opened new opportunities for learning dexterous robotic skills from human videos. However, existing dexterous imitation learning methods often rely on costly and manually teleoperated robot demonstrations, requiring substantial human effort. Therefore, we build DEXCAST, a framework that learns dexterous robotic hand control directly from monocular RGB-D videos by leveraging joint HOI reconstructions, without requiring any teleoperation. Furthermore, how to model high-dimensional robotic hand motion and extract temporal context to inform future action generation remains a key challenge. To this end, we propose a DexHand Motion Perception Module (DMPM) to capture inter-joint coordination and temporal dependencies in compact latent representations that condition our diffusion policy. Extensive real-world experiments demonstrate that DEXCAST achieves exceptional performance across diverse dexterous manipulation tasks.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: VGGT-Diff: Visual Geometry Meets Diffusion for Sparse-View Novel View Synthesis
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Kangjie Chen, Xiangyu Li, Dongbin Zhang, Chaoda Zheng, Shijia Chen
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: VGGT-Diff integrates geometry-based routing with a diffusion model for enhanced novel view synthesis from sparse views, achieving state-of-the-art performance through robust conditioning and consistency techniques.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: We present VGGT-Diff, a geometry-routed multi-view diffusion model for sparse-view novel view synthesis. Existing novel view synthesis (NVS) methods face a fundamental trade-off: reconstruction-based approaches preserve observed geometry but struggle to synthesize unseen regions, while diffusion-based methods provide strong generative priors yet rely on implicit source-to-query correspondence. VGGT-Diff bridges these regimes by routing visual geometry latents from VGGT-Ω into a pretrained video diffusion model. Each visual token is associated with a 3D point and confidence, then transformed into query-aligned latent conditions through a confidence-aware Visual Geometry Router (VGR) that preserves front and back surface evidence. These conditions guide joint target-view denoising, while Point-Track Residual Consistency (PTRC) regularizes predicted-clean residuals along reliable 3D tracks, improving multi-view stability. We further introduce robust geometry conditioning, combining training-time regularization with inference-time guidance for improved robustness. Experiments show competitive or state-of-the-art performance across interpolation and extrapolation under different viewpoint difficulties. Our code is available at https://github.com/chenkangjie1123/VGGT-Diff.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: Cracking Mobile Manipulation: From Failure Diagnosis to Agentic Robot System
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Zixuan Wang, Jia-Ning Li, Yinzhou Tang, Yanzhao Yu, Biao Wu
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: This paper identifies failure points in long-horizon mobile manipulation and presents interventions that significantly enhance task success rates in robotic systems.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: Recent vision-language-action (VLA) models have shown strong performance on local robot manipulation, yet their success does not readily translate to long-horizon mobile manipulation. In our experiments, a pretrained subtask VLA achieves 80% success rate on atomic manipulation tasks but only 19% when these skills are composed into mobile manipulation. We argue that this gap stems from failures across the execution process rather than from local manipulation capability alone. To uncover these bottlenecks, we systematically diagnose failures in long-horizon mobile manipulation and identify three dominant regimes: task planning, navigation and base positioning, and local manipulation. Based on this diagnosis, we develop failure-guided agentic intervention that augments a fixed subtask VLA with demonstration-based planning guidance, adaptive visual memory, accessibility-aware base adjustment, and local end-effector adjustment. On RoboCasa365, these interventions progressively improve task success from 19% to 47%, with the finalized system reaching 49% on held-out episode seeds, compared with 18% for the baseline. The same design improves performance from 14% to 37% on BEHAVIOR-1K and from 5/20 to 13/20 on real-robot tasks. These results suggest that reliable mobile manipulation can be advanced by diagnosing and intervening on the current bottleneck, rather than uniformly scaling the underlying policy. Our code will be released at https://github.com/PKU-VaLuE-Lab/Cracking-Mobile-Manipulation.git.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: How Far Can Coding Agents Go in Visual Generation?
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Hengguang Zhou, Yuanhao Ban, Jiaqi Feng, Xiaohuan Pei, Justin Cui
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: This paper investigates coding agents' capabilities in visual generation, highlighting their strengths in structure preservation and visual constraints, while exploring their internal representation and procedural skills.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: Modern image generation largely relies on specialized generative models that leave the process of image construction implicit in learned parameters. We explore an alternative: general-purpose coding agents that construct images through executable programs. Our study of zero-shot drawing on AgentDrawBench, a 200-prompt benchmark, reveals a distinctive capability profile. Agents excel at preserving structure and satisfying precise visual constraints, achieving competitive results in domains where compositional accuracy matters more than photorealistic appearance, while remaining limited in perceptual richness. Their visual expressiveness varies with the drawing interface, and a qualitative study on reconstruction shows how procedural skills extracted from human demonstrations support different artistic media. We then examine code as an external visual language of thought: a structured, executable representation that agents can construct and inspect. We test it in visual question answering task and find reconstructed visual code retains substantial information for question answering and, in some domains, supports higher accuracy than the original image. These abilities raise a further question: do agents draw on a shared internal representation of scene content beyond a particular drawing program? We explore an internal visual language-of-thought hypothesis, in which a shared, compositionally structured representation supports visual operations across drawing languages. Cross-harness drawings and images assembled from independent single-pixel queries exhibit related layouts and tones. Agents also maintain self-generated room arrangements across viewpoints after visible drawings are removed. These results demonstrate that the coding agent would maintain a consistent and coherent world inside its imagine even before the harness gets involved and the generation starts.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: MMTA: Benchmarking Multimodal Temporal Analysis with Time Series, Text, and Vision
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Ziyang Zhang, Shenyi Li, Yilin Wang, Ziyun Cui, Bowen Zhou
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: The MMTA benchmark evaluates multimodal temporal analysis across diverse domains, revealing challenges in integrating time series with visual evidence and proposing TimeOmni-v for improved performance.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: Time-series analysis is increasingly studied in multimodal settings, yet most benchmarks pair temporal signals with text or with visualizations derived from the same signal. This leaves open whether multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can integrate time series with real-world visual evidence. We introduce MMTA (multimodal temporal analysis), a benchmark of tri-modal tasks with diverse cross-modal complementarity patterns among time series, text, and vision. MMTA spans nine domains -- robotics, autonomous driving, human action, manufacturing, AR assistance, healthcare, recommendation, finance, and climate -- under video+TS and image+TS layouts, with a 3,524-sample test split covering classification and forecasting. The benchmark standardizes heterogeneous real-world sources into a shared schema with domain-specific prompts, provenance documentation, and success-weighted metrics that penalize both wrong answers and failed generations. Evaluating eight open-source and proprietary MLLMs reveals a shared bottleneck: representing time series as text creates very long token sequences and weakens fine-grained alignment with visual evidence, especially in long-video settings. We then introduce TimeOmni-v, a multimodal LLM extension with a dedicated time-series encoder, temporal positional alignment, modality-aware token layout, and a forecasting head. TimeOmni-v improves long-video classification and time-series inference efficiency, showing that MMTA not only exposes representation and grounding failures but also motivates targeted model design.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: SkillForge: Co-Evolving Skills and Agents via Dynamic Skill Lifecycles
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Yuyao Ge, Yiwei Wang, Yuchen He, Baolong Bi, Lingrui Mei
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: SkillForge enhances reinforcement learning by dynamically evolving a skill library through a fitness-driven lifecycle, improving agent performance while maintaining a compact skill set.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: Memory-augmented reinforcement learning strengthens LLM agents' ability to solve complex long-horizon tasks. Skills are one such form of memory, pairing instructions with an applicability condition over task types. However, retaining every skill indiscriminately as the policy improves lets obsolete or harmful entries accumulate and mislead the agent. We propose SkillForge, an agentic RL method that compiles and evolves the skill library through a fitness-driven skill lifecycle of trial, active, stable, and retired states, so that the skills and the model co-evolve throughout training. A pre-RL evaluation phase first uses the base model's own rollouts to pre-retire low-fitness skills, yielding a filtered library that then seeds supervised fine-tuning. Reinforcement learning takes over from this checkpoint, and at each iteration selective retirement, stabilization, and LLM-guided mutation continue to forge the skill library alongside policy optimization. Across multiple interactive agent benchmarks, SkillForge achieves the highest aggregate success rate, delivering up to 7.8% relative improvement over the strongest baseline while keeping the skill library compact throughout training. We introduce SkillFurnace, a dataset of 5k+ annotated records bundling retirement-filtered SFT trajectories, evolved skill libraries with fitness annotations, and retirement events with human-annotated failure categories to support research on skill quality and lifecycle management.

智能产业研究院 (AIR).title: ICM-Bench: Person-Level Identity Reasoning in Multimodal Agents with Long-Term Memory
智能产业研究院 (AIR).authors_text: Shidu Ren, Yunze Liu, Xing Liu, Chi-Hao Wu, Enmin Zhou
智能产业研究院 (AIR).summary: ICM-Bench introduces a benchmark for evaluating multimodal agents' ability to maintain and reason about person identities over long video memories, highlighting current limitations in identity-centric reasoning.
智能产业研究院 (AIR).debug_abstract: Long-horizon multimodal agents should remember not only what happened but also who participated. This capability depends on linking recurring faces, voices, names, person-associated objects, events, and social relations to consistent identities over time. Existing long-video and multimodal-agent benchmarks measure broad memory question answering, but they do not isolate the ability to maintain recurring person identities and reason over their cross-time relations.
