Remembering past observations alone may not be sufficient in every scenario, as they may no longer reflect the world after a sequence of actions. 机器人系统实验室 (RSL).authors_text: Julia Barth, Armin Sommer, Kunvar Thaman, Jannik Schilling

机器人系统实验室 (RSL).debug_abstract: Goal misgeneralization is a common failure mode in which an agent behaves competently out of distribution but does not pursue the intended goal. 机器人系统实验室 (RSL).authors_text: Linyi Huang, Guowei Huai, Weibin Liu, Shulong Jiang, Ping Tan

机器人系统实验室 (RSL).debug_abstract: While multi-fingered dexterous robot hands have the potential to provide human-level dexterity, using them for functional manipulation remains difficult because task success depends on precise contact, coordinated arm-hand motion, and reactive recovery from execution errors. Our key insight is to decouple the control complexity into a functional hand skill for precise contact execution and an arm-hand coordination policy for arm control and hand-skill activation. This design enables effective real-time human intervention for reactive recovery learning and efficient data collection with Dynamic Movement Primitive (DMP) augmentation. 机器人系统实验室 (RSL).authors_text: Eren Cetin, Julius Erbach, Vukasin Bozic, Hyojun Go, Zixiang Zhao

Recurrent memories keep a constant-size state, but retention is governed by temporal recurrence, causing old observations to fade with time. We introduce SMART, a slot memory addressed by region tokens, which combines bounded storage with spatially addressed recall. SMART stores content in a constant-size slot recurrence whose writes are addressed by the observing camera and whose reads are queried by the rendering camera, without constructing an explicit 3D representation or maintaining a growing cache. Consequently, recall is conditioned on inter-view geometry rather than on recency. Each read additionally provides a confidence estimate that conditions a chunk-causal diffusion transformer, allowing it to selectively trust retrieved content while relying on its generative prior elsewhere. On long trajectories in Memory Maze and Minecraft, SMART maintains high-fidelity recall far beyond its training horizon while using constant memory and per-step cost.

机器人系统实验室 (RSL).title: LIME: Learning Intent-aware Camera Motion from Egocentric Video
机器人系统实验室 (RSL).authors_text: Boyang Sun, Jiajie Li, Yung-Hsu Yang, Chenyangguang Zhang, Tim Engelbracht

机器人系统实验室 (RSL).debug_abstract: Autonomous robots often need to move their camera before they can act: to inspect an object, reveal an occluded region, or obtain a view that responds to a user's intent. This design lets the model jointly predict what the next view should reveal while representing multi-hypothesis target views. Across viewpoint-prediction experiments and downstream robotic tasks, we show that LIME learns intent-conditioned camera motion from passive egocentric video, turning ordinary human recordings into supervision for a reusable active-perception primitive that supports general-purpose viewpoint selection, manipulation, embodied question answering, and mid-distance navigation.

机器人系统实验室 (RSL).title: PROSE: Training-Free Egocentric Scene Registration with Vision-Language Models
机器人系统实验室 (RSL).authors_text: Zhiang Chen, Nahyuk Lee, Boyang Sun, Taein Kwon, Marc Pollefeys
机器人系统实验室 (RSL).summary: PROSE enables training-free egocentric scene registration using vision-language models to match object instances across RGB sequences, outperforming traditional methods in accuracy.
机器人系统实验室 (RSL).debug_abstract: Registering two captures of the same indoor space taken at different times underpins persistent spatial memory for robots and AR systems, yet the realistic version of this task is egocentric and its most scalable form is RGB-only. Head-mounted cameras yield blurry, fast-moving, partially overlapping views from which dense geometry is hard to recover. Classical registration leans on exactly the clean point clouds this setting lacks, while learned scene-graph methods require a pre-built or annotated graph and a trained matcher that we find brittle under egocentric data. PROSE adds no learned parameters and requires no depth sensor, training, or annotated graph. On the egocentric Aria Digital Twin and Aria Everyday Activities benchmarks, it outperforms both geometric and learned scene-graph baselines in registration accuracy, on ground-truth and RGB-reconstructed point clouds alike, and the scene graph it produces transfers directly to downstream tasks.

Sensing, Interaction & Perception Lab (S.title: VIGOR-MPC: Vision-Guided Objective Regulation MPC
Sensing, Interaction & Perception Lab (S.authors_text: Jelena Trisovic, Rahel Rickenbach, Marek Landert, Panagiotis Minos, Melanie N. Zeilinger
Sensing, Interaction & Perception Lab (S.summary: VIGOR-MPC is a vision-guided control framework that distills long-horizon MPC into a lightweight, adaptive short-horizon MPC for efficient navigation in noisy environments.
Sensing, Interaction & Perception Lab (S.debug_abstract: Controlling an agent in an environment solely perceived through onboard vision is challenging: perception yields noisy, variable-length, and partially occluded context, while onboard compute is shared between perception and control, limiting the planning horizon executable in real time. Sensing, Interaction & Perception Lab (S.authors_text: Tianyu Liu, Davide Belli, Bence Major, Arash Behboodi, Tribhuvanesh Orekondy

Oxford Robotics Institute (ORI).title: SAM3RL: Memory Control via Reinforcement Learning for Visual Object Tracking
Oxford Robotics Institute (ORI).authors_text: Tomáš Čížek, Matej Straka, Illia Volkov, Matěj Kripner, Ervin Macić
Oxford Robotics Institute (ORI).summary: SAM3RL enhances visual object tracking by using reinforcement learning for memory control, achieving state-of-the-art performance across multiple benchmarks without added runtime overhead.
Oxford Robotics Institute (ORI).debug_abstract: Segment Anything Model 3 (SAM 3) is a foundation model for image and video segmentation that sets the state of the art in visual object tracking. Its tracker, inherited from SAM 2, stores information from past frames in a memory bank, managed by a simple First-In-First-Out rule, allowing temporal consistency in complex videos. Several recent methods improve SAM 2 with hand-crafted memory update rules, each targeting a specific failure mode, such as distractors, occlusions, or object motion. However, their gains transfer only partially to the stronger SAM 3 backbone. We instead present a more general, data-driven approach that frames memory control as a sequential decision-making task. SAM3RL is an extension of the SAM 3 tracker with a lightweight memory controller, trained by reinforcement learning, that decides which frames enter the memory bank in order to maximize tracking performance. SAM3RL sets a new state of the art on 10 of 12 tracking and video object segmentation benchmarks, outperforming all hand-crafted rules without any runtime overhead. The same approach applied to SAM 2 gives SAM2RL, which outperforms hand-crafted rules on 9 of the 12 benchmarks, showing the generality of our method across model generations.

Oxford Robotics Institute (ORI).title: Refine Actions If Needed: Adaptive Action Chunk Refinement for Robot Manipulation
Oxford Robotics Institute (ORI).authors_text: Hanlin Liu, Zichen Zhou, Jiacheng Zhang, Liuyuan Na, Jin Jin
Oxford Robotics Institute (ORI).summary: RAIN is a framework that adaptively refines robot manipulation actions by predicting error levels, enhancing task success while minimizing inference latency.
Oxford Robotics Institute (ORI).debug_abstract: Computationally lightweight manipulation policies predict executable actions with low inference latency, but prediction errors can limit task success. Iterative generative policies can achieve higher task success rates, but repeated network evaluations increase inference latency. Refining action proposals from computationally lightweight policies can combine these strengths, but the amount of refinement needed varies across states. We introduce RAIN (Refine Actions If Needed), a framework that predicts action errors at different refinement levels to decide whether and how much to refine each executable proposal, before performing any refinement. We train an ensemble to predict these errors by comparing action proposals and their refined versions with expert actions from offline demonstrations, without requiring explicit labels of refinement needs. Calibration balances uncertainty, computation, and temporal consistency. We evaluate RAIN on eight ManiSkill tasks and four real-robot tasks. In simulation, our policy achieves 66.6% success, approaching the best evaluated diffusion-policy success rate with 5.71 times lower policy latency. On the real robot, success increases from 55.0% with Action Chunking with Transformers (ACT) to 72.5%, with comparable average successful completion time. Matched controls show that dynamic routing maintains the strongest observed fixed-refinement success level with 26.6% fewer refiner evaluations. Project page: https://rain-policy.github.io/.

Oxford Robotics Institute (ORI).title: Runtime Monitoring of Supermartingale Certificates
Oxford Robotics Institute (ORI).authors_text: Mirco Giacobbe, Thomas A. Henzinger, Konstantin Kueffner, Emily Yu, Đorđe Žikelić
Oxford Robotics Institute (ORI).summary: This paper presents a runtime monitoring algorithm for supermartingale certificates that detects violations in stochastic systems, enhancing reliability while minimizing false alarms.
Oxford Robotics Institute (ORI).debug_abstract: Supermartingale certificates formally guarantee temporal properties of discrete and continuous-time stochastic dynamical systems. However, these guarantees rely on a mathematical model of the world, leaving a sim-to-real gap that can invalidate them for the deployed system. We formulate the runtime monitoring problem for supermartingale certificates, in which a monitor observes a single system trajectory and raises an alarm when there is sufficient statistical evidence that the supermartingale certificate has been violated during execution. We present an algorithm to automatically construct a monitor using betting-based sequential tests that bound the probability of ever raising a false alarm at a user-specified level. Within this betting framework, we formulate strategies that allow the monitor to exploit spatial regularity to improve detection power while preserving this statistical guarantee. We demonstrate the efficacy of our approach on supermartingale certificate benchmarks from the literature.

电子科技大学.title: Physical Time as a Missing Dimension of Robot Policy Memory Dynamics
电子科技大学.authors_text: Yushen Liang, Yue Peng, Baosheng Jin, Tianluo Zhang, Xinyu Zhang
电子科技大学.summary: The paper introduces Temporal Flow Policy (TFP), enhancing robot memory dynamics by incorporating physical time, leading to improved action timing and performance in manipulation tasks.
电子科技大学.debug_abstract: Existing robot policy memories typically evolve with observation sequences, implicitly treating each update as the same amount of physical time. Yet identical observation histories can span different durations and require different actions, exposing physical time as a missing dimension of policy memory. We introduce Temporal Flow Policy (TFP), which learns memory dynamics to retain past events and evolve the memory state over measured time intervals. Observations and prior memory determine the content and time scales of each transition; elapsed time determines how far the state advances. TFP conditions diffusion and flow-matching policies through this memory state and is trained with their native imitation objectives. We evaluate TFP with Diffusion Policy and $π_{0.5}$ through controlled comparisons of memory designs. These experiments show that successful timing depends on both measured intervals and retained history. TFP achieves higher average success than the recurrent and state-space memories we equip with the same intervals and than a variant that feeds the interval to a learned gate. Memory readouts recover the time since an event and motion information after occlusion. Changing the supplied intervals systematically delays or advances actions, linking time inputs to behavior. Real-robot tasks requiring timing or memory, together with LIBERO evaluations, demonstrate benefits in physical and general manipulation. These results suggest viewing robot memory not as stored observation history, but as a state that retains past events and evolves with physical time.

电子科技大学.title: Reflect After Failure: Brain-Inspired Self-Evolving Agents for Embodied Spatial Intelligence
电子科技大学.authors_text: Xin Li, Xiaohuan Gu, Yifan Wang, Shaobin Ling, Tianli Shi
电子科技大学.summary: HiMeco, a brain-inspired self-evolving agent, enhances embodied spatial intelligence by diagnosing failures and refining strategies through metacognitive reflection and memory consolidation.
电子科技大学.debug_abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have made substantial progress in spatial reasoning, and self-evolving agents further extend these capabilities to embodied environments by learning from interactions. However, current self-evolution remains particularly challenging in embodied spatial tasks, complex and multi-step decisions from partial visual evidence making it difficult to determine why an execution fails. The failure may stem from misperception, insufficient exploration, or incorrect planning, yet execution feedback alone rarely reveals which component is responsible. As a result, simply accumulating interaction experience can reinforce ineffective strategies. To address this, we propose HiMeco, a brain-inspired self-evolving agent for embodied spatial intelligence, inspired by metacognitive monitoring and hippocampal memory consolidation. Through Hippocampal-Metacognitive Reflection, HiMeco diagnoses failures in perception-exploration-planning (PEP), then compares execution attempts to derive reusable strategies and guidance for avoiding recurring errors. It also abstracts interaction programs into parameterized skills, using evidence contracts and execution-based validation to determine their retention and reuse. These strategies and skills guide subsequent interactions, with memory updated only between rounds and model parameters kept frozen. HiMeco achieves state-of-the-art performance on ESI-Bench, and it also improves accuracy on EmbSpatial-Bench by 3.94 percentage points without evolution.

电子科技大学.title: Provable Transformer Context Compression for In-Context Reinforcement Learning
电子科技大学.authors_text: Yajie Zhao, Yingjun Mo, Zhiyong Wang, Bo Tang, Chao Xu
电子科技大学.summary: This paper establishes the minimum context dimension for in-context reinforcement learning using transformers, demonstrating optimal memory costs and approximation errors related to TD evaluation.
电子科技大学.debug_abstract: Transformers can perform in-context reinforcement learning without parameter updates. However, existing theoretical constructions often require context sizes that grow with the number of sampled transitions, leading to increasing memory costs in large-scale problems. This raises a fundamental scalability question: how much context is intrinsically necessary to carry out such learning? We answer this question for fixed-policy TD evaluation. We show that, with a shared linear decoder, the minimum context dimension required to exactly reproduce the first $L$ TD iterates is the Krylov dimension induced by the sampled transitions. When the available context dimension $m$ falls below this threshold, exact reproduction is no longer possible. In this regime, we characterize the optimal approximation error and show that it decays as $Θ(γ^m\max\{1,1/(m(1-γ))\})$ where $γ$ is the discounting factor. Moving from representation complexity to actual memory cost, we characterize the optimal retained memory for exact continuous representations as $Θ(nk_L)$ and show experimentally that on a sampled task whose exact rank is full but whose numerical rank is small, a context accurate to $10^{-2}$ is $88.7\%$ smaller than the sparse sufficient statistics of TD. Finally, we establish the learnability of the shared executor through pretraining by proving global convergence of an auxiliary objective over effective attention parameters under suitable task diversity. Experiments across diverse TD evaluation problems validate parameter recovery and the predicted context--accuracy tradeoff.

电子科技大学.title: Data-Free Continual Learning for World Action Model with Rectified Generative Replay
电子科技大学.authors_text: Kaipeng Fang, Hangxu Liu, Chaojian Shi, Yunsong Zhou, Hongzi Zhu
电子科技大学.summary: The paper presents R²-WAM, a method enabling data-free continual learning in world action models by autoregressively regenerating and rectifying past task rollouts to reduce forgetting.
电子科技大学.debug_abstract: World action models (WAMs) built on pretrained video generation models adapt quickly to new robotic tasks, but they forget previously learned tasks under sequential fine-tuning. Experience replay (ER) mitigates such forgetting by rehearsing data of previous tasks, yet this data is often unavailable in robotics, where a policy is deployed as weights only and its training data is not shared along with it. In this work, we ask whether a WAM can achieve data-free continual learning by regenerating its own past. Our key observation is that a WAM can indeed autoregressively regenerate complete rollouts of previously learned tasks and replay them to mitigate forgetting. However, replaying such raw rollouts still lags far behind replaying real data, which we attribute to two issues. First, the WAM is unable to recognize task completion and keeps generating purposeless motion after the task is done. Second, under open-loop generation, the generated actions gradually drift away from the generated observations. To address both issues, we present rectified generative replay (R$^2$-WAM), which truncates generated rollouts at task completion with an agentic evaluator and filters out rollouts whose actions are physically inconsistent with the observations. On the four LIBERO suites and five real-world tasks, R$^2$-WAM reduces forgetting by over 90% relative to sequential fine-tuning and nearly matches ER without accessing any data from previous tasks. Our analysis further reveals that forgetting in WAMs concentrates in inverse dynamics modeling: a forgotten WAM still produces visually plausible observations of previous tasks while its generated actions fail. Project page: https://kaipengfang.github.io/r2-wam/

电子科技大学.title: When Privileged Guidance Misaligns: State-Matched Routing and Contextualized Self-Distillation for Multi-Turn Agents
电子科技大学.authors_text: Junzhuo Liu, Weiwei Li, Jun Ling, Peng Wang
电子科技大学.summary: The paper presents SMRC-SD, a method that enhances multi-turn agent training by aligning state-matched routing with contextualized self-distillation to improve decision-making and performance.
电子科技大学.debug_abstract: Multi-turn agents trained with sparse outcome rewards receive limited supervision for intermediate decisions. Privileged on-policy self-distillation provides denser guidance by having a synchronized teacher re-score student responses with training-only references. However, the student may take different actions or complete subgoals in another order, reaching states for which the reference provides no applicable continuation. The resulting state--reference mismatch can lead the reference-conditioned teacher to penalize valid actions. We introduce State-Matched Routing and Contextualized Self-Distillation (SMRC-SD), which uses the student's reached state to decide when and how a reference should guide the student. At each turn, SMRC-SD checks state compatibility with the reference, distills only on matched turns, and contextualizes the reference by augmenting it with a reached-state summary and a compatible continuation. At inference, the policy requires neither references nor state matching. Experiments spanning three model sizes show gains over unconditional full-path self-distillation in embodied interaction (ALFWorld), web navigation (WebShop), and tool use (FTRL). FTRL-trained policies also transfer to BFCL and ToolHop without additional training. Code is available at https://github.com/liujunzhuo/SMRC-SD.

范明明老师实验室.title: TacClaw-Infinity: A Large-Scale Vision-Tactile-Language-Action Dataset for Dexterous Manipulation
范明明老师实验室.authors_text: Fucai Zhu, Xidong Zhang, Yichi Zhang, Yipan Wang, Fubo Wang
范明明老师实验室.summary: TacClaw-Infinity is a comprehensive VTLA dataset for dexterous manipulation, featuring over 10,000 hours of diverse, high-quality, structured tactile and visual data from various environments.
范明明老师实验室.debug_abstract: Large-scale robot learning increasingly relies on diverse human demonstrations, yet tactile manipulation data remain difficult to scale, and existing multimodal datasets often lack consistent quality control and structured supervision. We present TacClaw-Infinity, a large-scale structured Vision-Tactile-Language-Action (VTLA) dataset for contact-rich manipulation, collected with TacClaw, a tactile-enabled UMI-style handheld interface that records synchronized visual observations, fingertip tactile signals, and end-effector trajectories without requiring a target robot during data collection. TacClaw-Infinity is built through a distributed worldwide collection across homes, laboratories, industrial workplaces, retail stores, and outdoor environments including tasks contributed by academic and industrial collaborators. Together, these efforts yield over 10,000 hours, 1 million episodes, and 1 billion frames spanning more than 1,000 task types. We develop a scalable pipeline for trajectory reconstruction, multimodal quality control, embodiment-aware filtering, and structured annotation, covering contact-centric segmentation, subtask description, and spatial grounding. We validate TacClaw-Infinity at both the data and model levels: At the data level, we assess the collection interface, the action-space compatibility of the curated demonstrations, and the structured annotations, while for the model level, we demonstrate cross-embodiment transfer across three heterogeneous robots without robot-specific demonstrations.

范明明老师实验室.title: FOMI: A Force-Feedback Manipulation Interface for Teaching Contact-Rich Manipulation
范明明老师实验室.authors_text: Yishu Shen, Yiming Luo, Ruilin Wang, Bowen Yang, Shuai Yang
范明明老师实验室.summary: FOMI is a novel force-feedback interface that enhances robot-free collection of contact-rich demonstrations, improving efficiency and enabling effective teleoperation for manipulation tasks.
范明明老师实验室.debug_abstract: Robot-free collection with handheld interfaces enables scalable acquisition of human demonstrations for policy learning. However, existing handheld interfaces often provide limited intuitive force feedback, making contact-rich demonstration collection challenging for human operators. To address this, we present FOMI, a force-feedback manipulation interface with a scissor-shaped mechanism, which transmits object interaction forces directly to the operator's hands through actuation links without force sensors. This intuitive force feedback supports real-time action adjustment during robot-free collection of contact-rich demonstrations. Around FOMI, we build a demonstration collection system that integrates sensor calibration, data acquisition, and synchronization for robot-free collection. By further mapping pose changes and gripper opening of FOMI to robot end-effector poses and gripper commands, the system also supports teleoperation. Across four contact-rich tasks, FOMI improves collection efficiency by approximately 29% and 18% over the best baselines in robot-free collection and teleoperation, respectively. Demonstrations collected with FOMI in both modes enable policies to perform challenging contact-rich manipulation tasks with high success rates.

范明明老师实验室.title: Holi-Spatial 360: Generative Reconstruction from Sparse Panoramas for Spatial Rendering and Intelligence
范明明老师实验室.authors_text: Yuanyuan Gao, Zhirui Liu, Yuning Gong, Yifei Liu, Yifan Zhan
范明明老师实验室.summary: Holi-Spatial 360 presents a framework for generating annotated multi-room 3D environments from sparse panoramas, enhancing spatial reasoning in VLMs through improved reconstruction and curation.
范明明老师实验室.debug_abstract: Spatial intelligence requires scalable 3D environments that are both photorealistic and semantically grounded, yet existing indoor datasets are dominated by room-scale captures and costly LiDAR acquisition. Online real-estate platforms offer abundant panoramas of diverse multi-room homes, but sparse viewpoints and texture-poor regions make reconstruction severely under-constrained. We introduce Holi-Spatial 360, a generative reconstruction and data curation framework for converting these panoramas into annotated multi-room 3D environments. Because reconstruction quality bounds subsequent generation, our Correspondence-Guided Geometric Optimization converts feed-forward reconstruction priors into reliable cross-view constraints and builds a coherent 3D Gaussian Splatting representation as 3D spatial memory. Adapted single-image and video priors then restore appearance and complete continuous trajectories while preserving observed content. The reconstructed scenes support arbitrary RGB-D rendering and an automated curation pipeline that combines end-to-end 3D grounding with VLM-based verification. Holi360 contains over 1K multi-room 3DGS scenes, more than 100K instance annotations, and 2M spatial question-answer pairs. We also introduce the Holi360 benchmark to evaluate the spatial understanding of VLMs in real-world, multi-room indoor environments. Experiments demonstrate superior reconstruction and curation quality under sparse panoramic inputs, while fine-tuning VLMs on Holi360 substantially improves spatial reasoning capabilities.

范明明老师实验室.title: Why Do VLMs Fail at Remote Physiological Measurement? Rethinking with Physiological Grounding and Numerical Alignment
范明明老师实验室.authors_text: Xiao Yang, Zekun Zhang, Yuxuan Fan, Duoxun Tang, Ziyang Liu
范明明老师实验室.summary: The paper introduces VITAL, a framework enhancing Vision-Language Models for remote physiological measurement by aligning visual and physiological data while improving numerical accuracy.
范明明老师实验室.debug_abstract: Video-based remote physiological measurement (RPM) has broad applications, while Vision-Language Models (VLMs) provide a promising opportunity to enable end-to-end physiological monitoring for future human-aware intelligent systems. However, existing RPM methods rely on task-specific models and cannot be seamlessly integrated with the multimodal understanding and interaction capabilities of VLMs. We revisit RPM with VLMs and provide empirical evidence for two major bottlenecks: generic visual semantic representations fail to preserve fine-grained physiological cues; while discrete token prediction in autoregressive generation is inherently misaligned with continuous numerical measurement. To address these challenges, we propose VITAL (Visual-physiological Token Alignment for Language Models), a visual-physiological token alignment framework for RPM and preserving general vision tasks. VITAL retains the original visual pathway for semantic understanding and introduces an independent physiological pathway to jointly model semantic and physiological information. Moreover, we propose a structured numerical alignment approach to improve the reliability of generative heart rate estimation by enhancing numerical relationship modeling. Extensive experiments show that VITAL improves cross-domain estimation performance on multiple rPPG datasets while preserving the general visual understanding capability of VLMs, demonstrating its effectiveness as a unified visual-physiological model. Code will be released.

范明明老师实验室.title: EvoSpatial: Experience-Driven Skill and Tool Evolution for Spatial Reasoning Agents
范明明老师实验室.authors_text: Bin Yu, Shijie Lian, Zhaolong Shen, Xiaopeng Lin, Yao Zhang
范明明老师实验室.summary: EvoSpatial is a framework that enhances spatial reasoning agents by evolving skills and tools through execution feedback, improving performance across multiple benchmarks without requiring ground-truth data.
范明明老师实验室.debug_abstract: Spatial reasoning agents can inspect tool outputs and repair errors, but reusing these lessons requires preserving both the computation and the conditions that make it valid. We introduce EvoSpatial, a framework that learns from execution experience by updating a library of linked skills and tools. Skills describe procedures, geometric assumptions, and verification steps; tools implement the operations those procedures require. When solving a task, the agent retrieves relevant skills and synthesizes reusable computational functions if existing tools are insufficient. After each task, execution feedback and evidence checks guide skill revision and tool consolidation, without ground-truth answers or benchmark scores. Across 20 benchmarks, EvoSpatial averages 63.9, 4.0 percentage points above the average reported by SpatialClaw. The evolved library also improves held-out and cross-benchmark performance when updates are disabled, and trajectories generated with evolved skills improve supervised fine-tuning, even without external skills at evaluation. Keeping checked procedures on record, together with the tools that support them, lets an agent carry spatial reasoning experience from one task to the next.

范明明老师实验室.title: Hindsight-Privileged RLVR: Single-Rollout Token Credit Without Group Sampling
范明明老师实验室.authors_text: Wei Chen, Yubing Wu, Zhou Xu, Haoyue Zhang, Delu Zeng
范明明老师实验室.summary: Hindsight-Privileged RLVR (HP-RLVR) improves token credit assignment in RLVR by using single-rollout updates based on future outcomes, outperforming GRPO in efficiency and maintaining accuracy.
范明明老师实验室.debug_abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) trains language models from checked task outcomes, but assigning a terminal reward to individual reasoning tokens or actions remains difficult. Group-relative methods such as Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) sample several attempts per prompt, but lose their reward-based learning signal when all attempts receive the same outcome. We propose Hindsight-Privileged RLVR (HP-RLVR), a single-rollout method that turns a completed trajectory's own future into token-level update weights. The generating policy snapshot scores each eligible token under its causal history and under a hindsight context containing the realized future and verifier feedback. A normalized Jensen--Shannon divergence between the two views weights the reward relative to a historical baseline, yielding bounded token credit for both successful and failed attempts, with no reference solution or learned critic. In paired Qwen3-8B runs over a shared $100$-step schedule, HP-RLVR trains $1.21\times$, $1.46\times$, and $2.30\times$ faster than GRPO on mathematics, code generation, and ALFWorld, using one eighth the rollouts per prompt. Accuracy is comparable overall, with HP-RLVR ahead on mathematics at all three sizes and GRPO ahead on code and ALFWorld. In ALFWorld, $43.2\%$ (4B) and $49.0\%$ (8B) of GRPO's gradient-norm records are zero, versus none for HP-RLVR.

范明明老师实验室.title: SkillCommit: Evolving Agent Skills through Behaviorally Validated Scope Expansion
范明明老师实验室.summary: SkillCommit is an online framework that evolves agent skills by preserving instance-specific experiences and hierarchically abstracting behaviorally validated strategies to enhance performance.
范明明老师实验室.debug_abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents can continually improve without parameter updates by converting historical experience into reusable procedural knowledge. However, existing methods often consolidate experience based on semantic similarity or LLM judgments, which may merge superficially related but behaviorally incompatible strategies and thereby degrade performance. To address the issue, we propose SkillCommit, an online skill evolution framework that continuously transforms experience into a hierarchical library of reusable skills. Rather than generalizing from individual experiences immediately, SkillCommit first preserves each experience as an instance-specific patch, retaining its locally validated behavior. As patches accumulate, SkillCommit abstracts those sharing a common behavioral mechanism into higher-level skills. Specifically, for each incoming skill, embedding-based retrieval first identifies candidate related skills. Cross-instance replay and an LLM-based mechanism check determine whether these skills transfer across cases and share a common underlying mechanism. Candidates that pass both checks are abstracted into a higher-level skill and committed only if it preserves the validated behavior of all constituent skills. Experiments on RuleArena, OpenExempt and KOR-Bench demonstrate that SkillCommit consistently improves agent performance across diverse domains. Moreover, the learned skills transfer across model scales and families, enabling cross-model experience transfer.

范明明老师实验室.title: GeoCloak: An Agentic Framework for Semantics-Preserving Geolocation Privacy via Peripheral Clue Manipulation
范明明老师实验室.authors_text: Yixin Wu, Mingjie Li, Yun Shen, Michael Backes, Yang Zhang
范明明老师实验室.summary: GeoCloak is a framework that enhances geolocation privacy by manipulating peripheral clues in images while preserving semantic content, significantly reducing location inference accuracy.
范明明老师实验室.debug_abstract: The rapid advancement of large vision language models (LVLMs) has made geolocation inference from images highly accurate and accessible. This poses serious privacy risks: a passive adversary with black-box LVLM access can infer a user's location from a single photo with no metadata. Existing protection methods rely almost exclusively on adversarial perturbation, which introduces perceptible visual artifacts and utility degradation. We identify the visual-geolocation asymmetry: geolocation-decisive clues, such as street signs, tend to be visually peripheral but dominate location inference. Exploiting this asymmetry, we propose GeoCloak, an agentic framework for semantics-preserving geolocation privacy protection. It acts as a clue-aware planner that analyzes each image to identify geolocation-relevant clues, dispatches targeted semantic edits to directly suppress peripheral clues, and autonomously configures adversarial perturbation to further suppress residual geolocation features, all under iterative utility-aware feedback. We evaluate GeoCloak on four diverse datasets spanning 108 countries and 576 cities against five LVLMs and three inference methods. GeoCloak reduces overall city-level accuracy from 41.2% to 9.9%, approximately half of the best-performing baseline, while achieving substantially superior utility preservation both qualitatively and quantitatively. We hope this work takes a meaningful step toward practical, semantics-preserving geolocation privacy protection, giving users greater control over the location information inadvertently embedded in their shared images.

范明明老师实验室.title: Refine Actions If Needed: Adaptive Action Chunk Refinement for Robot Manipulation
范明明老师实验室.authors_text: Hanlin Liu, Zichen Zhou, Jiacheng Zhang, Liuyuan Na, Jin Jin
范明明老师实验室.summary: RAIN is a framework that adaptively refines robot manipulation actions by predicting error levels, enhancing task success while minimizing inference latency.
范明明老师实验室.debug_abstract: Computationally lightweight manipulation policies predict executable actions with low inference latency, but prediction errors can limit task success. Iterative generative policies can achieve higher task success rates, but repeated network evaluations increase inference latency. Refining action proposals from computationally lightweight policies can combine these strengths, but the amount of refinement needed varies across states. We introduce RAIN (Refine Actions If Needed), a framework that predicts action errors at different refinement levels to decide whether and how much to refine each executable proposal, before performing any refinement. We train an ensemble to predict these errors by comparing action proposals and their refined versions with expert actions from offline demonstrations, without requiring explicit labels of refinement needs. Calibration balances uncertainty, computation, and temporal consistency. We evaluate RAIN on eight ManiSkill tasks and four real-robot tasks. In simulation, our policy achieves 66.6% success, approaching the best evaluated diffusion-policy success rate with 5.71 times lower policy latency. On the real robot, success increases from 55.0% with Action Chunking with Transformers (ACT) to 72.5%, with comparable average successful completion time. Matched controls show that dynamic routing maintains the strongest observed fixed-refinement success level with 26.6% fewer refiner evaluations. Project page: https://rain-policy.github.io/.

范明明老师实验室.title: Interlock: From Local Correctness to Task Completion in Long-Horizon Agents
范明明老师实验室.authors_text: Linji Hao, Yanji He, Zihan Wang, Hansi Yang, Jiayuan Zhang
范明明老师实验室.summary: The Interlock framework enhances long-horizon task completion in agents by using a typed completion graph to maintain relationships among tasks, improving performance metrics across various benchmarks.
范明明老师实验室.debug_abstract: Large language model agents increasingly undertake long-horizon tasks in complex environments characterized by fragmented evidence, partially completed states, and dependencies across resources and artifacts. Existing agents may satisfy individual requirements while failing to maintain these relationships, producing locally correct but incomplete outcomes. These failures arise because task completion depends on relationships among environmental evidence, consequential decisions, and required effects. To address this completion gap, we propose Interlock, a framework for task synthesis that represents each task as a typed completion graph. Grounding edges connect public evidence to decisions, coupling hyperedges impose joint constraints across components, and realization edges connect decisions to all required downstream effects. Interlock compiles this graph into a resettable workspace, a public request, and an evaluation rubric. A source-coverage review checks whether the original requirements survive generation, while a public-input review checks whether the rubric is supported by the materials available to the solver. An agent-as-judge inspects execution artifacts and runs verification scripts, retaining trajectories judged to satisfy all mandatory requirements. To evaluate training utility, we fine-tune two Qwen3.6 backbones on their own accepted trajectories. Across the two backbones, training improves AutomationBench task pass rates by 4.00-4.50 percentage points, JobBench weighted scores by 3.20-6.64 points, and Harvey LAB criterion pass rates by 3.89-4.16 percentage points. These results demonstrate the training utility of the synthesized experience across external task environments.

范明明老师实验室.title: GAE: Learning a Geometry-Native Latent Space for 3D-Consistent World Generation
范明明老师实验室.authors_text: Jiahao Lu, Minghao Yin, Wenbo Hu, Hengyu Liu, Wang Zhao
范明明老师实验室.summary: The GAE introduces a geometry-native latent space enhancing 3D-consistent world generation, improving visual quality and coherence by reparameterizing features for diverse tasks.
范明明老师实验室.debug_abstract: We present a compact geometry-native latent space as a shared foundation for perception and generation. Visual generators can produce photorealistic frames without preserving a consistent 3D scene. We argue that this is not only a modeling problem but also a representation problem: generators typically evolve appearance-centric latents, while perception models recover geometry in a semantically rich space that encodes cross-view structure. Rather than adding geometry as another output, we reparameterize a geometry foundation model's features into a compact latent space for generation. We realize this shift with the geometry-native autoencoder (GAE), whose latent is jointly decodable to appearance, depth, cameras, and point maps. With this state, a standard conditional flow supports diverse generation tasks. In controlled comparisons that hold the generator and training protocol fixed, replacing the latent with GAE improves both visual quality and independently measured 3D coherence: FVD falls by $12.7\%$ and $23.1\%$ on RealEstate10K and DL3DV, and camera-trajectory error is halved on RealEstate10K. Together, these results show that the latent space is central to geometry-consistent generation and can serve as a shared interface between perception and generation.

范明明老师实验室.title: Synergistic Vision-Language Reinforcement Enables Scalable On-Demand Analysis across Diverse Clinical Tasks
范明明老师实验室.authors_text: Haonan Wang, Jiaji Mao, Lehan Wang, Qixiang Zhang, Marawan Elbatel
范明明老师实验室.summary: SyRe is a vision-language reinforcement model that enhances tumor and organ segmentation in oncology through diverse prompts and extensive training data, achieving high accuracy and generalization.
范明明老师实验室.debug_abstract: Accurate segmentation of tumors and organs-at-risk is essential for oncology but remains time-consuming and expertise-intensive. Existing AI systems often require manual spatial prompts or task-specific retraining, while generic class labels provide limited guidance for heterogeneous disease targets. Here we present SyRe, a text-prompted segmentation foundation model based on Synergistic vision-language Reinforcement, which strengthens bidirectional interaction between visual and linguistic representations. We introduce Color Region Description (CRD) to generate region-level semantic supervision and construct SyReData, comprising 20 million image-mask-description triplets across 9 modalities and 229 segmentation tasks. Training with diversified prompt formats enables single-target, multi-target and open-ended segmentation, together with invalid-prompt rejection. SyRe achieves accurate segmentation across diverse clinical scenarios, with strong gains on disease-related targets. Evaluation on 28 unseen external datasets, including 17 cancer types, 3 non-cancer diseases and multinational in-house cohorts, demonstrates generalization under distribution shift. Beyond spatial overlap, SyRe-generated masks preserve quantitative pathology information. Across five retrospective tumor imaging cohorts spanning CT and MRI, radiomics derived from these masks stratify survival and improve prognostic modeling over clinical baselines. Clinician-in-the-loop refinement further supports case-level correction. These results establish SyRe as a generalizable framework for scalable quantitative oncology analysis and clinician-guided segmentation.

范明明老师实验室.title: ReEnvision: Future-Guided Selective Action Repair for Long-Horizon Manipulation
范明明老师实验室.authors_text: Xiyin Zeng, Xuewei Huang, Yi Lu, Weihao Yuan, Hao Wang
范明明老师实验室.summary: ReEnvision introduces a future-guided selective action repair framework for long-horizon robotic manipulation, enhancing action success rates by preserving valid actions amid execution deviations.
范明明老师实验室.debug_abstract: Long-horizon robotic manipulation requires robust execution over sequences of interdependent actions. Existing methods typically handle execution deviations by replanning the remaining action chunk or correcting actions step by step as new observations arrive. However, a local deviation may affect only a few actions under distribution shift, yet replanning regenerates the entire chunk from an unfamiliar state, potentially introducing errors into otherwise valid actions. Step-wise correction may react too late, as it does not explicitly anticipate how the deviation affects subsequent actions. We propose ReEnvision, a future-guided selective action repair framework that updates a joint future-action belief using execution feedback. It then learns how the resulting belief revision affects each unexecuted action. The resulting belief revision enables selective repair of only the affected actions within a cached action chunk, preserving valid actions and reserving full replanning for severe deviations. On CALVIN, L-CALVIN, and RLBench, ReEnvision achieves 86.6% 5-step success, improves 10-step success from 56% to 63%, and reaches an average success rate of 88.8%, respectively. On five real-world manipulation tasks, it achieves an average success rate of 82.8%. Controlled repair experiments further demonstrate the benefits of localizing affected actions and preserving valid ones during execution.

范明明老师实验室.title: AVA-Encoder: Towards Agent-Native Video Representation Learning
范明明老师实验室.authors_text: Chuyue Li, Jinpeng Yu, Haozhe Wang, Tian Xueyun, Zhijing Zhang
范明明老师实验室.summary: The AVA-Encoder transforms finished films into agent-native representations via a Film Knowledge Graph, enhancing video creation quality and enabling improved editing and downstream applications.
范明明老师实验室.debug_abstract: Agentic video creation systems remain far from cinematic-grade quality: their underlying models struggle to plan how story, characters, visuals, and sound fit together, and high-quality creation trajectories to learn such planning abilities are scarce. Finished human films embody this knowledge, but in a tightly coupled audiovisual form that agents cannot directly read or manipulate. We propose the Agentic Video Auto-Encoder (AVA-Encoder), which works backward from finished films, turning them into agent-native representations with reconstruction itself as supervision. It encodes a film into a Film Knowledge Graph (Film KG) of structured-text nodes, typed dependency edges, and linked multimodal assets, then regenerates the film from this graph with a fixed decoder. Reconstruction residuals are distilled into textual gradients that drive dual-loop self-evolution: an outer loop learns a shared encoding policy across videos, and an inner loop refines each video's Film KG at test time. AVA-Encoder improves reconstruction fidelity by 20.7 percentage points over the strongest baseline; its learned policy outperforms a finely human-tuned policy with over 70 percent fewer system-prompt tokens; and Film KGs support coordinated editing and improve all tested downstream creation systems. We release the framework, a reconstruction benchmark, and a Film KG dataset.

Cheng Kar-Shun Robotics Institute (CKSRI.title: TacClaw-Infinity: A Large-Scale Vision-Tactile-Language-Action Dataset for Dexterous Manipulation
Cheng Kar-Shun Robotics Institute (CKSRI.authors_text: Fucai Zhu, Xidong Zhang, Yichi Zhang, Yipan Wang, Fubo Wang
Cheng Kar-Shun Robotics Institute (CKSRI.summary: TacClaw-Infinity is a comprehensive VTLA dataset for dexterous manipulation, featuring over 10,000 hours of diverse, high-quality, structured tactile and visual data from various environments.
Cheng Kar-Shun Robotics Institute (CKSRI.debug_abstract: Large-scale robot learning increasingly relies on diverse human demonstrations, yet tactile manipulation data remain difficult to scale, and existing multimodal datasets often lack consistent quality control and structured supervision. We present TacClaw-Infinity, a large-scale structured Vision-Tactile-Language-Action (VTLA) dataset for contact-rich manipulation, collected with TacClaw, a tactile-enabled UMI-style handheld interface that records synchronized visual observations, fingertip tactile signals, and end-effector trajectories without requiring a target robot during data collection. TacClaw-Infinity is built through a distributed worldwide collection across homes, laboratories, industrial workplaces, retail stores, and outdoor environments including tasks contributed by academic and industrial collaborators. Together, these efforts yield over 10,000 hours, 1 million episodes, and 1 billion frames spanning more than 1,000 task types. We develop a scalable pipeline for trajectory reconstruction, multimodal quality control, embodiment-aware filtering, and structured annotation, covering contact-centric segmentation, subtask description, and spatial grounding. We validate TacClaw-Infinity at both the data and model levels: At the data level, we assess the collection interface, the action-space compatibility of the curated demonstrations, and the structured annotations, while for the model level, we demonstrate cross-embodiment transfer across three heterogeneous robots without robot-specific demonstrations.

Cheng Kar-Shun Robotics Institute (CKSRI.title: FOMI: A Force-Feedback Manipulation Interface for Teaching Contact-Rich Manipulation
Cheng Kar-Shun Robotics Institute (CKSRI.authors_text: Yishu Shen, Yiming Luo, Ruilin Wang, Bowen Yang, Shuai Yang
Cheng Kar-Shun Robotics Institute (CKSRI.summary: FOMI is a novel force-feedback interface that enhances robot-free collection of contact-rich demonstrations, improving efficiency and enabling effective teleoperation for manipulation tasks.
Cheng Kar-Shun Robotics Institute (CKSRI.debug_abstract: Robot-free collection with handheld interfaces enables scalable acquisition of human demonstrations for policy learning. However, existing handheld interfaces often provide limited intuitive force feedback, making contact-rich demonstration collection challenging for human operators. To address this, we present FOMI, a force-feedback manipulation interface with a scissor-shaped mechanism, which transmits object interaction forces directly to the operator's hands through actuation links without force sensors. This intuitive force feedback supports real-time action adjustment during robot-free collection of contact-rich demonstrations. Around FOMI, we build a demonstration collection system that integrates sensor calibration, data acquisition, and synchronization for robot-free collection. By further mapping pose changes and gripper opening of FOMI to robot end-effector poses and gripper commands, the system also supports teleoperation. Across four contact-rich tasks, FOMI improves collection efficiency by approximately 29% and 18% over the best baselines in robot-free collection and teleoperation, respectively. Demonstrations collected with FOMI in both modes enable policies to perform challenging contact-rich manipulation tasks with high success rates.

Cheng Kar-Shun Robotics Institute (CKSRI.title: Holi-Spatial 360: Generative Reconstruction from Sparse Panoramas for Spatial Rendering and Intelligence
Cheng Kar-Shun Robotics Institute (CKSRI.authors_text: Yuanyuan Gao, Zhirui Liu, Yuning Gong, Yifei Liu, Yifan Zhan
Cheng Kar-Shun Robotics Institute (CKSRI.summary: Holi-Spatial 360 presents a framework for generating annotated multi-room 3D environments from sparse panoramas, enhancing spatial reasoning in VLMs through improved reconstruction and curation.
Cheng Kar-Shun Robotics Institute (CKSRI.debug_abstract: Spatial intelligence requires scalable 3D environments that are both photorealistic and semantically grounded, yet existing indoor datasets are dominated by room-scale captures and costly LiDAR acquisition. Online real-estate platforms offer abundant panoramas of diverse multi-room homes, but sparse viewpoints and texture-poor regions make reconstruction severely under-constrained. We introduce Holi-Spatial 360, a generative reconstruction and data curation framework for converting these panoramas into annotated multi-room 3D environments. Because reconstruction quality bounds subsequent generation, our Correspondence-Guided Geometric Optimization converts feed-forward reconstruction priors into reliable cross-view constraints and builds a coherent 3D Gaussian Splatting representation as 3D spatial memory. Adapted single-image and video priors then restore appearance and complete continuous trajectories while preserving observed content. The reconstructed scenes support arbitrary RGB-D rendering and an automated curation pipeline that combines end-to-end 3D grounding with VLM-based verification. Holi360 contains over 1K multi-room 3DGS scenes, more than 100K instance annotations, and 2M spatial question-answer pairs. We also introduce the Holi360 benchmark to evaluate the spatial understanding of VLMs in real-world, multi-room indoor environments. Experiments demonstrate superior reconstruction and curation quality under sparse panoramic inputs, while fine-tuning VLMs on Holi360 substantially improves spatial reasoning capabilities.

Cheng Kar-Shun Robotics Institute (CKSRI.title: Why Do VLMs Fail at Remote Physiological Measurement? Rethinking with Physiological Grounding and Numerical Alignment
Cheng Kar-Shun Robotics Institute (CKSRI.authors_text: Xiao Yang, Zekun Zhang, Yuxuan Fan, Duoxun Tang, Ziyang Liu
Cheng Kar-Shun Robotics Institute (CKSRI.summary: The paper introduces VITAL, a framework enhancing Vision-Language Models for remote physiological measurement by aligning visual and physiological data while improving numerical accuracy.
Cheng Kar-Shun Robotics Institute (CKSRI.debug_abstract: Video-based remote physiological measurement (RPM) has broad applications, while Vision-Language Models (VLMs) provide a promising opportunity to enable end-to-end physiological monitoring for future human-aware intelligent systems. However, existing RPM methods rely on task-specific models and cannot be seamlessly integrated with the multimodal understanding and interaction capabilities of VLMs. We revisit RPM with VLMs and provide empirical evidence for two major bottlenecks: generic visual semantic representations fail to preserve fine-grained physiological cues; while discrete token prediction in autoregressive generation is inherently misaligned with continuous numerical measurement. To address these challenges, we propose VITAL (Visual-physiological Token Alignment for Language Models), a visual-physiological token alignment framework for RPM and preserving general vision tasks. VITAL retains the original visual pathway for semantic understanding and introduces an independent physiological pathway to jointly model semantic and physiological information. Moreover, we propose a structured numerical alignment approach to improve the reliability of generative heart rate estimation by enhancing numerical relationship modeling. Extensive experiments show that VITAL improves cross-domain estimation performance on multiple rPPG datasets while preserving the general visual understanding capability of VLMs, demonstrating its effectiveness as a unified visual-physiological model. Code will be released.

Cheng Kar-Shun Robotics Institute (CKSRI.title: EvoSpatial: Experience-Driven Skill and Tool Evolution for Spatial Reasoning Agents
Cheng Kar-Shun Robotics Institute (CKSRI.authors_text: Bin Yu, Shijie Lian, Zhaolong Shen, Xiaopeng Lin, Yao Zhang
Cheng Kar-Shun Robotics Institute (CKSRI.summary: EvoSpatial is a framework that enhances spatial reasoning agents by evolving skills and tools through execution feedback, improving performance across multiple benchmarks without requiring ground-truth data.
Cheng Kar-Shun Robotics Institute (CKSRI.debug_abstract: Spatial reasoning agents can inspect tool outputs and repair errors, but reusing these lessons requires preserving both the computation and the conditions that make it valid. We introduce EvoSpatial, a framework that learns from execution experience by updating a library of linked skills and tools. Skills describe procedures, geometric assumptions, and verification steps; tools implement the operations those procedures require. When solving a task, the agent retrieves relevant skills and synthesizes reusable computational functions if existing tools are insufficient. After each task, execution feedback and evidence checks guide skill revision and tool consolidation, without ground-truth answers or benchmark scores. Across 20 benchmarks, EvoSpatial averages 63.9, 4.0 percentage points above the average reported by SpatialClaw. The evolved library also improves held-out and cross-benchmark performance when updates are disabled, and trajectories generated with evolved skills improve supervised fine-tuning, even without external skills at evaluation. Keeping checked procedures on record, together with the tools that support them, lets an agent carry spatial reasoning experience from one task to the next.

Cheng Kar-Shun Robotics Institute (CKSRI.title: Hindsight-Privileged RLVR: Single-Rollout Token Credit Without Group Sampling
Cheng Kar-Shun Robotics Institute (CKSRI.authors_text: Wei Chen, Yubing Wu, Zhou Xu, Haoyue Zhang, Delu Zeng
Cheng Kar-Shun Robotics Institute (CKSRI.summary: Hindsight-Privileged RLVR (HP-RLVR) improves token credit assignment in RLVR by using single-rollout updates based on future outcomes, outperforming GRPO in efficiency and maintaining accuracy.
Cheng Kar-Shun Robotics Institute (CKSRI.debug_abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) trains language models from checked task outcomes, but assigning a terminal reward to individual reasoning tokens or actions remains difficult. Group-relative methods such as Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) sample several attempts per prompt, but lose their reward-based learning signal when all attempts receive the same outcome. We propose Hindsight-Privileged RLVR (HP-RLVR), a single-rollout method that turns a completed trajectory's own future into token-level update weights. The generating policy snapshot scores each eligible token under its causal history and under a hindsight context containing the realized future and verifier feedback. A normalized Jensen--Shannon divergence between the two views weights the reward relative to a historical baseline, yielding bounded token credit for both successful and failed attempts, with no reference solution or learned critic. In paired Qwen3-8B runs over a shared $100$-step schedule, HP-RLVR trains $1.21\times$, $1.46\times$, and $2.30\times$ faster than GRPO on mathematics, code generation, and ALFWorld, using one eighth the rollouts per prompt. Accuracy is comparable overall, with HP-RLVR ahead on mathematics at all three sizes and GRPO ahead on code and ALFWorld. In ALFWorld, $43.2\%$ (4B) and $49.0\%$ (8B) of GRPO's gradient-norm records are zero, versus none for HP-RLVR.

Cheng Kar-Shun Robotics Institute (CKSRI.title: SkillCommit: Evolving Agent Skills through Behaviorally Validated Scope Expansion
Cheng Kar-Shun Robotics Institute (CKSRI.summary: SkillCommit is an online framework that evolves agent skills by preserving instance-specific experiences and hierarchically abstracting behaviorally validated strategies to enhance performance.
Cheng Kar-Shun Robotics Institute (CKSRI.debug_abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents can continually improve without parameter updates by converting historical experience into reusable procedural knowledge. However, existing methods often consolidate experience based on semantic similarity or LLM judgments, which may merge superficially related but behaviorally incompatible strategies and thereby degrade performance. To address the issue, we propose SkillCommit, an online skill evolution framework that continuously transforms experience into a hierarchical library of reusable skills. Rather than generalizing from individual experiences immediately, SkillCommit first preserves each experience as an instance-specific patch, retaining its locally validated behavior. As patches accumulate, SkillCommit abstracts those sharing a common behavioral mechanism into higher-level skills. Specifically, for each incoming skill, embedding-based retrieval first identifies candidate related skills. Cross-instance replay and an LLM-based mechanism check determine whether these skills transfer across cases and share a common underlying mechanism. Candidates that pass both checks are abstracted into a higher-level skill and committed only if it preserves the validated behavior of all constituent skills. Experiments on RuleArena, OpenExempt and KOR-Bench demonstrate that SkillCommit consistently improves agent performance across diverse domains. Moreover, the learned skills transfer across model scales and families, enabling cross-model experience transfer.

Cheng Kar-Shun Robotics Institute (CKSRI.title: GeoCloak: An Agentic Framework for Semantics-Preserving Geolocation Privacy via Peripheral Clue Manipulation
Cheng Kar-Shun Robotics Institute (CKSRI.authors_text: Yixin Wu, Mingjie Li, Yun Shen, Michael Backes, Yang Zhang
Cheng Kar-Shun Robotics Institute (CKSRI.summary: GeoCloak is a framework that enhances geolocation privacy by manipulating peripheral clues in images while preserving semantic content, significantly reducing location inference accuracy.
Cheng Kar-Shun Robotics Institute (CKSRI.debug_abstract: The rapid advancement of large vision language models (LVLMs) has made geolocation inference from images highly accurate and accessible. This poses serious privacy risks: a passive adversary with black-box LVLM access can infer a user's location from a single photo with no metadata. Existing protection methods rely almost exclusively on adversarial perturbation, which introduces perceptible visual artifacts and utility degradation. We identify the visual-geolocation asymmetry: geolocation-decisive clues, such as street signs, tend to be visually peripheral but dominate location inference. Exploiting this asymmetry, we propose GeoCloak, an agentic framework for semantics-preserving geolocation privacy protection. It acts as a clue-aware planner that analyzes each image to identify geolocation-relevant clues, dispatches targeted semantic edits to directly suppress peripheral clues, and autonomously configures adversarial perturbation to further suppress residual geolocation features, all under iterative utility-aware feedback. We evaluate GeoCloak on four diverse datasets spanning 108 countries and 576 cities against five LVLMs and three inference methods. GeoCloak reduces overall city-level accuracy from 41.2% to 9.9%, approximately half of the best-performing baseline, while achieving substantially superior utility preservation both qualitatively and quantitatively. We hope this work takes a meaningful step toward practical, semantics-preserving geolocation privacy protection, giving users greater control over the location information inadvertently embedded in their shared images.

Cheng Kar-Shun Robotics Institute (CKSRI.title: Refine Actions If Needed: Adaptive Action Chunk Refinement for Robot Manipulation
Cheng Kar-Shun Robotics Institute (CKSRI.authors_text: Hanlin Liu, Zichen Zhou, Jiacheng Zhang, Liuyuan Na, Jin Jin
Cheng Kar-Shun Robotics Institute (CKSRI.summary: RAIN is a framework that adaptively refines robot manipulation actions by predicting error levels, enhancing task success while minimizing inference latency.
Cheng Kar-Shun Robotics Institute (CKSRI.debug_abstract: Computationally lightweight manipulation policies predict executable actions with low inference latency, but prediction errors can limit task success. Iterative generative policies can achieve higher task success rates, but repeated network evaluations increase inference latency. Refining action proposals from computationally lightweight policies can combine these strengths, but the amount of refinement needed varies across states. We introduce RAIN (Refine Actions If Needed), a framework that predicts action errors at different refinement levels to decide whether and how much to refine each executable proposal, before performing any refinement. We train an ensemble to predict these errors by comparing action proposals and their refined versions with expert actions from offline demonstrations, without requiring explicit labels of refinement needs. Calibration balances uncertainty, computation, and temporal consistency. We evaluate RAIN on eight ManiSkill tasks and four real-robot tasks. In simulation, our policy achieves 66.6% success, approaching the best evaluated diffusion-policy success rate with 5.71 times lower policy latency. On the real robot, success increases from 55.0% with Action Chunking with Transformers (ACT) to 72.5%, with comparable average successful completion time. Matched controls show that dynamic routing maintains the strongest observed fixed-refinement success level with 26.6% fewer refiner evaluations. Project page: https://rain-policy.github.io/.

Cheng Kar-Shun Robotics Institute (CKSRI.title: Interlock: From Local Correctness to Task Completion in Long-Horizon Agents
Cheng Kar-Shun Robotics Institute (CKSRI.authors_text: Linji Hao, Yanji He, Zihan Wang, Hansi Yang, Jiayuan Zhang
Cheng Kar-Shun Robotics Institute (CKSRI.summary: The Interlock framework enhances long-horizon task completion in agents by using a typed completion graph to maintain relationships among tasks, improving performance metrics across various benchmarks.
Cheng Kar-Shun Robotics Institute (CKSRI.debug_abstract: Large language model agents increasingly undertake long-horizon tasks in complex environments characterized by fragmented evidence, partially completed states, and dependencies across resources and artifacts. Existing agents may satisfy individual requirements while failing to maintain these relationships, producing locally correct but incomplete outcomes. These failures arise because task completion depends on relationships among environmental evidence, consequential decisions, and required effects. To address this completion gap, we propose Interlock, a framework for task synthesis that represents each task as a typed completion graph. Grounding edges connect public evidence to decisions, coupling hyperedges impose joint constraints across components, and realization edges connect decisions to all required downstream effects. Interlock compiles this graph into a resettable workspace, a public request, and an evaluation rubric. A source-coverage review checks whether the original requirements survive generation, while a public-input review checks whether the rubric is supported by the materials available to the solver. An agent-as-judge inspects execution artifacts and runs verification scripts, retaining trajectories judged to satisfy all mandatory requirements. To evaluate training utility, we fine-tune two Qwen3.6 backbones on their own accepted trajectories. Across the two backbones, training improves AutomationBench task pass rates by 4.00-4.50 percentage points, JobBench weighted scores by 3.20-6.64 points, and Harvey LAB criterion pass rates by 3.89-4.16 percentage points. These results demonstrate the training utility of the synthesized experience across external task environments.

Cheng Kar-Shun Robotics Institute (CKSRI.title: GAE: Learning a Geometry-Native Latent Space for 3D-Consistent World Generation
Cheng Kar-Shun Robotics Institute (CKSRI.authors_text: Jiahao Lu, Minghao Yin, Wenbo Hu, Hengyu Liu, Wang Zhao
Cheng Kar-Shun Robotics Institute (CKSRI.summary: The GAE introduces a geometry-native latent space enhancing 3D-consistent world generation, improving visual quality and coherence by reparameterizing features for diverse tasks.
Cheng Kar-Shun Robotics Institute (CKSRI.debug_abstract: We present a compact geometry-native latent space as a shared foundation for perception and generation. Visual generators can produce photorealistic frames without preserving a consistent 3D scene. We argue that this is not only a modeling problem but also a representation problem: generators typically evolve appearance-centric latents, while perception models recover geometry in a semantically rich space that encodes cross-view structure. Rather than adding geometry as another output, we reparameterize a geometry foundation model's features into a compact latent space for generation. We realize this shift with the geometry-native autoencoder (GAE), whose latent is jointly decodable to appearance, depth, cameras, and point maps. With this state, a standard conditional flow supports diverse generation tasks. In controlled comparisons that hold the generator and training protocol fixed, replacing the latent with GAE improves both visual quality and independently measured 3D coherence: FVD falls by $12.7\%$ and $23.1\%$ on RealEstate10K and DL3DV, and camera-trajectory error is halved on RealEstate10K. Together, these results show that the latent space is central to geometry-consistent generation and can serve as a shared interface between perception and generation.

Cheng Kar-Shun Robotics Institute (CKSRI.title: Synergistic Vision-Language Reinforcement Enables Scalable On-Demand Analysis across Diverse Clinical Tasks
Cheng Kar-Shun Robotics Institute (CKSRI.authors_text: Haonan Wang, Jiaji Mao, Lehan Wang, Qixiang Zhang, Marawan Elbatel
Cheng Kar-Shun Robotics Institute (CKSRI.summary: SyRe is a vision-language reinforcement model that enhances tumor and organ segmentation in oncology through diverse prompts and extensive training data, achieving high accuracy and generalization.
Cheng Kar-Shun Robotics Institute (CKSRI.debug_abstract: Accurate segmentation of tumors and organs-at-risk is essential for oncology but remains time-consuming and expertise-intensive. Existing AI systems often require manual spatial prompts or task-specific retraining, while generic class labels provide limited guidance for heterogeneous disease targets. Here we present SyRe, a text-prompted segmentation foundation model based on Synergistic vision-language Reinforcement, which strengthens bidirectional interaction between visual and linguistic representations. We introduce Color Region Description (CRD) to generate region-level semantic supervision and construct SyReData, comprising 20 million image-mask-description triplets across 9 modalities and 229 segmentation tasks. Training with diversified prompt formats enables single-target, multi-target and open-ended segmentation, together with invalid-prompt rejection. SyRe achieves accurate segmentation across diverse clinical scenarios, with strong gains on disease-related targets. Evaluation on 28 unseen external datasets, including 17 cancer types, 3 non-cancer diseases and multinational in-house cohorts, demonstrates generalization under distribution shift. Beyond spatial overlap, SyRe-generated masks preserve quantitative pathology information. Across five retrospective tumor imaging cohorts spanning CT and MRI, radiomics derived from these masks stratify survival and improve prognostic modeling over clinical baselines. Clinician-in-the-loop refinement further supports case-level correction. These results establish SyRe as a generalizable framework for scalable quantitative oncology analysis and clinician-guided segmentation.

Cheng Kar-Shun Robotics Institute (CKSRI.title: ReEnvision: Future-Guided Selective Action Repair for Long-Horizon Manipulation
Cheng Kar-Shun Robotics Institute (CKSRI.authors_text: Xiyin Zeng, Xuewei Huang, Yi Lu, Weihao Yuan, Hao Wang
Cheng Kar-Shun Robotics Institute (CKSRI.summary: ReEnvision introduces a future-guided selective action repair framework for long-horizon robotic manipulation, enhancing action success rates by preserving valid actions amid execution deviations.
Cheng Kar-Shun Robotics Institute (CKSRI.debug_abstract: Long-horizon robotic manipulation requires robust execution over sequences of interdependent actions. Existing methods typically handle execution deviations by replanning the remaining action chunk or correcting actions step by step as new observations arrive. However, a local deviation may affect only a few actions under distribution shift, yet replanning regenerates the entire chunk from an unfamiliar state, potentially introducing errors into otherwise valid actions. Step-wise correction may react too late, as it does not explicitly anticipate how the deviation affects subsequent actions. We propose ReEnvision, a future-guided selective action repair framework that updates a joint future-action belief using execution feedback. It then learns how the resulting belief revision affects each unexecuted action. The resulting belief revision enables selective repair of only the affected actions within a cached action chunk, preserving valid actions and reserving full replanning for severe deviations. On CALVIN, L-CALVIN, and RLBench, ReEnvision achieves 86.6% 5-step success, improves 10-step success from 56% to 63%, and reaches an average success rate of 88.8%, respectively. On five real-world manipulation tasks, it achieves an average success rate of 82.8%. Controlled repair experiments further demonstrate the benefits of localizing affected actions and preserving valid ones during execution.

Cheng Kar-Shun Robotics Institute (CKSRI.title: AVA-Encoder: Towards Agent-Native Video Representation Learning
Cheng Kar-Shun Robotics Institute (CKSRI.authors_text: Chuyue Li, Jinpeng Yu, Haozhe Wang, Tian Xueyun, Zhijing Zhang
Cheng Kar-Shun Robotics Institute (CKSRI.summary: The AVA-Encoder transforms finished films into agent-native representations via a Film Knowledge Graph, enhancing video creation quality and enabling improved editing and downstream applications.
Cheng Kar-Shun Robotics Institute (CKSRI.debug_abstract: Agentic video creation systems remain far from cinematic-grade quality: their underlying models struggle to plan how story, characters, visuals, and sound fit together, and high-quality creation trajectories to learn such planning abilities are scarce. Finished human films embody this knowledge, but in a tightly coupled audiovisual form that agents cannot directly read or manipulate. We propose the Agentic Video Auto-Encoder (AVA-Encoder), which works backward from finished films, turning them into agent-native representations with reconstruction itself as supervision. It encodes a film into a Film Knowledge Graph (Film KG) of structured-text nodes, typed dependency edges, and linked multimodal assets, then regenerates the film from this graph with a fixed decoder. Reconstruction residuals are distilled into textual gradients that drive dual-loop self-evolution: an outer loop learns a shared encoding policy across videos, and an inner loop refines each video's Film KG at test time. AVA-Encoder improves reconstruction fidelity by 20.7 percentage points over the strongest baseline; its learned policy outperforms a finely human-tuned policy with over 70 percent fewer system-prompt tokens; and Film KGs support coordinated editing and improve all tested downstream creation systems. We release the framework, a reconstruction benchmark, and a Film KG dataset.

Jun MA老师实验室.title: Hindsight-Privileged RLVR: Single-Rollout Token Credit Without Group Sampling
Jun MA老师实验室.authors_text: Wei Chen, Yubing Wu, Zhou Xu, Haoyue Zhang, Delu Zeng
Jun MA老师实验室.summary: Hindsight-Privileged RLVR (HP-RLVR) improves token credit assignment in RLVR by using single-rollout updates based on future outcomes, outperforming GRPO in efficiency and maintaining accuracy.
Jun MA老师实验室.debug_abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) trains language models from checked task outcomes, but assigning a terminal reward to individual reasoning tokens or actions remains difficult. Group-relative methods such as Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) sample several attempts per prompt, but lose their reward-based learning signal when all attempts receive the same outcome. We propose Hindsight-Privileged RLVR (HP-RLVR), a single-rollout method that turns a completed trajectory's own future into token-level update weights. The generating policy snapshot scores each eligible token under its causal history and under a hindsight context containing the realized future and verifier feedback. A normalized Jensen--Shannon divergence between the two views weights the reward relative to a historical baseline, yielding bounded token credit for both successful and failed attempts, with no reference solution or learned critic. In paired Qwen3-8B runs over a shared $100$-step schedule, HP-RLVR trains $1.21\times$, $1.46\times$, and $2.30\times$ faster than GRPO on mathematics, code generation, and ALFWorld, using one eighth the rollouts per prompt. Accuracy is comparable overall, with HP-RLVR ahead on mathematics at all three sizes and GRPO ahead on code and ALFWorld. In ALFWorld, $43.2\%$ (4B) and $49.0\%$ (8B) of GRPO's gradient-norm records are zero, versus none for HP-RLVR.

Jun MA老师实验室.title: SkillCommit: Evolving Agent Skills through Behaviorally Validated Scope Expansion
Jun MA老师实验室.summary: SkillCommit is an online framework that evolves agent skills by preserving instance-specific experiences and hierarchically abstracting behaviorally validated strategies to enhance performance.
Jun MA老师实验室.debug_abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents can continually improve without parameter updates by converting historical experience into reusable procedural knowledge. However, existing methods often consolidate experience based on semantic similarity or LLM judgments, which may merge superficially related but behaviorally incompatible strategies and thereby degrade performance. To address the issue, we propose SkillCommit, an online skill evolution framework that continuously transforms experience into a hierarchical library of reusable skills. Rather than generalizing from individual experiences immediately, SkillCommit first preserves each experience as an instance-specific patch, retaining its locally validated behavior. As patches accumulate, SkillCommit abstracts those sharing a common behavioral mechanism into higher-level skills. Specifically, for each incoming skill, embedding-based retrieval first identifies candidate related skills. Cross-instance replay and an LLM-based mechanism check determine whether these skills transfer across cases and share a common underlying mechanism. Candidates that pass both checks are abstracted into a higher-level skill and committed only if it preserves the validated behavior of all constituent skills. Experiments on RuleArena, OpenExempt and KOR-Bench demonstrate that SkillCommit consistently improves agent performance across diverse domains. Moreover, the learned skills transfer across model scales and families, enabling cross-model experience transfer.

Jun MA老师实验室.title: GeoCloak: An Agentic Framework for Semantics-Preserving Geolocation Privacy via Peripheral Clue Manipulation
Jun MA老师实验室.authors_text: Yixin Wu, Mingjie Li, Yun Shen, Michael Backes, Yang Zhang
Jun MA老师实验室.summary: GeoCloak is a framework that enhances geolocation privacy by manipulating peripheral clues in images while preserving semantic content, significantly reducing location inference accuracy.
Jun MA老师实验室.debug_abstract: The rapid advancement of large vision language models (LVLMs) has made geolocation inference from images highly accurate and accessible.
