We train an ensemble to predict these errors by comparing action proposals and their refined versions with expert actions from offline demonstrations, without requiring explicit labels of refinement needs. Calibration balances uncertainty, computation, and temporal consistency. We evaluate RAIN on eight ManiSkill tasks and four real-robot tasks. In simulation, our policy achieves 66.6% success, approaching the best evaluated diffusion-policy success rate with 5.71 times lower policy latency. On the real robot, success increases from 55.0% with Action Chunking with Transformers (ACT) to 72.5%, with comparable average successful completion time. Matched controls show that dynamic routing maintains the strongest observed fixed-refinement success level with 26.6% fewer refiner evaluations. Project page: https://rain-policy.github.io/.

IWIN-FINS实验室.title: Coordi-pi: Coordination-Aware Dual-Hand Action Representation for Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation
IWIN-FINS实验室.authors_text: Yiming Meng, Yanming Shao, Weijie Shen, Kunyang Lin, Jiayu Sun
IWIN-FINS实验室.summary: Coordi-$\pi$ introduces a structured action representation for bimanual manipulation, enhancing performance significantly by explicitly encoding hand identity and temporal synchronization.
IWIN-FINS实验室.debug_abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have shown strong potential for general-purpose robotic manipulation, but extending them to bimanual dexterous manipulation introduces a high-dimensional and structured action space. Existing bimanual VLA policies commonly concatenate right- and left-side arm--hand actions at each control timestep, leaving cross-hand interactions implicit within a single action vector. We introduce Coordi-$π$, a structured action representation for bimanual dexterous manipulation. Coordi-$π$ represents the right- and left-side arm--hand actions as individual action tokens and organizes them into an interleaved sequence, explicitly exposing the two sides within the action sequence. To explicitly encode hand identity and temporal synchronization in this interleaved representation, a learnable hand-identity embedding distinguishes the two sides, while sequence--control-timestep factorized rotary positional encoding (RoPE) separates sequence position from control timestep, allowing actions at the same control timestep to share a temporal coordinate while retaining distinct sequence positions. Across all five bimanual dexterous manipulation tasks in DexJoCo, Coordi-$π$ achieves state-of-the-art performance under both \textit{rand-obj} and \textit{rand-full}, improving the average success rate over $π_{0.5}$ from 31.9\% to 51.3\% and from 18.3\% to 32.3\%, respectively. Coordi-$π$ also consistently outperforms $π_{0.5}$ across four real-world bimanual dexterous manipulation tasks.

IWIN-FINS实验室.title: Data-Free Continual Learning for World Action Model with Rectified Generative Replay
IWIN-FINS实验室.authors_text: Kaipeng Fang, Hangxu Liu, Chaojian Shi, Yunsong Zhou, Hongzi Zhu
IWIN-FINS实验室.summary: The paper presents R²-WAM, a method enabling data-free continual learning in world action models by autoregressively regenerating and rectifying past task rollouts to reduce forgetting.
IWIN-FINS实验室.debug_abstract: World action models (WAMs) built on pretrained video generation models adapt quickly to new robotic tasks, but they forget previously learned tasks under sequential fine-tuning. Experience replay (ER) mitigates such forgetting by rehearsing data of previous tasks, yet this data is often unavailable in robotics, where a policy is deployed as weights only and its training data is not shared along with it. In this work, we ask whether a WAM can achieve data-free continual learning by regenerating its own past. Our key observation is that a WAM can indeed autoregressively regenerate complete rollouts of previously learned tasks and replay them to mitigate forgetting. However, replaying such raw rollouts still lags far behind replaying real data, which we attribute to two issues. First, the WAM is unable to recognize task completion and keeps generating purposeless motion after the task is done. Second, under open-loop generation, the generated actions gradually drift away from the generated observations. To address both issues, we present rectified generative replay (R$^2$-WAM), which truncates generated rollouts at task completion with an agentic evaluator and filters out rollouts whose actions are physically inconsistent with the observations. On the four LIBERO suites and five real-world tasks, R$^2$-WAM reduces forgetting by over 90% relative to sequential fine-tuning and nearly matches ER without accessing any data from previous tasks. Our analysis further reveals that forgetting in WAMs concentrates in inverse dynamics modeling: a forgotten WAM still produces visually plausible observations of previous tasks while its generated actions fail. Project page: https://kaipengfang.github.io/r2-wam/

IWIN-FINS实验室.title: DexBioLab: Benchmarking Dexterous Manipulation with Dynamic Experimental Phenomena in Realistic Laboratories
IWIN-FINS实验室.authors_text: Xuanye Wu, Yue Shi, Yongcan Yang, Yiqun Wang, Zhaoqi Wan
IWIN-FINS实验室.summary: DexBioLab introduces a benchmark for evaluating robotic dexterous manipulation in realistic biological labs, incorporating dynamic phenomena and advanced simulation techniques across diverse tasks and robot embodiments.
IWIN-FINS实验室.debug_abstract: Automating biological laboratories requires robots to perform dexterous tool interactions under realistic visual conditions while handling dynamic experimental phenomena, presenting significant challenges for robotic manipulation. To enable systematic evaluation under these conditions, we introduce DexBioLab, a simulation benchmark and framework for dexterous manipulation in realistic biological laboratory environments. DexBioLab comprises 14 tasks across 4 robot embodiments, spanning functional tool use, precision manipulation, language-conditioned visual grounding, and instrument operation. We introduce controllable dynamic experimental phenomena, including flames, vapor, and bubbles, to capture the evolving visual conditions of laboratory procedures. To further enhance environmental realism, we develop a hybrid rendering pipeline that integrates interactive simulated foreground objects with Gaussian-splatting backgrounds reconstructed from 6 real laboratory scenes. For efficient large-scale data generation and evaluation, we further build a parallel simulation framework on top of mjlab, proposing Parallel Finite-State Machine (PFSM) and integrating batched rendering with decoupled trajectory replay for demonstration generation and model-independent closed-loop policy evaluation. Our evaluation reveals substantial variation in policy performance across tasks, exposing distinct strengths and weaknesses of current manipulation policies. Real-world experiments further demonstrate a reduced sim-to-real gap, supporting the validity of AutoBio+ for realistic manipulation evaluation. Supplementary materials are available at https://cumulusalpha.github.io/DexBioLabWebPage.

IWIN-FINS实验室.title: OmniHOI: Dexterous Hand-Object Interaction from Monocular Human Video
IWIN-FINS实验室.authors_text: Ting Mao, Yanming Shao, Ziheng Wang, Haoyu Liu, Yiqun Wang
IWIN-FINS实验室.summary: OmniHOI is a novel pipeline that converts monocular videos of hand-object interactions into accurate trajectories for dexterous robots, achieving significantly improved success rates over prior methods.
IWIN-FINS实验室.debug_abstract: Monocular videos of human manipulation provide abundant dexterous demonstrations, yet reconstructing hand-object interaction from a single view and transferring it to robot hands remain difficult, limiting their direct use for robot execution. Prior methods either require task-specific RL training, limiting scalability, or assume clean motion-capture trajectories and thus cannot operate directly on video. We present OmniHOI, a pipeline that turns an RGB video of hand-object interaction into an interaction-faithful trajectory on dexterous hands. The key idea is to enforce physical consistency using the evidence available at each stage: image evidence during reconstruction, contact geometry during retargeting, and dynamics during physics-in-the-loop refinement. Each stage optimizes the corresponding representation directly, correcting errors before they propagate downstream or must be absorbed by a learned policy. Across 150 motion-capture trajectories transferred to each of five dexterous hands with 6 to 22 DoF, we achieve 39-89% success, compared with at most 31% for prior transfer methods. On 60 monocular video clips, we achieve 53% success, compared with 28% for the best prior video-to-robot pipeline. Its trajectories also execute on a real bimanual robot across diverse tasks.

IWIN-FINS实验室.title: TGPO: Trace-Guided Policy Optimization for Robot Task Planning via Verifiable Subgoal Generation
IWIN-FINS实验室.authors_text: Zhihong Liu, Yang Li, Renming Huang, Chendong Zeng, Cewu Lu
IWIN-FINS实验室.summary: TGPO introduces a reinforcement learning framework for robot task planning that generates verifiable subgoals from natural language instructions, outperforming existing methods in complex environments.
IWIN-FINS实验室.debug_abstract: Robot task planning in real-world environments requires mapping abstract natural language instructions to executable action sequences under long horizons and complex constraints. While large language models (LLMs) provide strong commonsense reasoning, they often fail to generate reliable and feasible plans. In contrast, symbolic planners ensure feasibility and optimality but require well-specified goals and cannot directly interpret high-level human intent.We formulate robot task planning as learning to generate verifiable subgoals in the Planning Domain Definition Language (PDDL), bridging language understanding and symbolic planning. To address the challenges of sparse and noisy supervision, we propose Trace-Guided Policy Optimization (TGPO), a reinforcement learning framework that improves structured subgoal generation through (i) verifier-grounded rewards, (ii) external correction of intermediate reasoning traces, and (iii) constrained policy updates that incorporate corrected traces into training.We evaluate TGPO on large-scale household planning tasks with long horizons, abstract instructions, and complex constraints. TGPO significantly outperforms prompting-based and reinforcement learning baselines, with the largest gains on abstract tasks. Furthermore, TGPO integrates naturally with symbolic planners and language-conditioned executors, enabling robust long-horizon planning and combinatorial generalization in realistic environments.

IWIN-FINS实验室.title: Schrödinger's Navigator: Imagining an Ensemble of Futures for Zero-Shot Object Navigation
IWIN-FINS实验室.authors_text: Yu He, Da Huang, Zhenyang Liu, Zixiao Gu, Qiang Sun
IWIN-FINS实验室.summary: Schrödinger's Navigator enhances zero-shot object navigation by using a belief-aware framework that imagines multiple 3D futures for robust decision-making in uncertain environments.
IWIN-FINS实验室.debug_abstract: Zero-shot object navigation (ZSON) requires robots to find target objects in unseen environments without task-specific fine-tuning or pre-built maps, a key capability for general-purpose service robots. Yet methods that perform well in simulation often degrade in cluttered real-world scenes with severe occlusion and latent hazards, where large unseen regions make single-scene inference brittle and unsafe. We propose Schrödinger's Navigator, a belief-aware framework that reasons at inference time over multiple trajectory-conditioned imagined 3D futures. Given candidate paths, a trajectory-conditioned 3D world model predicts hypothetical observations and maintains a superposition of plausible scene realizations rather than committing to one map. An adaptive occluder-aware sampler directs imagination to uncertainty-critical regions, while a Future-Aware Value Map (FAVM) aggregates imagined futures for robust, proactive action selection. Experiments in simulation and on a physical Go2 quadruped show that Schrödinger's Navigator outperforms strong ZSON baselines, improving hidden-target discovery and risk-aware waypoint selection in occlusion-heavy navigation scenarios. These results highlight imagined 3D futures as a scalable and generalizable strategy for zero-shot navigation in uncertain real-world environments.

IWIN-FINS实验室.title: Context Value Informed In-Context Reinforcement Learning
IWIN-FINS实验室.authors_text: Wenhao Zhang, Shao Zhang, Xihuai Wang, Yang Li, Ying Wen
IWIN-FINS实验室.summary: The paper introduces Context Value Informed In-Context Reinforcement Learning (CV-ICRL), enhancing stability and performance in test time adaptation by incorporating a context value for lower-variance policy updates.
IWIN-FINS实验室.debug_abstract: In-context reinforcement learning (ICRL) has emerged as an effective paradigm for test time adaptation to unseen tasks without parameter updates. However, existing ICRL methods can exhibit brittle and unstable adaptions, and the mechanisms underlying such adaptions remain poorly understood. We provide a policy-gradient view of ICRL and argue that relying on trajectory-level return feedback can lead to high-variance updates when test time rollout is limited. Motivated by the actor--critic principle, we propose Context Value Informed ICRL (CV-ICRL), which equips the in-context policy with an explicit context value: the expected discounted return conditioned on the current state and accumulated interaction context. CV-ICRL trains a value head and writes its prediction back into the context as a value token, enabling TD-style return targets for lower-variance policy updates. Experiments on the Dark Room, Minigrid, and Procgen testbeds show that CV-ICRL substantially improves the stability of test time adaptation and achieves higher returns across tasks and environments. Code and data are available at https://github.com/Bluixe/CV-ICRL .

IWIN-FINS实验室.title: Model What Matters: Decision-Guided Selective World Modeling for Language Agents
IWIN-FINS实验室.authors_text: Maolin Ran, Minda Chen, Di Huang, Wei Xiong, Fei Huang
IWIN-FINS实验室.summary: DGS-WM enhances language agents' decision-making by selectively modeling relevant observations and adaptively weighting supervision, leading to improved performance in various tasks.
IWIN-FINS实验室.debug_abstract: Reinforcement learning provides a direct mechanism for optimizing task objectives in large language model-driven agents, but task rewards are typically sparse trajectory-level signals that only evaluate task success, without directly supervising action-conditioned environment transitions, leaving the model with limited explicit understanding of action consequences and environment dynamics. Recent work introduces auxiliary supervision through policy and world modeling co-training, yet typically treats complete environmental observations uniformly as world modeling targets, overlooking the varying decision relevance of observation content. We propose DGS-WM (Decision-Guided Selective World Modeling), a decision-guided policy-world modeling co-training approach for language agents. DGS-WM employs a Decision-Guided Observation Selection component that filters observation units with decision value as world modeling targets based on their support for subsequent policy responses, and a Confidence-Adaptive Weighting component that adaptively adjusts supervision strength according to the model's prediction confidence on selected targets. Together, these components form a decision-aware auxiliary world modeling loss, jointly optimized with the RL loss on the same policy model. Across multiple benchmarks covering single-hop/multi-hop question answering and interactive web tasks, DGS-WM achieves consistent improvements under different model scales and RL algorithms, demonstrating more stable and effective performance compared to full-observation world modeling methods.

IWIN-FINS实验室.title: CA-OPD: Confidence-Aware On-Policy Distillation for Structured Visual Prediction
IWIN-FINS实验室.authors_text: Menghao Li, Linjie Mu, Haotian Hu, Yannian Gu, Lujiayi Xue
IWIN-FINS实验室.summary: CA-OPD enhances structured visual prediction by leveraging teacher confidence for adaptive supervision, improving student performance and mitigating compounding errors in autoregressive vision language models.
IWIN-FINS实验室.debug_abstract: Autoregressive vision language models unify heterogeneous perception tasks but are highly susceptible to compounding errors. On-policy distillation (OPD) bridges the training-inference mismatch by training students on their own rollouts. However, unreliable student predictions, especially early in training, can derail the trajectory and degrade the quality of teacher supervision. While recent interleaved distillation methods allow the teacher to verify and replace student tokens, they primarily rely on rigid ranking metrics rather than exact teacher confidence, and they overlook how intervention decisions can inform token-level supervision. To address this, we introduce Confidence-Aware On-Policy Distillation (CA-OPD), a framework that couples reliable rollout construction with adaptive supervision. CA-OPD utilizes teacher confidence to selectively correct unreliable student transitions, gradually transferring rollout control to the student via a strict-to-relaxed schedule. Crucially, CA-OPD aligns knowledge transfer with these intervention decisions: corrected positions receive direct cross-entropy supervision from the teacher's prediction, while retained positions benefit from the teacher's full predictive distribution. Evaluated in a multi-teacher setting for GUI grounding and optical character recognition, CA-OPD substantially improves the Qwen3.5-0.8B baseline across all six target benchmarks, including gains of $9.50$ points on ScreenSpot-Pro and $6.72$ points on OCRBench-v2 English. Controlled studies further show that the gains depend on intervention placement, progressive rollout control, and intervention-aligned supervision, rather than intervention frequency alone.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: ReferFlow: Beyond Final-Target Localization for Complex Referring Expressions
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Tianyi Gao, Han Fang, Xin Wei, Yaoyao Zhong, Zhaoyan Pan
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: ReferFlow introduces trajectory-level referring expression comprehension, enhancing intermediate visual reference grounding through structured region transitions and improved decoding techniques, outperforming existing models.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models have made significant progress in referring expression comprehension (REC), yet most REC benchmarks still focus on final-target localization. Complex queries often involve intermediate visual references with different dependencies on prior grounding, but final-only evaluation leaves this process unexamined. To address this gap, we formulate trajectory-level REC, in which models receive an ordered sequence of grounding steps constructed from a single complex query and localize the target regions associated with each step. We instantiate this setting in ReferFlow-Bench, which characterizes structured region transitions through four trajectory types, namely Refinement, Shift, Reset, and Mixture. Experiments show that current models struggle to consistently ground intermediate visual references across successive steps. We further propose ReferFlow, which decouples interleaved text-latent trajectory generation from coordinate decoding. Specifically, Stateful Region Latent Reasoning represents each target region as an object-indexed state composed of continuous latents, with explicit visual and spatial supervision to preserve region information for subsequent grounding. Trajectory-Aware Parallel Decoding then recovers all coordinate blocks in parallel through four geometry-constrained refinement rounds, with each block conditioned on its corresponding trajectory prefix, thereby reducing within-box sequential dependencies and eliminating cross-box autoregression. We further apply Grounding-Aware GRPO to promote consistent grounding across steps and learn adaptive trajectory generation from complex REC queries. ReferFlow achieves leading performance on general REC benchmarks and ReferFlow-Bench.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: MIRAGE: Metric Inference and Reliability-Aware Gaussian Estimation from Feed-Forward Vision
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Xinzhe Wang, Changjian Jiang, Kaiwen Song, Xudong Li, Kerui Ren
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: MIRAGE integrates feed-forward visual geometry with LiDAR-IMU data for accurate metric pose estimation and high-fidelity reconstruction, outperforming existing vision-only methods.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: Feed-forward 3D priors enable high-quality reconstruction from image streams but often lack reliable metric scale and suffer from long-term trajectory drift. In contrast, LiDAR--inertial estimation provides metrically accurate motion but lacks the image-space consistency needed for high-fidelity reconstruction. We propose $MIRAGE$, which anchors feed-forward visual geometry to LiDAR--IMU metric motion and regulates online pose corrections according to correspondence support and cross-modal agreement, jointly enabling accurate metric pose estimation and high-fidelity Gaussian reconstruction. Experiments on Oxford Spires, M2DGR and INS show that MIRAGE achieves accurate metric trajectory estimation, outperforming COLMAP, a widely used but computationally expensive reference for vision-only benchmarks. Motivated by the scarcity of long-horizon monocular benchmarks for large-scale indoor reconstruction, we further build a multimodal data-collection platform and use MIRAGE to establish accurate 6-DoF reference trajectories for a new vision-only benchmark. We benchmark recent monocular large-scale reconstruction methods on this dataset, providing a systematic evaluation of their performance in long-horizon indoor scenes.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: Holi-Spatial 360: Generative Reconstruction from Sparse Panoramas for Spatial Rendering and Intelligence
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Yuanyuan Gao, Zhirui Liu, Yuning Gong, Yifei Liu, Yifan Zhan
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: Holi-Spatial 360 presents a framework for generating annotated multi-room 3D environments from sparse panoramas, enhancing spatial reasoning in VLMs through improved reconstruction and curation.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: Spatial intelligence requires scalable 3D environments that are both photorealistic and semantically grounded, yet existing indoor datasets are dominated by room-scale captures and costly LiDAR acquisition. Online real-estate platforms offer abundant panoramas of diverse multi-room homes, but sparse viewpoints and texture-poor regions make reconstruction severely under-constrained. We introduce Holi-Spatial 360, a generative reconstruction and data curation framework for converting these panoramas into annotated multi-room 3D environments. Because reconstruction quality bounds subsequent generation, our Correspondence-Guided Geometric Optimization converts feed-forward reconstruction priors into reliable cross-view constraints and builds a coherent 3D Gaussian Splatting representation as 3D spatial memory. Adapted single-image and video priors then restore appearance and complete continuous trajectories while preserving observed content. The reconstructed scenes support arbitrary RGB-D rendering and an automated curation pipeline that combines end-to-end 3D grounding with VLM-based verification. Holi360 contains over 1K multi-room 3DGS scenes, more than 100K instance annotations, and 2M spatial question-answer pairs. We also introduce the Holi360 benchmark to evaluate the spatial understanding of VLMs in real-world, multi-room indoor environments. Experiments demonstrate superior reconstruction and curation quality under sparse panoramic inputs, while fine-tuning VLMs on Holi360 substantially improves spatial reasoning capabilities.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: SERO: Learning from Executable Oracle Continuations for Long-Horizon Agentic Reinforcement Learning
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Dingyi Rong, Yue Shi, Chaofan Ma, Zongrui Wang, Jiezhang Cao
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: SERO enhances long-horizon agentic reinforcement learning by utilizing executable oracle continuations and policy-reachability weighting to improve learning from previously unvisited states.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: Long-horizon agentic RL is constrained by the futures visited by the current policy. When rollouts fail to reach useful behaviors, improved credit assignment cannot provide supervision for states and actions that were never encountered. On-policy distillation (OPD) introduces teacher guidance on policy-induced states, and recent multi-turn variants improve how this guidance is scheduled, replayed, refined, or validated. However, they do not directly use the oracle-controlled future itself as the training trajectory. We introduce \textbf{State-Rooted Executable Rollout Optimization (SERO)}, which augments on-policy agentic RL with executable oracle continuations. SERO restores a state actually reached by the current policy and lets a training-only oracle continue interacting with the real environment, making the downstream observations and oracle actions themselves available for learning. It then applies \textbf{policy-reachability weighting}, which weights each oracle step by the frozen behavior policy's compatibility with the preceding oracle actions. This allows deeper supervision to become effective as the policy becomes more compatible with the oracle branch. The oracle loss is optimized separately from the base RL estimator and no oracle is used at inference time. We evaluate SERO on two challenging interactive-agent benchmarks, ALFWorld and WebShop, using Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct. On ALFWorld, learning the full executable continuation is substantially more effective than supervising only the root oracle action, while policy-reachability weighting further improves out-of-distribution performance.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: When Does Momentum Help in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards?
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Kaifei Wang, Zikang Shan, Liwei Wang, Yinyu Ye, Han Zhong
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: This paper investigates the role of bias-corrected exponential moving average momentum in reinforcement learning, demonstrating that optimal momentum selection enhances performance in policy gradient optimization.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: Momentum is a classical tool for accelerating convex optimization and a standard component of modern large language model training. Yet recent empirical work has questioned the usefulness of first-moment momentum in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR). We study this question through a bandit formulation of RLVR with bias-corrected exponential moving average (EMA) momentum, where the EMA coefficient $β$ controls how quickly the weights on past gradients decay. When policy gradients are evaluated exactly, we prove that increasing $β$ within a range that prevents overshoot strictly accelerates optimization. When gradients are estimated from sampled responses, a positive expected gain can be obscured by sampling fluctuations. We show that as the learning rate $η$ decreases, the expected gain with fixed $β$ vanishes faster than these fluctuations, whereas increasing $β$ to keep $η/(1-β)$ within the safe regime preserves a nonvanishing gain that eventually dominates them. Bandit simulations quantitatively validate these predictions. RLVR experiments on Qwen3-4B-Base using SGD with EMA and AdamW support our principle of choosing larger coefficients in practical LLM post-training. On Qwen2.5-32B with AdamW, simply increasing $β_1$ improves mean validation accuracy by nearly $2$ percentage points over the conventional choice, demonstrating the principle's effectiveness at a larger model scale.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: ObjDream: Guiding Vision-Language-Action Models with Object-Level Understanding and Future State Prediction
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Huailiang Ma, Yuxuan Li, Ziyi Zhao, Xinkai Wang, Mingyu Li
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: ObjDream enhances vision-language-action models by integrating object-level understanding and future state prediction, improving robustness in robotic manipulation across diverse environments.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have emerged as a powerful paradigm for robotic manipulation, enabling robots to generate actions from visual observations and language instructions. However, most existing VLA models still operate on image-level visual representations inherited from pretrained vision-language backbones, while lacking fine-grained object understanding for manipulation. As a result, their robustness can degrade under out-of-distribution object layouts, clutter, and background variations. To address these limitations, we introduce ObjDream, an object-centric VLA framework centered on object-level understanding and future object state prediction. ObjDream uses a spatio-temporal object encoder to organize visual observations into temporal object slots, where persistent object identity and dynamic object state are represented through separate channels. These structured object representations are inserted into the token sequence of the vision-language model (VLM), where identity-guided routing modulates VLM attention to the corresponding object tokens. In addition, an action-conditioned object dynamics module predicts compact future object states relevant to manipulation during training, explicitly supervising object state evolution under robot actions without requiring future prediction at inference. Experiments on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, and RoboTwin 2.0 show that ObjDream improves generalization under diverse distribution shifts and scene perturbations. Real-world robot experiments further demonstrate that ObjDream transfers to physical manipulation settings with novel object arrangements and background changes.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: MorphAct: Robot Policies Morphing with the Worlds They Act In
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Ziyan Liu, Jiting Liu, Weihong Zhong, Wenda Yu, Yeqiu Chen
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: MorphAct introduces a dynamic framework for robot policy adaptation that optimizes performance across diverse environments by adjusting parameters contextually, achieving significant improvements in various tasks.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: Progress toward general intelligence in the physical world requires scaling robot learning across diverse environments and interactions. However, existing robot policies use shared parameters that remain fixed across interaction contexts. When different operations favor competing parameter adjustments, fitting their mixture can leave individual operations insufficiently adapted. Our atomic-task diagnostics reveal competing update directions in both vision-language and action parameters, with source-improving updates increasing loss on other tasks. This motivates MorphAct, a contextual parameterization framework that dynamically adjusts robot policy parameters as interaction contexts change. Two coupled generators produce context-dependent low-rank updates for the vision-language and action modules. Their coupling follows the policy's computational dependency: vision-language updates shape the representations that condition action-side parameter generation. Both generators are trained jointly through the native action objective, without operation labels or expert-adapter targets. MorphAct improves performance across three VLA backbones on LIBERO and Meta-World, with gains of up to 16.30%. In real-world evaluation, it achieves gains of up to 14% over $π_{0.5}$. Ablations support the benefits of contextual parameter generation and representation coupling.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: OmniPoser: Flexible Human Motion Recovery in the Wild with Masked Flow Matching
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: OmniPoser is a versatile framework for real-time 3D human motion recovery from diverse sensor inputs, achieving state-of-the-art performance at over 700 FPS.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: Recovering 3D human motion from sparse wearable sensors is challenging due to the inherent noise, occlusion, and instability of real-world tracking signals. Existing approaches are restricted to fixed sensor configurations and, when built on diffusion models, are computationally prohibitive for real-time deployment. We propose OmniPoser, a universal framework that recovers full-body SMPL motion from a flexible combination of heterogeneous inputs, such as 3D keypoints, sparse IMU rotations, head-mounted 6-DoF poses, or any subset thereof, within a single model. OmniPoser introduces a cross-modal masking mechanism paired with a Masked Conditioning Encoder, enabling one architecture to incorporate diverse sensor configurations through a masked design. A decoupled dual-stream generative backbone generates complete motion via Conditional Flow Matching, requiring only a single ODE integration step at inference. Across three settings and seven benchmarks, including in-the-wild Nymeria and Ego-Exo4D datasets, OmniPoser performs on par with state-of-the-art methods while running at over 700 FPS. The project page is available at https://jamesbridgewater51.github.io/omniposer-eccv/.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: LiFi: LiDAR Generation from Multi-View Images via Geometric and Semantic Collaborative Guidance
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Sizhuo Zhou, Xiaosong Jia, Fanrui Zhang, Qifeng Li, Junjie Li
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: LiFi is a novel framework that generates high-fidelity LiDAR point clouds from multi-view images using geometric and semantic collaborative guidance.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: Generating LiDAR point clouds from multi-view camera images is a valuable task with applications in controllable data synthesis, cross-modal simulation and various perception tasks. However, most existing methods are not specifically designed for this task, and the quality of their generated LiDAR remains limited. Moreover, these methods typically focus only on semantic cues in images or generate LiDAR from a monocular camera image. In this work, we introduce LiFi (LiDAR From images), a dedicated framework for generating visually and geometrically aligned LiDAR scenes from multi-view camera images. LiFi guides the latent diffusion process through two complementary branches: geometry and semantics. The geometry branch constructs scene features from images through a reverse sampling algorithm and an uncertainty-aware geometric encoder combined with DepthAnything3, whereas the semantic branch provides high-level semantic representations via a cross-view interaction module. We further introduce a dual-branch balanced classifier-free guidance (CFG) strategy, which enhances the model's conditional generation capability while preserving the independent learning and collaborative controllability of the two branches. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LiFi outperforms state-of-the-art methods in generating high-fidelity LiDAR scenes. The code will be publicly available at: https://github.com/szzhou88/LiFi.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: Refine Actions If Needed: Adaptive Action Chunk Refinement for Robot Manipulation
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Hanlin Liu, Zichen Zhou, Jiacheng Zhang, Liuyuan Na, Jin Jin
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: RAIN is a framework that adaptively refines robot manipulation actions by predicting error levels, enhancing task success while minimizing inference latency.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: Computationally lightweight manipulation policies predict executable actions with low inference latency, but prediction errors can limit task success. Iterative generative policies can achieve higher task success rates, but repeated network evaluations increase inference latency. Refining action proposals from computationally lightweight policies can combine these strengths, but the amount of refinement needed varies across states. We introduce RAIN (Refine Actions If Needed), a framework that predicts action errors at different refinement levels to decide whether and how much to refine each executable proposal, before performing any refinement. We train an ensemble to predict these errors by comparing action proposals and their refined versions with expert actions from offline demonstrations, without requiring explicit labels of refinement needs. Calibration balances uncertainty, computation, and temporal consistency. We evaluate RAIN on eight ManiSkill tasks and four real-robot tasks. In simulation, our policy achieves 66.6% success, approaching the best evaluated diffusion-policy success rate with 5.71 times lower policy latency. On the real robot, success increases from 55.0% with Action Chunking with Transformers (ACT) to 72.5%, with comparable average successful completion time. Matched controls show that dynamic routing maintains the strongest observed fixed-refinement success level with 26.6% fewer refiner evaluations. Project page: https://rain-policy.github.io/.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: Coordi-pi: Coordination-Aware Dual-Hand Action Representation for Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Yiming Meng, Yanming Shao, Weijie Shen, Kunyang Lin, Jiayu Sun
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: Coordi-$\pi$ introduces a structured action representation for bimanual manipulation, enhancing performance significantly by explicitly encoding hand identity and temporal synchronization.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have shown strong potential for general-purpose robotic manipulation, but extending them to bimanual dexterous manipulation introduces a high-dimensional and structured action space. Existing bimanual VLA policies commonly concatenate right- and left-side arm--hand actions at each control timestep, leaving cross-hand interactions implicit within a single action vector. We introduce Coordi-$π$, a structured action representation for bimanual dexterous manipulation. Coordi-$π$ represents the right- and left-side arm--hand actions as individual action tokens and organizes them into an interleaved sequence, explicitly exposing the two sides within the action sequence. To explicitly encode hand identity and temporal synchronization in this interleaved representation, a learnable hand-identity embedding distinguishes the two sides, while sequence--control-timestep factorized rotary positional encoding (RoPE) separates sequence position from control timestep, allowing actions at the same control timestep to share a temporal coordinate while retaining distinct sequence positions. Across all five bimanual dexterous manipulation tasks in DexJoCo, Coordi-$π$ achieves state-of-the-art performance under both \textit{rand-obj} and \textit{rand-full}, improving the average success rate over $π_{0.5}$ from 31.9\% to 51.3\% and from 18.3\% to 32.3\%, respectively. Coordi-$π$ also consistently outperforms $π_{0.5}$ across four real-world bimanual dexterous manipulation tasks.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: Data-Free Continual Learning for World Action Model with Rectified Generative Replay
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Kaipeng Fang, Hangxu Liu, Chaojian Shi, Yunsong Zhou, Hongzi Zhu
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: The paper presents R²-WAM, a method enabling data-free continual learning in world action models by autoregressively regenerating and rectifying past task rollouts to reduce forgetting.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: World action models (WAMs) built on pretrained video generation models adapt quickly to new robotic tasks, but they forget previously learned tasks under sequential fine-tuning. Experience replay (ER) mitigates such forgetting by rehearsing data of previous tasks, yet this data is often unavailable in robotics, where a policy is deployed as weights only and its training data is not shared along with it. In this work, we ask whether a WAM can achieve data-free continual learning by regenerating its own past. Our key observation is that a WAM can indeed autoregressively regenerate complete rollouts of previously learned tasks and replay them to mitigate forgetting. However, replaying such raw rollouts still lags far behind replaying real data, which we attribute to two issues. First, the WAM is unable to recognize task completion and keeps generating purposeless motion after the task is done. Second, under open-loop generation, the generated actions gradually drift away from the generated observations. To address both issues, we present rectified generative replay (R$^2$-WAM), which truncates generated rollouts at task completion with an agentic evaluator and filters out rollouts whose actions are physically inconsistent with the observations. On the four LIBERO suites and five real-world tasks, R$^2$-WAM reduces forgetting by over 90% relative to sequential fine-tuning and nearly matches ER without accessing any data from previous tasks. Our analysis further reveals that forgetting in WAMs concentrates in inverse dynamics modeling: a forgotten WAM still produces visually plausible observations of previous tasks while its generated actions fail. Project page: https://kaipengfang.github.io/r2-wam/

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: DexBioLab: Benchmarking Dexterous Manipulation with Dynamic Experimental Phenomena in Realistic Laboratories
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Xuanye Wu, Yue Shi, Yongcan Yang, Yiqun Wang, Zhaoqi Wan
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: DexBioLab introduces a benchmark for evaluating robotic dexterous manipulation in realistic biological labs, incorporating dynamic phenomena and advanced simulation techniques across diverse tasks and robot embodiments.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: Automating biological laboratories requires robots to perform dexterous tool interactions under realistic visual conditions while handling dynamic experimental phenomena, presenting significant challenges for robotic manipulation. To enable systematic evaluation under these conditions, we introduce DexBioLab, a simulation benchmark and framework for dexterous manipulation in realistic biological laboratory environments. DexBioLab comprises 14 tasks across 4 robot embodiments, spanning functional tool use, precision manipulation, language-conditioned visual grounding, and instrument operation. We introduce controllable dynamic experimental phenomena, including flames, vapor, and bubbles, to capture the evolving visual conditions of laboratory procedures. To further enhance environmental realism, we develop a hybrid rendering pipeline that integrates interactive simulated foreground objects with Gaussian-splatting backgrounds reconstructed from 6 real laboratory scenes. For efficient large-scale data generation and evaluation, we further build a parallel simulation framework on top of mjlab, proposing Parallel Finite-State Machine (PFSM) and integrating batched rendering with decoupled trajectory replay for demonstration generation and model-independent closed-loop policy evaluation. Our evaluation reveals substantial variation in policy performance across tasks, exposing distinct strengths and weaknesses of current manipulation policies. Real-world experiments further demonstrate a reduced sim-to-real gap, supporting the validity of AutoBio+ for realistic manipulation evaluation. Supplementary materials are available at https://cumulusalpha.github.io/DexBioLabWebPage.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: OmniHOI: Dexterous Hand-Object Interaction from Monocular Human Video
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Ting Mao, Yanming Shao, Ziheng Wang, Haoyu Liu, Yiqun Wang
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: OmniHOI is a novel pipeline that converts monocular videos of hand-object interactions into accurate trajectories for dexterous robots, achieving significantly improved success rates over prior methods.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: Monocular videos of human manipulation provide abundant dexterous demonstrations, yet reconstructing hand-object interaction from a single view and transferring it to robot hands remain difficult, limiting their direct use for robot execution. Prior methods either require task-specific RL training, limiting scalability, or assume clean motion-capture trajectories and thus cannot operate directly on video. We present OmniHOI, a pipeline that turns an RGB video of hand-object interaction into an interaction-faithful trajectory on dexterous hands. The key idea is to enforce physical consistency using the evidence available at each stage: image evidence during reconstruction, contact geometry during retargeting, and dynamics during physics-in-the-loop refinement. Each stage optimizes the corresponding representation directly, correcting errors before they propagate downstream or must be absorbed by a learned policy. Across 150 motion-capture trajectories transferred to each of five dexterous hands with 6 to 22 DoF, we achieve 39-89% success, compared with at most 31% for prior transfer methods. On 60 monocular video clips, we achieve 53% success, compared with 28% for the best prior video-to-robot pipeline. Its trajectories also execute on a real bimanual robot across diverse tasks.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: TGPO: Trace-Guided Policy Optimization for Robot Task Planning via Verifiable Subgoal Generation
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Zhihong Liu, Yang Li, Renming Huang, Chendong Zeng, Cewu Lu
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: TGPO introduces a reinforcement learning framework for robot task planning that generates verifiable subgoals from natural language instructions, outperforming existing methods in complex environments.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: Robot task planning in real-world environments requires mapping abstract natural language instructions to executable action sequences under long horizons and complex constraints. While large language models (LLMs) provide strong commonsense reasoning, they often fail to generate reliable and feasible plans. In contrast, symbolic planners ensure feasibility and optimality but require well-specified goals and cannot directly interpret high-level human intent.We formulate robot task planning as learning to generate verifiable subgoals in the Planning Domain Definition Language (PDDL), bridging language understanding and symbolic planning. To address the challenges of sparse and noisy supervision, we propose Trace-Guided Policy Optimization (TGPO), a reinforcement learning framework that improves structured subgoal generation through (i) verifier-grounded rewards, (ii) external correction of intermediate reasoning traces, and (iii) constrained policy updates that incorporate corrected traces into training.We evaluate TGPO on large-scale household planning tasks with long horizons, abstract instructions, and complex constraints. TGPO significantly outperforms prompting-based and reinforcement learning baselines, with the largest gains on abstract tasks. Furthermore, TGPO integrates naturally with symbolic planners and language-conditioned executors, enabling robust long-horizon planning and combinatorial generalization in realistic environments.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: Schrödinger's Navigator: Imagining an Ensemble of Futures for Zero-Shot Object Navigation
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Yu He, Da Huang, Zhenyang Liu, Zixiao Gu, Qiang Sun
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: Schrödinger's Navigator enhances zero-shot object navigation by using a belief-aware framework that imagines multiple 3D futures for robust decision-making in uncertain environments.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: Zero-shot object navigation (ZSON) requires robots to find target objects in unseen environments without task-specific fine-tuning or pre-built maps, a key capability for general-purpose service robots. Yet methods that perform well in simulation often degrade in cluttered real-world scenes with severe occlusion and latent hazards, where large unseen regions make single-scene inference brittle and unsafe. We propose Schrödinger's Navigator, a belief-aware framework that reasons at inference time over multiple trajectory-conditioned imagined 3D futures. Given candidate paths, a trajectory-conditioned 3D world model predicts hypothetical observations and maintains a superposition of plausible scene realizations rather than committing to one map. An adaptive occluder-aware sampler directs imagination to uncertainty-critical regions, while a Future-Aware Value Map (FAVM) aggregates imagined futures for robust, proactive action selection. Experiments in simulation and on a physical Go2 quadruped show that Schrödinger's Navigator outperforms strong ZSON baselines, improving hidden-target discovery and risk-aware waypoint selection in occlusion-heavy navigation scenarios. These results highlight imagined 3D futures as a scalable and generalizable strategy for zero-shot navigation in uncertain real-world environments.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: Context Value Informed In-Context Reinforcement Learning
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Wenhao Zhang, Shao Zhang, Xihuai Wang, Yang Li, Ying Wen
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: The paper introduces Context Value Informed In-Context Reinforcement Learning (CV-ICRL), enhancing stability and performance in test time adaptation by incorporating a context value for lower-variance policy updates.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: In-context reinforcement learning (ICRL) has emerged as an effective paradigm for test time adaptation to unseen tasks without parameter updates. However, existing ICRL methods can exhibit brittle and unstable adaptions, and the mechanisms underlying such adaptions remain poorly understood. We provide a policy-gradient view of ICRL and argue that relying on trajectory-level return feedback can lead to high-variance updates when test time rollout is limited. Motivated by the actor--critic principle, we propose Context Value Informed ICRL (CV-ICRL), which equips the in-context policy with an explicit context value: the expected discounted return conditioned on the current state and accumulated interaction context. CV-ICRL trains a value head and writes its prediction back into the context as a value token, enabling TD-style return targets for lower-variance policy updates. Experiments on the Dark Room, Minigrid, and Procgen testbeds show that CV-ICRL substantially improves the stability of test time adaptation and achieves higher returns across tasks and environments. Code and data are available at https://github.com/Bluixe/CV-ICRL .

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: Model What Matters: Decision-Guided Selective World Modeling for Language Agents
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Maolin Ran, Minda Chen, Di Huang, Wei Xiong, Fei Huang
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: DGS-WM enhances language agents' decision-making by selectively modeling relevant observations and adaptively weighting supervision, leading to improved performance in various tasks.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: Reinforcement learning provides a direct mechanism for optimizing task objectives in large language model-driven agents, but task rewards are typically sparse trajectory-level signals that only evaluate task success, without directly supervising action-conditioned environment transitions, leaving the model with limited explicit understanding of action consequences and environment dynamics. Recent work introduces auxiliary supervision through policy and world modeling co-training, yet typically treats complete environmental observations uniformly as world modeling targets, overlooking the varying decision relevance of observation content. We propose DGS-WM (Decision-Guided Selective World Modeling), a decision-guided policy-world modeling co-training approach for language agents. DGS-WM employs a Decision-Guided Observation Selection component that filters observation units with decision value as world modeling targets based on their support for subsequent policy responses, and a Confidence-Adaptive Weighting component that adaptively adjusts supervision strength according to the model's prediction confidence on selected targets. Together, these components form a decision-aware auxiliary world modeling loss, jointly optimized with the RL loss on the same policy model. Across multiple benchmarks covering single-hop/multi-hop question answering and interactive web tasks, DGS-WM achieves consistent improvements under different model scales and RL algorithms, demonstrating more stable and effective performance compared to full-observation world modeling methods.

智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.title: CA-OPD: Confidence-Aware On-Policy Distillation for Structured Visual Prediction
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.authors_text: Menghao Li, Linjie Mu, Haotian Hu, Yannian Gu, Lujiayi Xue
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.summary: CA-OPD enhances structured visual prediction by leveraging teacher confidence for adaptive supervision, improving student performance and mitigating compounding errors in autoregressive vision language models.
智能机器人与机器视觉(IRMV)实验室.debug_abstract: Autoregressive vision language models unify heterogeneous perception tasks but are highly susceptible to compounding errors. On-policy distillation (OPD) bridges the training-inference mismatch by training students on their own rollouts. However, unreliable student predictions, especially early in training, can derail the trajectory and degrade the quality of teacher supervision. While recent interleaved distillation methods allow the teacher to verify and replace student tokens, they primarily rely on rigid ranking metrics rather than exact teacher confidence, and they overlook how intervention decisions can inform token-level supervision. To address this, we introduce Confidence-Aware On-Policy Distillation (CA-OPD), a framework that couples reliable rollout construction with adaptive supervision. CA-OPD utilizes teacher confidence to selectively correct unreliable student transitions, gradually transferring rollout control to the student via a strict-to-relaxed schedule. Crucially, CA-OPD aligns knowledge transfer with these intervention decisions: corrected positions receive direct cross-entropy supervision from the teacher's prediction, while retained positions benefit from the teacher's full predictive distribution. Evaluated in a multi-teacher setting for GUI grounding and optical character recognition, CA-OPD substantially improves the Qwen3.5-0.8B baseline across all six target benchmarks, including gains of $9.50$ points on ScreenSpot-Pro and $6.72$ points on OCRBench-v2 English. Controlled studies further show that the gains depend on intervention placement, progressive rollout control, and intervention-aligned supervision, rather than intervention frequency alone.

高性能人形技术实验室 (H²T).title: SPARC: Reliable Spatial Annotations from Robot Demonstrations at Scale
高性能人形技术实验室 (H²T).authors_text: Nils Blank, Paul Mattes, Maximilian Xiling Li, Jakub Suliga, Thomas Roth
高性能人形技术实验室 (H²T).summary: SPARC is a risk-aware framework that enhances robot demonstration annotations with reliability scores, improving localization accuracy and sample retention for various robotics applications.
高性能人形技术实验室 (H²T).debug_abstract: This work introduces Spatial Annotations from Robot Demonstrations with Reliability Calibration (SPARC), a risk-aware framework that automatically labels robot demonstrations with structured spatial annotations and assigns each annotation a reliability score. Structured spatial annotations, such as bounding boxes, object trajectories, and manipulation phase labels, benefit a broad range of robotics applications from training grounded robot policies and embodied foundation models to motion planning and hierarchical task composition. Existing automated pipelines generate such annotations at scale but provide no reliable quality signal: detector confidence is poorly calibrated for annotation correctness, forcing a choice between accepting noisy labels or discarding useful samples. In contrast to existing automated pipelines, SPARC leverages the spatio-temporal structure inherent to robot tasks to generate a reliability signal, reducing noisy labels and retaining more useful samples. We further introduce Interaction-Aware Bench (IA-Bench), a benchmark that measures model accuracy in grounding the locations of interacted objects in robot demonstrations. On 1.7k human-annotated demonstrations spanning diverse embodiments and scenarios, SPARC significantly outperforms detection-only baselines in localization accuracy while retaining three times more samples at high-precision operating points. Our experiments demonstrate that models finetuned on our annotations achieve state-of-the-art results on object-grounding and pointing benchmarks among similarly sized models, while remaining competitive on broader spatial-reasoning suites without manually verified or annotated training data. Furthermore, policies trained on SPARC-generated annotations outperform baselines in cluttered, visually ambiguous real-world scenes. Code, data, and models are available at intuitive-robots.github.io/sparc-labeling.

高性能人形技术实验室 (H²T).title: Reinforcement Learning via Fixed-point Flow Matching
高性能人形技术实验室 (H²T).authors_text: Denis Blessing, Onur Celik, Gerhard Neumann
高性能人形技术实验室 (H²T).summary: The paper introduces fixed-point flow matching (FFM), a data-free method for training flow policies in reinforcement learning, enhancing online policy optimization without training data.
高性能人形技术实验室 (H²T).debug_abstract: In maximum entropy and behavior-constrained reinforcement learning (RL), the optimal policy is given by a Boltzmann distribution. Generating samples from this distribution can be challenging, as it is often complex and multimodal. While flow policies trained with flow matching provide a powerful framework for representing such distributions, they traditionally rely on access to training data, which is generally unavailable in online RL. To address this limitation, we propose fixed-point flow matching (FFM), a data-free procedure for training and fine-tuning flow policies in RL. FFM leverages the target flow identity to formulate the actor update as a fixed-point iteration, utilizing a flow-matching-style regression objective where the critic's action gradients serve as regression targets. We show that the optimal policy is a fixed point of this iteration. Through extensive experiments, we demonstrate that FFM effectively fine-tunes pretrained flow policies in the offline-to-online setting and enables efficient and accurate training of flow policies from scratch in online RL. These results establish fixed-point flow matching as a principled approach for learning expressive flow-based policies without requiring training data.

浙江大学.title: Graph-Reweighted Behavior Cloning with Human Interventions for Precise Robotic Manipulation
浙江大学.authors_text: Xiaoman Li, Zhiqiang Yang, Jiayu Hu, Jipeng Kong, Yang Zhang
浙江大学.summary: The paper introduces Graph-Reweighted Behavior Cloning (GR-BC), an offline framework that enhances robotic manipulation by optimizing action selection through a task-conditioned goal-reachability graph, improving success rates without requiring complex models.
浙江大学.debug_abstract: Long-horizon precise manipulation produces mixed-quality data for post-training vision-language-action (VLA) models: even successful demonstrations and intervention-assisted rollouts may contain detours, hesitations, failed attempts, and imperfect recoveries. The key challenge is to identify which action chunks actually advance the task, rather than uniformly cloning or discarding imperfect trajectories. We propose Graph-Reweighted Behavior Cloning (GR-BC), an offline iterative post-training framework that builds a task-conditioned goal-reachability graph over demonstrations and iteratively collected rollouts, including both successful and failed episodes with human interventions. Reverse graph search computes minimal remaining steps to task success within the dataset support, and each action chunk is weighted by how much its execution reduces this potential. This consequence-based weighting reuses recoverable segments from failed trajectories, leverages interventions as recovery paths, and down-weights locally regressive chunks even inside successful trajectories. New rollouts are incorporated by appending them to the graph and rerunning search, without training a reward model, action-conditioned critic, or progress predictor. Across four precise manipulation tasks and three VLA backbones, GR-BC improves single-round supervised fine-tuning and reaches 91% success after a few offline iterations, without trajectory comparisons or progress labels. More details and videos are available at: https://gr-bc.github.io

浙江大学.title: Towards Agentic Robots: Model, Data, Environment, and Harness
浙江大学.authors_text: Chonghan Qin, Dongming Wu, Kaituo Feng, Jiaxu Wang, Xinlei Yu
浙江大学.summary: This paper outlines the evolving concept of agentic robots, categorizing research into four domains while addressing challenges and future directions for enhancing robotic intelligence and adaptability.
浙江大学.debug_abstract: Foundation models are driving a paradigm shift in robotic intelligence, moving beyond low-level action prediction to goal-directed orchestration of data collection, model training, task planning, and real-world execution. We characterize this emerging paradigm as an agentic robots, in which agents reason over human instructions, interact with robotic environments, rectify execution errors autonomously, and dynamically adjust operational strategies. Although this field develops fast, current studies are not well connected. Researchers have no consistent view of how to combine different agentic functions into a complete robot system. This paper provides a unified overview of existing research on agentic robots. We first trace the development from robot policies to agentic systems, covering vision-language-action models, world models, and world-action models. We then clarify the definition and scope of agentic robots and organize existing research into seventeen categories across four functional domains: Model, Data, Environment, and Harness. Across these domains, we examine how agents shape model learning and robot decisions, collect and curate robot data, construct worlds, tasks, and tests for learning and evaluation, and organize capabilities for robot use. Finally, we discuss open challenges and outline directions for future research. Looking forward, we hope this work contributes to a clearer understanding of agentic robots and supports new approaches to making them more capable, reliable, and adaptive.

浙江大学.title: ReferFlow: Beyond Final-Target Localization for Complex Referring Expressions
浙江大学.authors_text: Tianyi Gao, Han Fang, Xin Wei, Yaoyao Zhong, Zhaoyan Pan
浙江大学.summary: ReferFlow introduces trajectory-level referring expression comprehension, enhancing intermediate visual reference grounding through structured region transitions and improved decoding techniques, outperforming existing models.
浙江大学.debug_abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models have made significant progress in referring expression comprehension (REC), yet most REC benchmarks still focus on final-target localization. Complex queries often involve intermediate visual references with different dependencies on prior grounding, but final-only evaluation leaves this process unexamined. To address this gap, we formulate trajectory-level REC, in which models receive an ordered sequence of grounding steps constructed from a single complex query and localize the target regions associated with each step. We instantiate this setting in ReferFlow-Bench, which characterizes structured region transitions through four trajectory types, namely Refinement, Shift, Reset, and Mixture. Experiments show that current models struggle to consistently ground intermediate visual references across successive steps. We further propose ReferFlow, which decouples interleaved text-latent trajectory generation from coordinate decoding. Specifically, Stateful Region Latent Reasoning represents each target region as an object-indexed state composed of continuous latents, with explicit visual and spatial supervision to preserve region information for subsequent grounding. Trajectory-Aware Parallel Decoding then recovers all coordinate blocks in parallel through four geometry-constrained refinement rounds, with each block conditioned on its corresponding trajectory prefix, thereby reducing within-box sequential dependencies and eliminating cross-box autoregression. We further apply Grounding-Aware GRPO to promote consistent grounding across steps and learn adaptive trajectory generation from complex REC queries. ReferFlow achieves leading performance on general REC benchmarks and ReferFlow-Bench.

浙江大学.title: REVEAL: Reverse Engineering Agentic Latents from Frontier-Model Traces
浙江大学.authors_text: Yuetian Du, Meng Wang, Yucheng Wang, Zhangzhe Chen, Wei Wang
浙江大学.summary: The REVEAL framework enables the extraction of reusable local controls from frontier-model trajectories, enhancing smaller agents' performance without requiring model retraining.
浙江大学.debug_abstract: Frontier LLM agents perform complex interactive tasks, but their inference costs motivate transferring their experience to smaller open-source agents. Distillation and latent communication typically require target-model training or access to source-model internals. We study how textual frontier-model trajectories can provide reusable local controls for a frozen agent. Inspired by protocol reverse engineering, we introduce $\textit{Agentic Latents}$, comprising anchored states and dynamic profiles of feedback--response cycles elicited by replay in the target model. Our training-free framework, $\textbf{REVEAL}$ ($\textbf{REV}$erse $\textbf{E}$ngineering $\textbf{A}$gentic $\textbf{L}$atents), uses these profiles and trajectory outcomes to match and select local events from successful and failed rollouts of the same task and source model. Their response-transition contrasts yield a target-specific steering direction, applied before each response. Within-benchmark evaluations on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and Humanity's Last Exam with tools report higher accuracy than unmodified agents across three targets. Representation analyses and behavioral case studies support reusing frontier-model experience as local activation control.

浙江大学.title: SEDM: Selective Self-Evolving Distributed Memory for Agents
浙江大学.authors_text: Yichen Liu, Anna Min, Yinzhi Wang, Yuhang Yao, Yichen Han
浙江大学.summary: SEDM introduces a selective memory framework for agents that optimizes memory sharing and usage, significantly enhancing task success while reducing processing costs.
浙江大学.debug_abstract: Agents in a society can reuse each other's experience, but indiscriminate memory use increases processing cost and can reduce task success. We present SEDM (Selective Self-Evolving Distributed Memory), a framework that selects both what agents share and when recipients use it. On the sender side, SEDM admits memories through paired execution tests, ranks them by relevance and measured utility, and abstracts them for cross-domain reuse. On the recipient side, Calibrated Memory Gating (CMG) predicts success with and without memory in a single forward pass, learning from paired outcomes including ties. It injects memory only when the calibrated success gain outweighs a context-cost penalty. SEDM exceeds the strongest evaluated baseline on LoCoMo open-domain questions by 15.1 F1 points and outperforms G-Memory on FEVER and HotpotQA with 16-32% fewer prompt tokens. In a controlled HotpotQA study, CMG achieves success comparable to always using memory with 18% fewer agent input tokens. Within the full SEDM pipeline on LoCoMo, CMG outperforms both always-use and no-memory policies for two SEDM memories while using 19-31% fewer input tokens than always-use. These results show that selective use can recover value from shared memories that hurt performance when injected indiscriminately.

浙江大学.title: PhySGA: A Physics-Space Grounded Agentic Framework for Generalizable and Interactive 3D Composition
浙江大学.authors_text: Weichen Lyu, Chong Xia, Mingyu Dong, Long Xu, Shengjun Zhang
浙江大学.summary: PhySGA introduces a novel framework for interactive 3D object composition, leveraging agent exploration and physical simulation to enhance precision and adaptability in complex tasks.
浙江大学.debug_abstract: 3D object composition is pivotal to digital content creation and robot simulation, while also serving as a critical testbed for physical intelligence in foundation models. Previous methods either leverage large language models to directly predict object coordinates, or utilize generative diffusion priors to synthesize composite images for visual alignment, both of which rely on static priors in digital spaces. However, these methods consistently struggle with complex compositions such as precise hanging, gravity-driven settling and hidden containment, as these tasks require interactive construction processes involving global planning, fine-grained alignment, and physical simulation. To address these challenges, we propose PhySGA, a Physics-Space Grounded Agentic Framework for 3D composition via agent exploration and physical simulation, enabling the universal interactive assembly of rigid, articulated, and deformable objects. Directly applying vanilla LLMs or VLMs to this task proves insufficient, as current models inherently lack grounded physical understanding and interactive construction experience. To overcome this limitation, we design a collaborative feedforward-feedback architecture: an Assembly Agent focuses on geometric and kinematic reasoning for global step planning and coarse adjustment, while a Critic Agent reasons over contact dynamics for simulator state diagnosis and fine-grained closed-loop correction. Furthermore, Action Routers map semantic planning and analysis onto executable physical primitives within the simulator, while a task-specific Self-Evolving Skill Library distills historical trial-and-error feedback into reusable experiences, boosting success rates and minimizing exploration attempts. Extensive experiments within Isaac Sim demonstrate that PhySGA significantly surpasses existing methods in relation fidelity, physical plausibility, and visual quality.

浙江大学.title: InfiniSplat v2: Analyzing and Improving Feed-Forward 3DGS from Any Views
浙江大学.authors_text: Yongzhen Hu, Hao Yu, Jiawei Wang, Xianming Zeng, Jianyun Xu
浙江大学.summary: InfiniSplat v2 enhances feed-forward Gaussian reconstruction for 3D scenes by decoupling geometry and attributes, achieving state-of-the-art rendering quality across multiple datasets.
浙江大学.debug_abstract: Feed-forward Gaussian reconstruction builds 3D scenes directly from input images for novel view rendering, but learning Gaussian attributes from predicted geometry for high-quality rendering under large viewpoint changes remains challenging. We analyze limitations in Gaussian attribute learning and introduce InfiniSplat v2, which improves rendering quality through architectural and training changes. Our method decouples geometry and attribute prediction with a frozen geometry branch, aligns predicted Gaussians using ground-truth camera poses during training, and adopts large-angle target view supervision. Across six datasets, the feed-forward outputs of the same trained model achieve state-of-the-art mean LPIPS and DISTS among the evaluated methods in both pose-conditioned and pose-free settings. In the pose-conditioned setting, mean LPIPS and DISTS decrease by 25.8% and 32.9%, respectively, compared with the strongest evaluated baselines. We further find that opacity learned with only image reconstruction supervision suppresses geometrically inconsistent points. Project page: https://zju3dv.github.io/InfiniSplat2/

浙江大学.title: Atomic-WAM: Execution-Grounded Atomic-Motion Reasoning for World Action Models
浙江大学.authors_text: Shijun Shi, Zhe Liu, Zhi Hou, Yinan Chen, Tao Zhang
浙江大学.summary: Atomic-WAM integrates task reasoning and action generation through atomic-motion descriptions, enhancing robotic control with execution-grounded learning for improved task success rates.
浙江大学.debug_abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) typically adapt video foundation models to robotic control through joint video and action prediction. However, task-level instructions may leave the next physical interaction underspecified, requiring semantic grounding and state-dependent motion selection. To this end, we introduce Atomic-WAM, an understand-then-execute framework that connects task reasoning to action generation through atomic-motion descriptions. Specifically, a vision-language reasoner describes the next local motion from the task instruction and visual context, guiding a WAM to predict future video and an action chunk. Furthermore, an automatic annotation pipeline curates temporally aligned, contact-enriched supervision from multi-view DROID demonstrations. To make atomic-motion predictions executable by the WAM, we post-train the reasoner with Execution-Grounded GRPO (EG-GRPO). With the WAM fixed, EG-GRPO adapts the reasoner through rewards for motion appropriateness and execution success. Finally, Atomic-WAM achieves 39.6% task success under default instructions and 31.6% under vague instructions in a real-to-sim evaluation on RoboLab. Project page: https://ssj9596.github.io/Atomic-WAM-project

浙江大学.title: Memorizing Who, Knowing How: Benchmarking Personal and Procedural Memory for Persistent Assistants
浙江大学.authors_text: Maosheng Qin, Qi Zhang, Mingxuan Xia, Jinglei Chen, Jiexiang Wang
浙江大学.summary: The paper introduces PraxisMemBench, a benchmark for persistent personal assistants that integrates personal and procedural memory, revealing their interdependence and proposing PraxisMem for improved memory management.
浙江大学.debug_abstract: Memory systems for persistent personal agents must move beyond isolated memories, maintaining both personal memory about whom they serve and procedural memory about how to act. Crucially, in harness-based personal assistance, procedures or skills are inherently user-conditioned: personal context determines which procedures apply, how they are instantiated, and when they should change. Existing benchmarks typically emphasize either personal or procedural memory, leaving their interaction underexplored. We introduce PraxisMemBench, a harness-based benchmark for persistent personal assistance across daily-life and work trajectories, where personal and procedural memory evolve together and later tasks depend on both. Experiments show that maintaining two memory types separately is insufficient, with completion dropping from single-type to interdependent dependencies (84.6% to 77.9%). More broadly, across existing methods, relation-related failures increase from early to late sessions as interaction history grows (59.8% to 72.9%), revealing a continual-maintenance challenge: writing correct memories is not enough if their evolving content and organization cannot be preserved for later retrieval. To address this, we propose PraxisMem, which uses privileged joint-state supervision to internalize the ability to maintain memory content and organization into the memory manager, with location-aware GRPO and dynamic residual-routed OPSD. PraxisMem reaches 40.78% overall Session Success Rate, compared with 20.60% for Claude Code's native memory.

浙江大学.title: OmniHOI: Dexterous Hand-Object Interaction from Monocular Human Video
浙江大学.authors_text: Ting Mao, Yanming Shao, Ziheng Wang, Haoyu Liu, Yiqun Wang
浙江大学.summary: OmniHOI is a novel pipeline that converts monocular videos of hand-object interactions into accurate trajectories for dexterous robots, achieving significantly improved success rates over prior methods.
浙江大学.debug_abstract: Monocular videos of human manipulation provide abundant dexterous demonstrations, yet reconstructing hand-object interaction from a single view and transferring it to robot hands remain difficult, limiting their direct use for robot execution. Prior methods either require task-specific RL training, limiting scalability, or assume clean motion-capture trajectories and thus cannot operate directly on video. We present OmniHOI, a pipeline that turns an RGB video of hand-object interaction into an interaction-faithful trajectory on dexterous hands. The key idea is to enforce physical consistency using the evidence available at each stage: image evidence during reconstruction, contact geometry during retargeting, and dynamics during physics-in-the-loop refinement. Each stage optimizes the corresponding representation directly, correcting errors before they propagate downstream or must be absorbed by a learned policy. Across 150 motion-capture trajectories transferred to each of five dexterous hands with 6 to 22 DoF, we achieve 39-89% success, compared with at most 31% for prior transfer methods. On 60 monocular video clips, we achieve 53% success, compared with 28% for the best prior video-to-robot pipeline. Its trajectories also execute on a real bimanual robot across diverse tasks.

浙江大学.title: VLRLA: Deployment-Time Adaptation of Vision-Language-Action Models through In-Context Reinforcement Learning
浙江大学.authors_text: Diyuan Shi, Yiqi Tang, Hongyin Zhang, You Wu, Donglin Wang
浙江大学.summary: VLRLA enhances vision-language-action models with in-context reinforcement learning for adaptive, deployment-time improvement of robotic manipulation tasks based on accumulated interaction experience.
浙江大学.debug_abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models connect visual perception and language understanding with robot control, providing a foundation for instruction-conditioned manipulation. However, conventional pretrained VLA policies lack a mechanism for gradual adaptation through accumulated interaction experience during deployment. We therefore propose VLRLA, a general framework that equips existing VLA models with \textit{in-context reinforcement learning} capabilities for deployment-time adaptation. Our approach augments a VLA model with a reinforcement learning module that learns from historical observations, actions, rewards, and termination signals. During deployment, the policy gradually refines its action generation and progressively improves task success while keeping model parameters fixed. Our approach is also designed for general applicability and compatibility with diverse learning history construction strategies and model training pipelines. Finally, through extensive experiments, we systematically investigate the learning properties of VLRLA in simulation and demonstrate its ability to adapt to unseen scenarios during real-world deployment.

浙江大学.title: AgentSafeEvo: Adversarial Co-Evolution for LLM Agent Safety
浙江大学.authors_text: Chenxu Wang, Xiaoyu Wen, Han Qi, Ziyuan Zhou, Cheng Jin
浙江大学.summary: AgentSafeEvo is a co-evolutionary reinforcement learning framework enhancing LLM agent safety against adversarial attacks through an attacker-defender game and learnability-guided task weighting.
浙江大学.debug_abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents accomplish complex tasks through multi-turn interactions with external tools.
