人机物智能融合实验室 (HCP).summary: GeoThinker-$F$ is an efficient framework that internalizes spatiotemporal perception in MLLMs, achieving significant inference speedup without relying on external 3D encoders.
人机物智能融合实验室 (HCP).debug_abstract: Existing geometry-aware Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) increasingly rely on external 3D encoders to provide structural priors, but executing these additional encoder paths at inference introduces substantial latency and computational overhead. We propose GeoThinker-$F$, an efficient framework that internalizes spatiotemporal perception by transforming causal MLLM hidden states into predictive latent world representations. Our key insight is that intermediate semantic representations contain sufficient information to predict useful representations of current geometry and future semantics, without requiring an exact reproduction of features from a dedicated 3D encoder. To realize this idea, GeoThinker-$F$ adopts a decoupled two-stage training strategy. In the first stage, the MLLM backbone is frozen while lightweight Latent Frame Prediction (LFP) heads learn from an offline 3D geometry expert and next-frame semantic targets. In the second stage, the external expert is removed, and the model is jointly optimized to generate and selectively integrate its self-predicted priors through a specialized Spatial-Grounded Temporal (SGT) Fusion module. Extensive evaluations show that GeoThinker-$F$ eliminates runtime dependence on external 3D geometry encoders while maintaining competitive performance across diverse spatial intelligence benchmarks. It achieves up to a $3.6\times$ inference speedup, reducing latency from $1.45\,\mathrm{s}$ to $0.40\,\mathrm{s}$ while retaining strong spatial reasoning performance.

人机物智能融合实验室 (HCP).title: Towards Agentic Robots: Model, Data, Environment, and Harness
人机物智能融合实验室 (HCP).authors_text: Chonghan Qin, Dongming Wu, Kaituo Feng, Jiaxu Wang, Xinlei Yu
人机物智能融合实验室 (HCP).summary: This paper outlines the evolving concept of agentic robots, categorizing research into four domains while addressing challenges and future directions for enhancing robotic intelligence and adaptability.
人机物智能融合实验室 (HCP).debug_abstract: Foundation models are driving a paradigm shift in robotic intelligence, moving beyond low-level action prediction to goal-directed orchestration of data collection, model training, task planning, and real-world execution. We characterize this emerging paradigm as an agentic robots, in which agents reason over human instructions, interact with robotic environments, rectify execution errors autonomously, and dynamically adjust operational strategies. Although this field develops fast, current studies are not well connected. Researchers have no consistent view of how to combine different agentic functions into a complete robot system. This paper provides a unified overview of existing research on agentic robots. We first trace the development from robot policies to agentic systems, covering vision-language-action models, world models, and world-action models. We then clarify the definition and scope of agentic robots and organize existing research into seventeen categories across four functional domains: Model, Data, Environment, and Harness. Across these domains, we examine how agents shape model learning and robot decisions, collect and curate robot data, construct worlds, tasks, and tests for learning and evaluation, and organize capabilities for robot use. Finally, we discuss open challenges and outline directions for future research. Looking forward, we hope this work contributes to a clearer understanding of agentic robots and supports new approaches to making them more capable, reliable, and adaptive.

人机物智能融合实验室 (HCP).title: DynThinker: Unifying Static 3D and Dynamic 4D Spatial Reasoning
人机物智能融合实验室 (HCP).authors_text: Qihang Cao, Haoyuan Li, Zihan Guo, Sensen Gao, Zihui Gao
人机物智能融合实验室 (HCP).summary: DynThinker is a novel framework that enhances spatial reasoning by effectively integrating static 3D and dynamic 4D capabilities, outperforming existing models across multiple benchmarks.
人机物智能融合实验室 (HCP).debug_abstract: Achieving general spatial intelligence requires a unified understanding of both static 3D and dynamic 4D. However, we find that existing models struggle to excel at both: 3D post-training can weaken dynamic understanding, while 4D-specialized models often lack strong static 3D reasoning. Our analysis reveals that this spatial--dynamic interference is highly non-uniform across parameter groups, with the balance between static and dynamic capabilities particularly sensitive to changes in late-layer MLPs. To address this interference, we propose DynThinker, a unified framework for jointly strengthening static and dynamic spatial reasoning. Decoupled Exponential Moving Average (D-EMA) applies configurable group-wise averaging to constrain drift in interference-sensitive pretrained parameters while preserving flexibility for capability enhancement. Spatial-Dynamic Fusion (SDF) complements D-EMA by selectively integrating spatial and temporal priors from a dynamic geometry encoder into intermediate VLM representations under semantic guidance. Across ten metrics spanning nine static 3D and dynamic 4D benchmarks, DynThinker achieves the highest average score among all evaluated models. Notably, DynThinker achieves 56.0 on ReVSI, 67.2 on DSR-Bench, and 51.2 and 40.1 under the sample-wise and group-wise evaluation protocols of DSI-Bench, respectively, setting new state-of-the-art results among the compared open-source models across all four evaluations within a unified model.

人机物智能融合实验室 (HCP).title: Synergistic Vision-Language Reinforcement Enables Scalable On-Demand Analysis across Diverse Clinical Tasks
人机物智能融合实验室 (HCP).authors_text: Haonan Wang, Jiaji Mao, Lehan Wang, Qixiang Zhang, Marawan Elbatel
人机物智能融合实验室 (HCP).summary: SyRe is a vision-language reinforcement model that enhances tumor and organ segmentation in oncology through diverse prompts and extensive training data, achieving high accuracy and generalization.
人机物智能融合实验室 (HCP).debug_abstract: Accurate segmentation of tumors and organs-at-risk is essential for oncology but remains time-consuming and expertise-intensive. Existing AI systems often require manual spatial prompts or task-specific retraining, while generic class labels provide limited guidance for heterogeneous disease targets. Here we present SyRe, a text-prompted segmentation foundation model based on Synergistic vision-language Reinforcement, which strengthens bidirectional interaction between visual and linguistic representations. We introduce Color Region Description (CRD) to generate region-level semantic supervision and construct SyReData, comprising 20 million image-mask-description triplets across 9 modalities and 229 segmentation tasks. Training with diversified prompt formats enables single-target, multi-target and open-ended segmentation, together with invalid-prompt rejection. SyRe achieves accurate segmentation across diverse clinical scenarios, with strong gains on disease-related targets. Evaluation on 28 unseen external datasets, including 17 cancer types, 3 non-cancer diseases and multinational in-house cohorts, demonstrates generalization under distribution shift. Beyond spatial overlap, SyRe-generated masks preserve quantitative pathology information. Across five retrospective tumor imaging cohorts spanning CT and MRI, radiomics derived from these masks stratify survival and improve prognostic modeling over clinical baselines. Clinician-in-the-loop refinement further supports case-level correction. These results establish SyRe as a generalizable framework for scalable quantitative oncology analysis and clinician-guided segmentation.

四川大学.title: Why Do VLMs Fail at Remote Physiological Measurement? Rethinking with Physiological Grounding and Numerical Alignment
四川大学.authors_text: Xiao Yang, Zekun Zhang, Yuxuan Fan, Duoxun Tang, Ziyang Liu
四川大学.summary: The paper introduces VITAL, a framework enhancing Vision-Language Models for remote physiological measurement by aligning visual and physiological data while improving numerical accuracy.
四川大学.debug_abstract: Video-based remote physiological measurement (RPM) has broad applications, while Vision-Language Models (VLMs) provide a promising opportunity to enable end-to-end physiological monitoring for future human-aware intelligent systems. However, existing RPM methods rely on task-specific models and cannot be seamlessly integrated with the multimodal understanding and interaction capabilities of VLMs. We revisit RPM with VLMs and provide empirical evidence for two major bottlenecks: generic visual semantic representations fail to preserve fine-grained physiological cues; while discrete token prediction in autoregressive generation is inherently misaligned with continuous numerical measurement. To address these challenges, we propose VITAL (Visual-physiological Token Alignment for Language Models), a visual-physiological token alignment framework for RPM and preserving general vision tasks. VITAL retains the original visual pathway for semantic understanding and introduces an independent physiological pathway to jointly model semantic and physiological information. Moreover, we propose a structured numerical alignment approach to improve the reliability of generative heart rate estimation by enhancing numerical relationship modeling. Extensive experiments show that VITAL improves cross-domain estimation performance on multiple rPPG datasets while preserving the general visual understanding capability of VLMs, demonstrating its effectiveness as a unified visual-physiological model. Code will be released.

四川大学.title: SCVIB: Editable State-Conditioned Visual Instance Binding for Multi-Turn Personalized Localization
四川大学.authors_text: Xiongtai Yang, Ziyan He, Tao Wang
四川大学.summary: The SCVIB framework enhances multi-turn personalized localization by addressing state-dependent visual evidence relevance, achieving notable improvements in target resolution and grounding accuracy.
四川大学.debug_abstract: Stored visual evidence can remain unchanged while its relevance to a current request changes with interaction state. To study this state-dependent source relevance, we introduce SCVIB, a controlled diagnostic benchmark for editable state-conditioned visual instance binding. SCVIB contains 1,050 manually verified support-query pairs and 1,500 multi-turn episodes across five visual domains and four target-state dependencies. Executable state semantics separate target resolution from evidence selection and query-side localization. Direct Qwen3-VL-8B inference achieves 99.53% target-resolution accuracy but 62.00% Joint@0.5, revealing a 37.53-point resolution-localization gap; 563 of its 570 joint failures follow correct target identification. Routing comparisons and fixed-checkpoint support interventions diagnose a post-resolution evidence-utilization bottleneck: successful resolution must be coupled with relevant visual evidence and effective query-side grounding. We introduce TT-VG (Transition-Trace Visual Grounding), a state-conditioned visual grounding framework with an explicit and auditable state-to-evidence-to-grounding path. Target-State Transition Trace (TSTT) executes editable state and selects an auditable support record; Visual Evidence Grounding Adaptation (VEGA) learns support-conditioned grounding from target appearance, boxed support context, and the query. The canonical TT-VG configuration reaches 69.80% Joint@0.5, improving over direct inference by 7.80 points at the combined evidence-utilization and grounding interface. Task adaptation improves the DINOv2 and MASA retrieval baselines to 51.47% and 55.67%, respectively, but both remain substantially below VEGA. These findings highlight state-dependent source selection and evidence utilization as consequential interfaces for interactive multimodal information fusion.

深圳大学.title: STP-GUI: Spatially-Aware Token Pruning for Efficient Web-GUI Agents
深圳大学.authors_text: Shuo Wang, Sifan Zhou, Xiaobo Wang, Tianyu Fu, Chenxu Zhao
深圳大学.summary: STP-GUI introduces a spatially-aware token pruning framework that enhances efficiency in Web-GUI agents by maintaining performance while significantly reducing inference overhead.
深圳大学.debug_abstract: With the rapid development of vision-language models (VLMs), Web-GUI agents have achieved promising performance in interacting with real-world interfaces through screenshot-based grounding. However, high-resolution screenshots and multi-turn histories introduce excessive visual tokens, causing substantial inference overhead. Existing token pruning methods, mainly designed for natural images, often select tokens independently based on importance scores, which can fragment the local visual structures required for recognizing small GUI elements such as buttons, icons, and hyperlinks. In this work, we propose STP-GUI (Spatially-aware Token Pruning for GUI agents), a query-guided token pruning framework that preserves fine-grained instruction-conditioned token scoring while performing spatially coherent window-level selection under aggressive token reduction. A lightweight selector is optimized through policy learning while the VLM backbone remains frozen. Experiments on Online-Mind2Web show that \papername achieves a favorable efficiency-performance tradeoff under low token budgets. At 21% token retention, it preserves 77.7% of full-token performance while reducing inference latency by 31% and FLOPs by 57%. Results on Android in the Wild further suggest that the method transfers to mobile GUI environments.

深圳大学.title: InfiniSplat v2: Analyzing and Improving Feed-Forward 3DGS from Any Views
深圳大学.authors_text: Yongzhen Hu, Hao Yu, Jiawei Wang, Xianming Zeng, Jianyun Xu
深圳大学.summary: InfiniSplat v2 enhances feed-forward Gaussian reconstruction for 3D scenes by decoupling geometry and attributes, achieving state-of-the-art rendering quality across multiple datasets.
深圳大学.debug_abstract: Feed-forward Gaussian reconstruction builds 3D scenes directly from input images for novel view rendering, but learning Gaussian attributes from predicted geometry for high-quality rendering under large viewpoint changes remains challenging. We analyze limitations in Gaussian attribute learning and introduce InfiniSplat v2, which improves rendering quality through architectural and training changes. Our method decouples geometry and attribute prediction with a frozen geometry branch, aligns predicted Gaussians using ground-truth camera poses during training, and adopts large-angle target view supervision. Across six datasets, the feed-forward outputs of the same trained model achieve state-of-the-art mean LPIPS and DISTS among the evaluated methods in both pose-conditioned and pose-free settings. In the pose-conditioned setting, mean LPIPS and DISTS decrease by 25.8% and 32.9%, respectively, compared with the strongest evaluated baselines. We further find that opacity learned with only image reconstruction supervision suppresses geometrically inconsistent points. Project page: https://zju3dv.github.io/InfiniSplat2/

深圳大学.title: LAGO: Language Agents with Reusable Growing Options
深圳大学.authors_text: Yuran Wu, Mengkang Hu, Qionglin Qiu, Fanqing Meng, Qiguang Chen
深圳大学.summary: LAGO introduces reusable language agents as temporally extended options to enhance task decomposition and execution, achieving improved performance on long-horizon tasks without model weight updates.
深圳大学.debug_abstract: Long-horizon tasks expose a weakness of monolithic tool-use loops: one agent must decompose, execute, and verify a task within a single trajectory. We introduce LAGO, which treats specialized language agents as reusable temporally extended options. A meta-agent retrieves options from a persistent library or spawns new ones, dispatches sub-tasks, verifies results, and admits successful novel options. The library grows across tasks without updating model weights. On 500 SWE-bench Verified tasks, frozen Qwen3.5-35B-A3B in both roles resolves 58.6% under single-attempt evaluation with the official Docker evaluator. On a fixed 150-task subset, we re-run mini-SWE-agent, Terminus 2, and LAGO with the same policy, temperature, task IDs, and evaluator; their resolve rates are 49.3%, 57.3%, and 60.3%, respectively. Cross-model experiments provide evidence consistent with a role for decomposition quality. A 50-task component ablation finds four fewer resolved tasks without decomposition, two fewer with shuffled reused content, and six fewer without the library. These results support reusable agent-options as a practical abstraction for task streams, while leaving component-level causality task- and model-dependent.

深圳大学.title: DexCast: Learning Real-World Dexterous Control from Human Videos
深圳大学.authors_text: Zihan Gao, Yuhong Zhang, Mengzhe Wang, Kaisheng Liu, Shengpeng Li
深圳大学.summary: DEXCAST enables learning dexterous robotic hand control from monocular RGB-D videos using a novel perception module, eliminating the need for costly teleoperated demonstrations.
深圳大学.debug_abstract: Recent advances in 3D hand-object interaction (HOI) perception have opened new opportunities for learning dexterous robotic skills from human videos. However, existing dexterous imitation learning methods often rely on costly and manually teleoperated robot demonstrations, requiring substantial human effort. Therefore, we build DEXCAST, a framework that learns dexterous robotic hand control directly from monocular RGB-D videos by leveraging joint HOI reconstructions, without requiring any teleoperation. Furthermore, how to model high-dimensional robotic hand motion and extract temporal context to inform future action generation remains a key challenge. To this end, we propose a DexHand Motion Perception Module (DMPM) to capture inter-joint coordination and temporal dependencies in compact latent representations that condition our diffusion policy. Extensive real-world experiments demonstrate that DEXCAST achieves exceptional performance across diverse dexterous manipulation tasks.

深圳大学.title: FoLD: Force-Informed Learning for Dexterous Articulated Object Manipulation
深圳大学.authors_text: Haowei Shen, Tingai Li, Yumeng Liu, Wenyuan Guang, Xuanze Yang
深圳大学.summary: FoLD is a framework that enhances dexterous robot manipulation by using force guidance from human demonstrations to adaptively retarget hand motions for articulated objects.
深圳大学.debug_abstract: Transferring human demonstrations to dexterous robots remains challenging because differences in hand morphology and contact dynamics often cause retargeted motions to fail at producing the intended object behavior. We present \textbf{FoLD}, a framework for learning dexterous manipulation of articulated objects through explicit force guidance. FoLD compute compensatory force fields from human demonstrations together with the robot's current interaction state, yielding a force prior that promotes the demonstrated object motion. This force prior informs a residual policy that adapts retargeted hand motions to the contact requirements of the task. We evaluate FoLD on a public benchmark for articulated object manipulation, where it consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines across tasks and embodiments. We further validate FoLD on real dexterous robot platforms, demonstrating successful transfer of human manipulation skills to robot execution. Here is the link of our project page: https://gghgghgghgg.github.io/FoLD-project-page/.

上海人工智能实验室.title: DexBioLab: Benchmarking Dexterous Manipulation with Dynamic Experimental Phenomena in Realistic Laboratories
上海人工智能实验室.authors_text: Xuanye Wu, Yue Shi, Yongcan Yang, Yiqun Wang, Zhaoqi Wan
上海人工智能实验室.summary: DexBioLab introduces a benchmark for evaluating robotic dexterous manipulation in realistic biological labs, incorporating dynamic phenomena and advanced simulation techniques across diverse tasks and robot embodiments.
上海人工智能实验室.debug_abstract: Automating biological laboratories requires robots to perform dexterous tool interactions under realistic visual conditions while handling dynamic experimental phenomena, presenting significant challenges for robotic manipulation. To enable systematic evaluation under these conditions, we introduce DexBioLab, a simulation benchmark and framework for dexterous manipulation in realistic biological laboratory environments. DexBioLab comprises 14 tasks across 4 robot embodiments, spanning functional tool use, precision manipulation, language-conditioned visual grounding, and instrument operation. We introduce controllable dynamic experimental phenomena, including flames, vapor, and bubbles, to capture the evolving visual conditions of laboratory procedures. To further enhance environmental realism, we develop a hybrid rendering pipeline that integrates interactive simulated foreground objects with Gaussian-splatting backgrounds reconstructed from 6 real laboratory scenes. For efficient large-scale data generation and evaluation, we further build a parallel simulation framework on top of mjlab, proposing Parallel Finite-State Machine (PFSM) and integrating batched rendering with decoupled trajectory replay for demonstration generation and model-independent closed-loop policy evaluation. Our evaluation reveals substantial variation in policy performance across tasks, exposing distinct strengths and weaknesses of current manipulation policies. Real-world experiments further demonstrate a reduced sim-to-real gap, supporting the validity of AutoBio+ for realistic manipulation evaluation. Supplementary materials are available at https://cumulusalpha.github.io/DexBioLabWebPage.

上海人工智能实验室.title: OmniHOI: Dexterous Hand-Object Interaction from Monocular Human Video
上海人工智能实验室.authors_text: Ting Mao, Yanming Shao, Ziheng Wang, Haoyu Liu, Yiqun Wang
上海人工智能实验室.summary: OmniHOI is a novel pipeline that converts monocular videos of hand-object interactions into accurate trajectories for dexterous robots, achieving significantly improved success rates over prior methods.
上海人工智能实验室.debug_abstract: Monocular videos of human manipulation provide abundant dexterous demonstrations, yet reconstructing hand-object interaction from a single view and transferring it to robot hands remain difficult, limiting their direct use for robot execution. Prior methods either require task-specific RL training, limiting scalability, or assume clean motion-capture trajectories and thus cannot operate directly on video. We present OmniHOI, a pipeline that turns an RGB video of hand-object interaction into an interaction-faithful trajectory on dexterous hands. The key idea is to enforce physical consistency using the evidence available at each stage: image evidence during reconstruction, contact geometry during retargeting, and dynamics during physics-in-the-loop refinement. Each stage optimizes the corresponding representation directly, correcting errors before they propagate downstream or must be absorbed by a learned policy. Across 150 motion-capture trajectories transferred to each of five dexterous hands with 6 to 22 DoF, we achieve 39-89% success, compared with at most 31% for prior transfer methods. On 60 monocular video clips, we achieve 53% success, compared with 28% for the best prior video-to-robot pipeline. Its trajectories also execute on a real bimanual robot across diverse tasks.

多智能体与具身智能研究所.title: DEFlow: Deep Equilibrium Flow Maximum-Entropy Reinforcement Learning
多智能体与具身智能研究所.authors_text: Ruslan Ageev, Huaze Tang, Runqing Miao, Jiarong Li, Wenbo Ding
多智能体与具身智能研究所.summary: DEFlow introduces a deep equilibrium flow policy that enhances sampling efficiency and off-policy training in reinforcement learning, achieving significant performance improvements across various tasks.
多智能体与具身智能研究所.debug_abstract: Expressive flow policies can represent multiple high-value actions, but sampling them with few integration steps while retaining tractable action densities remains challenging. We introduce DEFlow, a deep equilibrium flow policy that replaces explicit Euler sampling with implicit Euler integration and solves all intermediate actions jointly as an equilibrium system. We combine implicit differentiation with a discrete change-of-variables formula for the final-action density, enabling off-policy training within soft actor-critic without backpropagating through solver iterations. DEFlow achieves an average relative improvement of approximately 10% in mean successful coverage over the strongest baseline across four Multi-Goal docking variants. It also achieves the highest mean time-averaged return on four of five manipulation tasks, while remaining broadly competitive across five MuJoCo tasks. These results support implicit flow policies for tasks requiring both diversity and precision, at the cost of additional nonlinear and linear solves. Primary

北京航空航天大学.title: Mitigating Video Hallucinations via Attention-Guided Representation Perturbation
北京航空航天大学.authors_text: Zhixin Cai, Ruoqi Yuan, Xinchen Yang, Zhuofan Chen, Jun Bai
北京航空航天大学.summary: The paper presents ARP-CD, a training-free method that uses attention-guided representation perturbation to reduce hallucinations in Video LLMs by enhancing contrastive decoding effectiveness.
北京航空航天大学.debug_abstract: Video large language models (Video LLMs) often generate responses unsupported by the input video. Contrastive decoding (CD) can mitigate these hallucinations, but its effectiveness depends on how the negative branch weakens visual evidence. Existing methods rely on predefined perturbations or masking guided by question reconstruction, offering limited control over the model's visual reliance during answer generation. We introduce Attention-guided Representation Perturbation for Contrastive Decoding (ARP-CD), a training-free framework for constructing contrastive negatives directly in representation space. ARP-CD uses the attention mass assigned to visual tokens at the answer-prediction position to guide bounded gradient updates of the language model's input visual hidden states. These updates reduce visual attention and produce a negative input, whose predictions are contrasted with those of the original branch throughout generation. Experiments across four Video LLMs and four benchmarks show that ARP-CD outperforms representative training-free baselines in most model--benchmark settings, reducing hallucinations while improving general video understanding. Further analyses show that attention-guided perturbation directions improve negative quality and that the resulting negatives provide effective contrastive references for correcting the original predictions.

北京航空航天大学.title: Dual-arm Cooperation for Tabletop Wiping with Temporal Object Removal
北京航空航天大学.authors_text: Pengqi Zhang, Longchang Yu, Daohan Li, Liang Yan, Hangxin Liu
北京航空航天大学.summary: This paper presents a dual-arm cooperative framework for efficient tabletop wiping by integrating object rearrangement and coverage wiping through a geometry-aware task planner.
北京航空航天大学.debug_abstract: We devise a dual-arm cooperative planning framework for wiping table surface in the presence of scattered objects. Unlike conventional surface-cleaning strategies that only cover free areas and detour around obstacles, our framework explicitly assigns one arm to rearrange objects while the other performs coverage wiping, thereby enabling access to previously obstructed regions. Specifically, we first construct a set of wiping and object-rearrangement action primitives. Based on these primitives, we introduce Geo-MILP, a geometry-aware task planner formulated as Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP). By integrating Logic-Based Benders Decomposition (LBBD), Geo-MILP iteratively optimizes action sequencingand timing to resolve geometric conflicts, promoting efficient cooperation between wiping and object rearrangement. We then employ K-Order Markov Optimization (KOMO) to generate smooth, collision-free motions to ensure feasible execution. Simulation and physical experiments demonstrate that the proposed framework not only increases reachable coverage by enabling access to obstructed areas, but also significantly improves time efficiency compared to Task and Motion Planning (TAMP) baselines, reducing planning time by up to 9 times and execution makespan by approximately 40%.

北京航空航天大学.title: CoWear: Towards Collaborative Wearable Inertial Localization with Multiple Smart Devices
北京航空航天大学.authors_text: Zhuoyuan She, Zhanpeng Zhang, Yapeng Chen, Jiale Wang, Xin Xie
北京航空航天大学.summary: CoWear introduces a comprehensive dataset and framework for collaborative inertial localization using multiple smart devices, enhancing accuracy through synchronized multi-device fusion techniques.
北京航空航天大学.debug_abstract: Consumer smart devices observe the same human motion from different body locations, yet existing inertial-localization benchmarks rarely provide synchronized heterogeneous wearables with device-specific motion ground truth. We present CoWear, a dataset and reference framework for collaborative inertial localization using a smartphone, smartwatch, and smart glasses. The dataset contains over 30 participants, over 300 walking sessions, and more than 30 hours and 100 km of aggregate device trajectories, with each device individually tracked by motion capture. To enable collaboration across distinct body motions, we train role-specific estimators to predict the displacement of a common reference device over synchronized temporal windows. Their predictions are transformed to the world frame using gyroscope integration and fused according to learned uncertainty. Experiments using phone, glasses, and watch as reference targets show that multi-device fusion consistently improves both displacement and trajectory rollout accuracy over individual-device estimation. CoWear provides a dataset and reproducible baseline for studying collaborative inertial localization across heterogeneous consumer wearables.

北京航空航天大学.title: DreamHMR: From Video Generation to Human Motion Modeling via Structural Focusing
北京航空航天大学.authors_text: Zhengjie Xu, Ruihao Gong, Xianglong Liu
北京航空航天大学.summary: DreamHMR enhances human mesh recovery by integrating video generation priors for improved body and hand reconstruction, achieving superior performance in challenging occlusion scenarios.
北京航空航天大学.debug_abstract: Human mesh recovery (HMR) provides a geometric foundation for understanding human motion, but accurately reconstructing both body motion and fine hand articulation from videos remains challenging, especially in real-world scenes where occlusion and partial visibility are common. Video generation pretraining offers rich spatial and temporal priors for this task, but its focus on visual synthesis leaves a gap between these representations and explicit human geometry. We present DreamHMR, a general framework that adapts video generation priors for complete body-and-hand reconstruction. It follows a global-to-local strategy, first grounding video representations in human geometry and then refining body and hand detail with reliable local evidence. Global Body Representation Transfer trains the video backbone to predict complete human renderings, turning its native prediction task into a means of learning surface correspondence and posed geometry. Local Joint Feature Enhancement combines contextual estimates with reliable local evidence to recover fine body and hand detail, while limiting interference from occluders and background. Experiments on five datasets with four video backbones demonstrate strong reconstruction performance across backbone families. Under a unified evaluation protocol, our best model outperforms the best existing methods on all reported metrics of 3DPW, EMDB-1, and RICH, reducing body MPJPE by 4.2%, 4.7%, and 6.1%, respectively. In more challenging occlusion settings on held-out BEDLAM and EgoBody sequences, DreamHMR reduces overall body and hand MPJPE by 7.0% and 10.0%, respectively. Our code will be made publicly available.

Quest for Intelligence.title: Tactile-Guided Robot Learning: From Representation Learning to Foundation Models
Quest for Intelligence.authors_text: Kiyanoush Nazari, Luchen Li, Haoshu Fang, Nima Fazeli, Zhibin Li
Quest for Intelligence.summary: This paper reviews the evolution of tactile sensing in robotics, emphasizing its role in learning transferable representations and enhancing adaptive manipulation through foundational models.
Quest for Intelligence.debug_abstract: Tactile sensing is becoming central to robust, adaptive, and dexterous robotic manipulation. Beyond its traditional role in contact detection and reactive control, touch is increasingly used to learn transferable representations, condition manipulation policies, and support embodied physical reasoning. Yet existing surveys largely emphasize tactile hardware and perception, leaving the rapid shift toward learning-based tactile manipulation insufficiently synthesized. This paper reviews tactile-guided skill learning from a learning-centric perspective, organized by the functional role of touch across the learning and control pipeline. We examine tactile representation and policy learning, tactile foundation models, predictive and adaptive control, and generalization across objects, tasks, sensors, embodiments, and simulation-to-real transfer. Across these directions, we identify common design principles and remaining challenges in learning transferable physical representations, integrating semantic reasoning with contact-level control, and scaling tactile learning across heterogeneous data and hardware. Finally, we outline emerging directions toward tactile foundation and world models that can predict, reason about, and adapt physical interactions. Together, this review characterizes the transition of touch from a task-specific feedback signal toward a core modality for general-purpose embodied intelligence. An accompanying database of the reviewed literature and associated resources is available at https://sites.google.com/view/touch-in-robot-learning-review.

Finally, we outline emerging directions toward tactile foundation and world models that can predict, reason about, and adapt physical interactions. Together, this review characterizes the transition of touch from a task-specific feedback signal toward a core modality for general-purpose embodied intelligence. An accompanying database of the reviewed literature and associated resources is available at https://sites.google.com/view/touch-in-robot-learning-review.

中国人民大学.title: TacClaw-Infinity: A Large-Scale Vision-Tactile-Language-Action Dataset for Dexterous Manipulation
中国人民大学.authors_text: Fucai Zhu, Xidong Zhang, Yichi Zhang, Yipan Wang, Fubo Wang
中国人民大学.summary: TacClaw-Infinity is a comprehensive VTLA dataset for dexterous manipulation, featuring over 10,000 hours of diverse, high-quality, structured tactile and visual data from various environments.
中国人民大学.debug_abstract: Large-scale robot learning increasingly relies on diverse human demonstrations, yet tactile manipulation data remain difficult to scale, and existing multimodal datasets often lack consistent quality control and structured supervision. We present TacClaw-Infinity, a large-scale structured Vision-Tactile-Language-Action (VTLA) dataset for contact-rich manipulation, collected with TacClaw, a tactile-enabled UMI-style handheld interface that records synchronized visual observations, fingertip tactile signals, and end-effector trajectories without requiring a target robot during data collection. TacClaw-Infinity is built through a distributed worldwide collection across homes, laboratories, industrial workplaces, retail stores, and outdoor environments including tasks contributed by academic and industrial collaborators. Together, these efforts yield over 10,000 hours, 1 million episodes, and 1 billion frames spanning more than 1,000 task types. We develop a scalable pipeline for trajectory reconstruction, multimodal quality control, embodiment-aware filtering, and structured annotation, covering contact-centric segmentation, subtask description, and spatial grounding. We validate TacClaw-Infinity at both the data and model levels: At the data level, we assess the collection interface, the action-space compatibility of the curated demonstrations, and the structured annotations, while for the model level, we demonstrate cross-embodiment transfer across three heterogeneous robots without robot-specific demonstrations.

中国人民大学.title: AutoRSR: Automated Real-to-Sim-to-Real Data Generation for Scalable Robot Learning
中国人民大学.authors_text: Jiawei Zhang, Chang Liu, Litao Deng, Tao Zhang, Qin Jin
中国人民大学.summary: AutoRSR automates the conversion of real-world environments into scalable simulation data for robot learning, significantly reducing manual effort while achieving high success rates in manipulation tasks.
中国人民大学.debug_abstract: Scaling embodied robot learning requires large and diverse manipulation datasets, but collecting real-world demonstrations remains expensive in human effort and robot time. Simulation provides a scalable alternative, yet converting a real workspace into a robot-learning-ready environment still requires substantial manual effort for object extraction, asset processing, coordinate calibration, and trajectory specification. We present AutoRSR, a highly automated real-to-sim-to real framework that converts scanned real-world workspaces into reusable embodied simulation assets and scalable manipulation data. Given multi-view observations, robot states, and open-vocabulary semantic queries, AutoRSR reconstructs the workspace, extracts individual object assets, and automatically registers the reconstructed scene to the robot base frame at metric scale. Starting from a small number of reference motions, AutoRSR then generates executable manipulation trajectories and scales them through trajectory interpolation and domain randomization. After workspace scanning and semantic queries, the remaining pipeline requires no manual object annotation, scene-to-robot calibration, or robot teleoperation. Across three real-world manipulation tasks, policies trained on 1K automatically generated episodes per task achieve 73.3--86.7% real-world success rates, comparable to pi 0.5 trained from 150 human teleoperated demonstrations, while reducing the human time required for data generation by an order of magnitude. These results demonstrate that real-world observations can be converted into metrically aligned, executable, and scalable simulation data with substantially reduced human effort.

中国人民大学.title: Long-Horizon RL Needs Muon
中国人民大学.authors_text: Kai Ruan, Jinghao Lin, Tao Chen, Ziqi Zhou, Qianshan Wei
中国人民大学.summary: The paper presents a novel asynchronous learning method, Muon, enhancing long-horizon reinforcement learning by optimizing single-rollout sampling and integrating various penalties for improved policy training.
中国人民大学.debug_abstract: Long-horizon agents must coordinate reasoning, tool use, and environment feedback over extended interactions. Learning from sparse outcome rewards requires weighting trajectories of different lengths and updating the policy while rollouts are still being collected. We examine a single-rollout asynchronous recipe combining Muon, token-averaged loss, truncated importance sampling, and auxiliary length and tool-error penalties. Single-rollout sampling allows asynchronous learning without waiting for multiple trajectories for the same issue. We study optimizer choices and recipe components for repository-level issue resolution across two model families. The evaluated training runs show higher training success with the full recipe than with the baselines.

苏州大学.title: GenState-AI: State-Aware Dataset for Text-to-Video Retrieval on AI-Generated Videos
苏州大学.authors_text: Minghan Li, Tongna Chen, Tianrui Lv, Yishuai Zhang, Suchao An
苏州大学.summary: GenState-AI introduces a benchmark for evaluating text-to-video retrieval in AI-generated videos, focusing on state changes and semantic accuracy across various domains.
苏州大学.debug_abstract: Existing text-to-video retrieval benchmarks often permit matching from static appearance, making it difficult to determine whether models capture state changes and final outcomes. We introduce GenState-AI, a benchmark comprising 956 AI-generated videos and 195 verified state-change queries across Toy, Cartoon, Home, and Manipulation domains. Its construction uses prompt-controlled variants that target either conflicting temporal/state outcomes or semantic substitutions. Following human verification, all valid videos contribute to subset-level retrieval pools, while complete query-specific triplets support diagnostic hard-negative ordering. We evaluate VCF-Lik, Qwen3-VL, and LanguageBind using both standard Recall@K and triplet-based consistency metrics. Qwen3-VL (8B) achieves the best macro-average R@1 and triplet consistency, while LanguageBind obtains the highest semantic discrimination accuracy. However, stronger retrieval does not consistently yield correct hard-negative ordering, and Qwen3-VL and LanguageBind remain weak on Manipulation triplets, where VCF-Lik performs substantially better. GenState-AI therefore provides a controlled diagnostic testbed for distinguishing global retrieval quality from fine-grained temporal and semantic grounding in AI-generated videos.

Affective Intelligence and Robotics Labo.title: MultiFly: A Real-World Multimodal Aerial Dataset with Annotation-Efficient Label Transfer and Cross-Modal Semantic Consistency
Affective Intelligence and Robotics Labo.authors_text: Markus Gross, Andreas Greiner, Taehyoung Kim, Sivasubiramaniam Subbiah, Tomaž Cotič
Affective Intelligence and Robotics Labo.summary: MultiFly is a comprehensive multimodal UAV dataset that efficiently propagates semantic labels across RGB, thermal, LiDAR, and radar, achieving high annotation consistency and establishing new benchmarks.
Affective Intelligence and Robotics Labo.debug_abstract: We introduce MultiFly, a real-world, low-altitude UAV dataset for semantic perception across RGB, thermal, LiDAR, and radar modalities. MultiFly provides 17,272 synchronized samples from four suburban scenes with frame-wise annotations for 15 semantic classes, together with calibration and GNSS-RTK/IMU measurements. To avoid costly and inconsistent modality-specific annotation, we propagate labels from only 115 manually annotated RGB images through shared geometric representations to all four modalities. This approach generates semantic labels for 17,157 additional RGB images, 17,272 thermal images, 840M LiDAR points, and 3.4M radar points. Transferred annotations achieve 89.93% average agreement with held-out manual annotations, and 90.94% average semantic consistency across all six modality pairs. We further establish semantic segmentation benchmarks for all four modalities, revealing distinct architectural behavior for dense LiDAR and sparse radar data. Taken together, MultiFly provides a scalable foundation for multimodal aerial perception and, to the best of our knowledge, the first public real-world low-altitude aerial benchmark that combines consistent frame-wise semantic annotations for RGB, thermal, LiDAR, and radar. Data at https://github.com/markus-42/multifly.

Bio-Inspired Robotics Laboratory (BIRL).title: MultiFly: A Real-World Multimodal Aerial Dataset with Annotation-Efficient Label Transfer and Cross-Modal Semantic Consistency
Bio-Inspired Robotics Laboratory (BIRL).authors_text: Markus Gross, Andreas Greiner, Taehyoung Kim, Sivasubiramaniam Subbiah, Tomaž Cotič
Bio-Inspired Robotics Laboratory (BIRL).summary: MultiFly is a comprehensive multimodal UAV dataset that efficiently propagates semantic labels across RGB, thermal, LiDAR, and radar, achieving high annotation consistency and establishing new benchmarks.

SU Lab.title: Design and Characterization of a Unified Continuum Robot Actuation Platform
SU Lab.authors_text: Yunti Xu, Aedan Mangan, Miheer Potdar, Alex Lu, Tania K. Morimoto
SU Lab.summary: This paper introduces a modular actuation platform for continuum robots, enhancing versatility and accuracy in surgical applications while promoting open-source collaboration.
SU Lab.debug_abstract: Continuum robots enable dexterous access to confined spaces in applications such as minimally invasive surgery and industrial inspection. However, their actuation systems are often custom-designed for specific robot architectures and tasks, limiting reuse across publications, institutions, and applications. This paper presents a unified actuation platform that decouples actuation hardware and software from continuum robot design. The platform provides modular actuation across continuum robot classes, scales to a large number of degrees of freedom (DOFs), and integrates with conventional serial manipulators for hybrid architectures. We validate the platform on an open-sourced surgical robotic system and experimentally characterize the actuation modules, achieving sub-millimeter translational accuracy and less than $5^\circ$ rotational error over ranges of $30$~mm and $180^\circ$, respectively. We further demonstrate the platform in two surgical use cases: teleoperation of a continuum camera in a constrained environment and bimanual manipulation using $2.53$~mm concentric-tube-robot-based forceps alongside a conventional wristed instrument. All hardware designs and ROS-based software are open-sourced to facilitate reuse and further research in continuum and surgical robotics.

SU Lab.title: SEDM: Selective Self-Evolving Distributed Memory for Agents
SU Lab.authors_text: Yichen Liu, Anna Min, Yinzhi Wang, Yuhang Yao, Yichen Han
SU Lab.summary: SEDM introduces a selective memory framework for agents that optimizes memory sharing and usage, significantly enhancing task success while reducing processing costs.
SU Lab.debug_abstract: Agents in a society can reuse each other's experience, but indiscriminate memory use increases processing cost and can reduce task success. We present SEDM (Selective Self-Evolving Distributed Memory), a framework that selects both what agents share and when recipients use it. On the sender side, SEDM admits memories through paired execution tests, ranks them by relevance and measured utility, and abstracts them for cross-domain reuse. On the recipient side, Calibrated Memory Gating (CMG) predicts success with and without memory in a single forward pass, learning from paired outcomes including ties. It injects memory only when the calibrated success gain outweighs a context-cost penalty. SEDM exceeds the strongest evaluated baseline on LoCoMo open-domain questions by 15.1 F1 points and outperforms G-Memory on FEVER and HotpotQA with 16-32% fewer prompt tokens. In a controlled HotpotQA study, CMG achieves success comparable to always using memory with 18% fewer agent input tokens. Within the full SEDM pipeline on LoCoMo, CMG outperforms both always-use and no-memory policies for two SEDM memories while using 19-31% fewer input tokens than always-use. These results show that selective use can recover value from shared memories that hurt performance when injected indiscriminately.

加州理工-机器人实验室.title: Learning in Orbit: Onboard Training and Closed-Loop Attitude Control with a Thermal Segmentation Model on a Spacecraft
加州理工-机器人实验室.authors_text: Elena Sorina Lupu, Hannah Grauer, Phaedrus Leeds, Nikhil Ranganathan, Connor Lee
加州理工-机器人实验室.summary: This paper presents a 6U CubeSat's successful onboard training of a thermal segmentation model for closed-loop attitude control, enhancing autonomous operations in deep space.
加州理工-机器人实验室.debug_abstract: Deep space missions increasingly require spacecraft capable of autonomously operating in environments with communication delays and bandwidth limitations. A key enabler of such autonomy is the ability to run learning-based algorithms directly onboard. In this work, we present a flight deployment on a 6U CubeSat that demonstrates (1) onboard training and inference of a thermal segmentation model on an NVIDIA Jetson TX2 NX GPU in space and (2) closed-loop attitude control using the segmentation model on a real-time, thermal image feed to track the Moon. In addition to this demonstration, we implement ROS 2 Foxy as a data transport middleware and integrate an open-source file system that provides strong data integrity guarantees and self-healing features. Over the course of approximately one year, we performed 12 experiments on the spacecraft, advancing the state of the art in autonomous spacecraft systems by showing how modern learning-based pipelines, commercially available hardware, and open-source software can operate reliably under the compute and environmental constraints of Low Earth Orbit (LEO).

具身智能实验室.title: Holi-Spatial 360: Generative Reconstruction from Sparse Panoramas for Spatial Rendering and Intelligence
具身智能实验室.authors_text: Yuanyuan Gao, Zhirui Liu, Yuning Gong, Yifei Liu, Yifan Zhan
具身智能实验室.summary: Holi-Spatial 360 presents a framework for generating annotated multi-room 3D environments from sparse panoramas, enhancing spatial reasoning in VLMs through improved reconstruction and curation.
具身智能实验室.debug_abstract: Spatial intelligence requires scalable 3D environments that are both photorealistic and semantically grounded, yet existing indoor datasets are dominated by room-scale captures and costly LiDAR acquisition. Online real-estate platforms offer abundant panoramas of diverse multi-room homes, but sparse viewpoints and texture-poor regions make reconstruction severely under-constrained. We introduce Holi-Spatial 360, a generative reconstruction and data curation framework for converting these panoramas into annotated multi-room 3D environments. Because reconstruction quality bounds subsequent generation, our Correspondence-Guided Geometric Optimization converts feed-forward reconstruction priors into reliable cross-view constraints and builds a coherent 3D Gaussian Splatting representation as 3D spatial memory. Adapted single-image and video priors then restore appearance and complete continuous trajectories while preserving observed content. The reconstructed scenes support arbitrary RGB-D rendering and an automated curation pipeline that combines end-to-end 3D grounding with VLM-based verification. Holi360 contains over 1K multi-room 3DGS scenes, more than 100K instance annotations, and 2M spatial question-answer pairs. We also introduce the Holi360 benchmark to evaluate the spatial understanding of VLMs in real-world, multi-room indoor environments. Experiments demonstrate superior reconstruction and curation quality under sparse panoramic inputs, while fine-tuning VLMs on Holi360 substantially improves spatial reasoning capabilities.

BIGAI.title: Mitigating Video Hallucinations via Attention-Guided Representation Perturbation
BIGAI.authors_text: Zhixin Cai, Ruoqi Yuan, Xinchen Yang, Zhuofan Chen, Jun Bai
BIGAI.summary: The paper presents ARP-CD, a training-free method that uses attention-guided representation perturbation to reduce hallucinations in Video LLMs by enhancing contrastive decoding effectiveness.
BIGAI.debug_abstract: Video large language models (Video LLMs) often generate responses unsupported by the input video. Contrastive decoding (CD) can mitigate these hallucinations, but its effectiveness depends on how the negative branch weakens visual evidence. Existing methods rely on predefined perturbations or masking guided by question reconstruction, offering limited control over the model's visual reliance during answer generation. We introduce Attention-guided Representation Perturbation for Contrastive Decoding (ARP-CD), a training-free framework for constructing contrastive negatives directly in representation space. ARP-CD uses the attention mass assigned to visual tokens at the answer-prediction position to guide bounded gradient updates of the language model's input visual hidden states. These updates reduce visual attention and produce a negative input, whose predictions are contrasted with those of the original branch throughout generation. Experiments across four Video LLMs and four benchmarks show that ARP-CD outperforms representative training-free baselines in most model--benchmark settings, reducing hallucinations while improving general video understanding. Further analyses show that attention-guided perturbation directions improve negative quality and that the resulting negatives provide effective contrastive references for correcting the original predictions.

BIGAI.title: Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Model Decision-Making for Autonomous Driving Guided by Chinese Philosophical Wisdom
BIGAI.authors_text: Xiaojun Bi, Xiaoyuan Ma, Yiwen Sun, Tianren Huang, Chaoran Liu
BIGAI.summary: The CPW-Drive framework integrates Chinese philosophical wisdom into autonomous driving decision-making, enhancing safety and efficiency through a retrieval-augmented generation approach, outperforming traditional methods.
BIGAI.debug_abstract: Autonomous driving decision systems must balance safety, efficiency, and social norms in complex traffic interactions. Philosophical and ethical considerations have received limited attention in existing autonomous driving decision-making approaches based on numerical optimization, sequence prediction, and large language models (LLMs). We propose Chinese Philosophical Wisdom-Guided Driving (CPW-Drive), a closed-loop retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) framework that incorporates value guidance derived from Chinese philosophy into autonomous driving decision-making. Using Chinese Confucian thought as its knowledge source, CPW-Drive consolidates LLM-extracted keywords from relevant classical texts into driving-relevant value principles through manual screening and validation. It then contextualizes these principles through scenario-specific cases to form retrievable and reusable value guidance. We further propose Physics-aware Spatial Similarity Retrieval (PSSR), which compares vehicle layouts and velocity-extrapolated states to retrieve physically relevant historical cases. On Highway-env's multilane highway-driving task, CPW-Drive achieves success rates of 93.0%, 86.0%, and 72.0% across three traffic configurations. These results outperform the strongest baseline by 8.0, 22.5, and 25.0 percentage points, respectively. Across all configurations, CPW-Drive achieves the highest collision-free step count and maintains a low lane-change frequency. The results suggest that structured value guidance can improve simulated closed-loop safety and stability while introducing efficiency and latency trade-offs.

BIGAI.title: Dual-arm Cooperation for Tabletop Wiping with Temporal Object Removal
BIGAI.authors_text: Pengqi Zhang, Longchang Yu, Daohan Li, Liang Yan, Hangxin Liu
BIGAI.summary: This paper presents a dual-arm cooperative framework for efficient tabletop wiping by integrating object rearrangement and coverage wiping through a geometry-aware task planner.
BIGAI.debug_abstract: We devise a dual-arm cooperative planning framework for wiping table surface in the presence of scattered objects. Unlike conventional surface-cleaning strategies that only cover free areas and detour around obstacles, our framework explicitly assigns one arm to rearrange objects while the other performs coverage wiping, thereby enabling access to previously obstructed regions. Specifically, we first construct a set of wiping and object-rearrangement action primitives. Based on these primitives, we introduce Geo-MILP, a geometry-aware task planner formulated as Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP). By integrating Logic-Based Benders Decomposition (LBBD), Geo-MILP iteratively optimizes action sequencingand timing to resolve geometric conflicts, promoting efficient cooperation between wiping and object rearrangement. We then employ K-Order Markov Optimization (KOMO) to generate smooth, collision-free motions to ensure feasible execution. Simulation and physical experiments demonstrate that the proposed framework not only increases reachable coverage by enabling access to obstructed areas, but also significantly improves time efficiency compared to Task and Motion Planning (TAMP) baselines, reducing planning time by up to 9 times and execution makespan by approximately 40%.

具身智能多模态大模型中心.title: RuleTrek: Benchmarking Agentic Rule Reasoning in Complex Scenarios
具身智能多模态大模型中心.authors_text: Chenhao Yuan, Bohan Yu, Yinhao Xu, Chao Yin, Chenxi Zhou
具身智能多模态大模型中心.summary: RuleTrek introduces a multi-domain benchmark for evaluating agentic rule reasoning in complex scenarios, revealing significant challenges faced by large language models in this area.
具身智能多模态大模型中心.debug_abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly tackle complex real-world tasks in specialized domains. However, identifying and correctly applying domain-specific rules remains challenging when scenario information is distributed across multiple files. Existing rule-reasoning benchmarks typically represent scenarios using only a few factual statements, simplifying the identification and application of relevant rules. To address this gap, this paper introduces \textbf{RuleTrek}, a multi-domain benchmark for agentic rule reasoning in complex scenarios. Its rule-grounded construction pipeline extracts structured rule graphs, generates and incrementally composes rule-specific sub-scenarios while ensuring consistency and solvability. To systematically evaluate agentic rule reasoning in complex scenarios, RuleTrek assesses three capabilities in interactive workspaces: Rule Identification (RI), Rule Deduction (RD), and End-to-End Rule Reasoning (E2E). Experiments on 11 frontier LLMs show that the highest RI and RD scores are only 62.47\% and 60.43\%, respectively, while E2E scores range from 26.97\% to 55.29\%. These results demonstrate that current LLM agents face substantial challenges in rule reasoning over complex scenarios. We make our code and dataset publicly available at \href{https://github.com/yuan247/RuleTrek}{RuleTrek}.
